items.title: What We Know About the Deadly Moscow Restaurant Attack
items.summary: While Russia's Embassy in Italy blamed Ukraine and reports said a high-ranking general was targeted in the attack, much remains unconfirmed.
items.body_text:
At least three people were killed and 21 injured after a bomb carried by a woman exploded outside an upscale restaurant in central Moscow on Saturday evening, authorities said.
Authorities have described the incident as a terrorist attack, but have yet to say who the intended target was.
Reports suggested the attack may have been connected to the war in Ukraine and that the newly appointed commander of Russia's Aerospace Forces, Colonel General Alexander Chaiko, was expected to celebrate his birthday at the restaurant.
Here is what we know so far:
What happened?
The explosion occurred just before 8 p.m. close to Balzi Rossi, an upscale Italian restaurant located in one of Moscow's seven Stalin-era skyscrapers at Kudrinskaya Ploshchad, police said.
Russia's National Anti-Terrorism Committee said the woman tried to enter the restaurant with a homemade explosive device and identified her as the suspected perpetrator of the attack.
The woman was killed in the blast together with a security guard who stopped her from entering. The guard reportedly decided to inspect the package disguised as a gift, which then exploded.
According to preliminary reports, the attacker was likely unaware she was carrying a bomb, the newspaper Kommersant said.
On Sunday, the death toll from the explosion rose to five, according to the Telegram channel 112, pro-Kremlin broadcaster Ren TV and the newspaper Izvestia, media outlets believed to be close to the security services.
The Russian Embassy in Italy on Monday also put the number of killed at five.
The blast was equivalent to one kilogram of TNT, and the device was packed with metal balls, Kommersant reported, adding that the explosion was so powerful that the attacker's remains were found 15 meters from the blast site.
What do officials say?
Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin on Sunday offered his condolences to the families of those killed and called the blast “a brutal terrorist attack,” without specifying who was responsible for it.
The Russian Embassy in Italy blamed Ukraine for the attack, saying that “the bloody tentacles of [President Volodymyr] Zelensky’s terrorist gang have reached an Italian restaurant in Moscow.”
“It is clear that by planning a terrorist attack at one of Moscow’s best Italian restaurants, Kyiv terrorists sought to intimidate Italians working in Russia, showing them that they too are targets and could at any moment become the next victims of these criminals," the embassy said.
Neither President Vladimir Putin nor his spokesman Dmitry Peskov have commented on the attack.
Ukrainian authorities have also not issued any comments.
Who was targeted?
Reports said that the restaurant was hosting a birthday celebration for Colonel General Alexander Chaiko, who turned 55 on July 27, as well as his appointment as the commander of Russia's Aerospace Forces.
A sign reading “Alexander 55” could be seen on the restaurant’s stage in a video allegedly posted from the event.
Senior officials from the Federal Security Service (FSB), Defense Ministry generals, government officials and lawmakers may have attended the event, said VChK-OGPU, an anonymously run Telegram channel that claims to share insider information from Russia’s security and law enforcement agencies.
Chaiko’s daughter, Maria Chaiko, may have been injured in the explosion, the exiled news outlet Vyorstka reported, citing a source close to the restaurant’s management.
Unverified lists of victims published by Telegram channels also include a 25-year-old woman identified as “Maria P.”, who is reported to have suffered a traumatic brain injury. The surname appears to correspond to the surname of her husband, Daniil Peredriy. Reports said he may also have been injured in the blast, but no details were provided.
Chaiko himself was not injured in the explosion, reports said.
Who is General Chaiko?
If confirmed, Chaiko would become one of the highest-ranking Russian generals to be targeted in an apparent assassination attempt since the start

items.title: Did Russian air defenses bring down the drone that killed seven on a Black Sea beach?
items.summary: A Ukrainian drone came down on a beach crowded with vacationers in the village of Arkhipo-Osipovka near Gelendzhik on the morning of August 3. Seven people died, including three children, and 40 more were injured, 21 of them hospitalized, according to data from the Krasnodar Krai operational headquarters.
items.body_text:
Did Russian air defenses bring down the drone that killed seven on a Black Sea beach?
A Ukrainian drone came down on a beach crowded with vacationers in the village of Arkhipo-Osipovka near Gelendzhik on the morning of August 3. Seven people died, including three children, and 40 more were injured, 21 of them hospitalized, according to data from the Krasnodar Krai operational headquarters.
The news outlet 93.ru reports that the city’s mayor, Alexey Bogodistov, declared a drone threat at 8:34 a.m. and canceled it just 10 minutes later. Local residents and tourists say the village’s warning sirens never sounded, even though there’s a system in place there. “Yesterday, they were blaring starting at 3:42 a.m. But today, it’s quiet,” the Russian Telegram news channel Ostorozhno Novosti quoted one local resident as saying.
Krasnodar Governor Veniamin Kondratyev wrote on his Telegram channel that the attack targeted civilian infrastructure, saying “drone debris” had fallen in Arkhipo-Osipovka. Footage shot by witnesses at the scene, however, shows an entire drone crashing onto the beach.
Agentstvo, an independent Russian investigative outlet, reports, citing military experts, that Russian air defenses may have caused the drone to come down on the beach — the flight trajectory, in particular, supports that theory. One clip published by the Ukrainian monitoring Telegram channel Supernova+ also captures sounds resembling automatic gunfire; its caption reads: “MOG [mobile firing group] shoots down the drone, and it falls on vacationers.”
Witnesses have confirmed hearing gunfire. “Thank God we left the beach early, with our dog. We were already home when we heard a barrage of gunfire, like from a machine gun, and an explosion. Everything that could shake, shook,” one tourist told 93.ru.
OSINT analyst Kirill Mikhailov told the outlet that the sound of automatic weapons fire dies down just as the drone begins to fall. “So it’s as if a MOG was there and was firing specifically at this drone, but whether it hit it, we can’t see on the video,” he said.
Military analyst David Sharp, who spoke with journalists from the independent Russian investigative outlet The Insider, agrees:
The cause of the crash could have been a malfunction, or the drone could have been damaged by a hit. Most likely, this wasn’t a drone with video guidance. Most likely, it was programmed with GPS coordinates. I find it hard to imagine that Ukrainians programmed it to strike a specific point on the beach in order to kill the people there. It’s not even a question of morality — it’s that it would be pointless, because drones attack other targets. This could have been a defect, a shootdown, or the result of electronic warfare. All of that looks more plausible than a deliberate attack on the beach.
Sharp also points out that the sound of gunfire suggests a protected facility somewhere nearby. That facility could have been the drone’s actual target. He did not specify what kind of facility it might have been.
Agentstvo reports that the beach where the drone came down sits in front of the Rassvet resort, which is a branch of NPO Mashinostroyeniya, one of the country’s key rocket and space enterprises.
“Putin’s Palace” also sits on the Black Sea coast near the village of Praskoveevka outside Gelendzhik, a property FBK, the Navalny-founded anti-corruption organization, described in detail in one of its investigations. Arkhipo-Osipovka lies less than 30 kilometers (about 19 miles) from Praskoveevka in a straight line, though there’s no confirmation the palace was the attack’s target.

items.title: FT: Russia is expanding its ‘shadow fleet’ of tankers to carry liquefied natural gas ahead of looming supply ban
items.summary: Russia is expanding its “shadow fleet” of gas carriers, adding secondhand vessels along with its first domestically built tankers, the Financial Times reports, citing data from the maritime analytics firm Windward.
items.body_text:
FT: Russia is expanding its ‘shadow fleet’ of tankers to carry liquefied natural gas ahead of looming supply ban
Russia is expanding its “shadow fleet” of gas carriers, adding secondhand vessels along with its first domestically built tankers, the Financial Times reports, citing data from the maritime analytics firm Windward.
The “shadow fleet” used to transport liquefied natural gas (LNG) has grown to 25 vessels over the past six months, according to the analysts’ count. That total includes at least eight secondhand tankers and two new ones built at the Zvezda shipyard.
Most of the tankers belong to shell companies linked to Russia and registered in jurisdictions such as Dubai, Hong Kong, and Singapore.
Novatek holds the leading position in the Russian LNG market. Its Siberian Yamal LNG plant and the sanctioned Arctic LNG 2 project together account for more than 65% of Russia’s total production, while another 30% comes from Gazprom’s Sakhalin-2 project in the Far East.
The Financial Times identifies China as the main buyer of LNG from the Arctic LNG 2 project. Eleven vessels with an average age of 10 years handle shipments from the project, according to estimates from the FT and the analytics firm Kpler. The cargo is then transferred at floating terminals onto conventional tankers, which carry it on to China.
Expanding the gas carrier fleet will let Moscow keep LNG shipments running once the EU’s ban on supplies takes effect on January 1, 2027, following the model of the “shadow fleet” already used to move oil, which now numbers more than a thousand vessels. Moscow has been slower to build up its shadow gas-carrier fleet, however, since these vessels are technically far more complex, the outlet says.
Novatek suspended production of liquefied natural gas at the Arctic LNG 2 project in April 2024, citing sanctions and a shortage of tankers, according to Reuters. At the time, the company had three specialized tankers from the shipyard, out of the 15 planned back in 2020.
A ban on transporting Russian LNG to third countries was expected to be included in the EU’s 21st sanctions package against Russia. Greece opposed it, however, acting in the interest of its shipping company Dynagas, and the proposal was ultimately left out of the latest sanctions package.

items.title: In occupied Crimea, a soldier opens fire on fellow servicemen and locals, killing four
items.summary: A serviceman opened fire in Sevastopol, leaving people dead and wounded, according to Mikhail Razvozhayev, the Russian-installed governor of the occupied city.
items.body_text:
In occupied Crimea, a soldier opens fire on fellow servicemen and locals, killing four
A serviceman opened fire in Sevastopol, leaving people dead and wounded, according to Mikhail Razvozhayev, the Russian-installed governor of the occupied city.
According to Razvozhayev, the serviceman first opened fire on his fellow servicemen, killing one and wounding another. He then wounded three more people and killed three civilians: two men — ages 59 and 71 — and a 64-year-old woman.
Razvozhayev said the serviceman has been detained and that those injured are receiving medical care.
He did not provide further details, including what caused the incident.

Saurabh Sinha / TNN / Updated: Aug 04, 2026, 13:52 IST

Air India flight from Phuket to Delhi experienced turbulence-related event during cruise. (Photo: TOI)
NEW DELHI: Some passengers and crew members onboard Air India's Phuket-Delhi flight (AI 2379) suffered injuries when the aircraft encountered turbulence during descent at the destination on Tuesday morning, causing a sudden drop in altitude.An AI with medical support received the 134 passengers onboard the Airbus A320 on arrival just after 11 am. About 10 passengers and two crew members are learnt to have been taken to the Medanta medical centre at the airport.An AI spokesperson said: "Air India confirms that flight AI2379, operating from Phuket to Delhi on 4 August, experienced a brief in-flight turbulence-related event during cruise, resulting in a momentary change in altitude.
The aircraft landed safely in Delhi and all passengers and crew have safely disembarked.There have been no serious injuries reported as of now. A small number of passengers and crew members with minor injuries requiring medical assessment have been taken to a medical facility at the airport for precautionary examination and care by Air Indiaâs airport team and medical personnel.The safety and well-being of our passengers and crew remain Air Indiaâs highest priority. We are providing all necessary support to those affected and are cooperating fully with the relevant authorities as part of the investigation."

items.title: AAP E20 protest: Kejriwal, Sisodia stage sit-in after march to PM's residence stopped
items.summary: Delhi Police stopped Arvind Kejriwal and AAP leaders marching to Prime Minister Modi's residence. The party staged a sit-in protest on Firoz Shah Road after being prevented from proceeding. They carried over 2.30 lakh petitions against the Centre's E20 petrol policy. items.body_text:
AAP protest E20 petrol policy: Kejriwal, Sisodia stage sit-in after march to PM Modi's residence stopped
Edited by: Kanchan Yadav / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Aug 04, 2026, 14:23 IST
Comments
Share
AA
Text Size
Small
Medium
Large
AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal and other party leaders stopped from marching to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence. (Photo: PTI)
NEW DELHI: Delhi Police on Tuesday stopped AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal and other party leaders from marching to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence, prompting the party to stage a sit-in protest on Firoz Shah Road.Kejriwal, along with former Delhi deputy chief minister Manish Sisodia, AAP leader Jasmine Shah and several party workers, sat on the road after police prevented the group from proceeding further to submit more than 2.30 lakh petitions against E20.Police stopped the protesters near Firoz Shah Road and did not allow them to move towards the Prime Minister's residence."No one will be allowed ahead of 5, Firoz Shah Road. We have deployed adequate security, including Delhi Police and paramilitary forces, to maintain law and order," a police source said, as quoted by PTI.Following the barricading, Kejriwal and other AAP leaders staged a sit-in protest on the road.
The AAP had begun the march with around 100 supporters, carrying petitions collected from people across the country against the Centre's policy of promoting E20 petrol. The party has alleged that ethanol-blended fuel is adversely affecting vehicle owners.Addressing supporters before the march, Kejriwal said the party wanted the government to hear the concerns of people affected by the policy."We are going to the Prime Minister's residence with over 2.30 lakh petitions signed by people from across the country.
We want the government to listen to the concerns of crores of vehicle owners who are facing problems because of E20 petrol," he said."People are asking why the government is forcing E20 petrol despite complaints from vehicle owners. We only want people to have the choice of buying pure petrol and E20, and if E20 is being promoted, it should be sold at a lower price," he said.AAP has been campaigning against E20 petrol in recent weeks, holding an "Ethanol Town Hall" and launching a nationwide signature campaign. Kejriwal had also written to PM Modi seeking an appointment to discuss concerns over ethanol-blended fuel.
Kejriwal trying to revive failed politics: BJP
BJP criticised Kejriwal's protest, accusing him of opposing the interests of farmers and trying to revive his political fortunes. BJP national general secretary Tarun Chugh described the protest as politically motivated.
"Arvind Kejriwal's march is absurd, irresponsible and meaningless. Everything has been done in a scientific manner. The process has been duly approved and no one has raised any complaint," Chugh told reporters in the Parliament House complex."Kejriwal's campaign is against India's farmers. You are trying to deprive farmers of their income, Kejriwal ji. Ethanol is produced from crops such as maize, sugarcane and other agricultural produce. Ethanol has been used in many countries around the world for several decades, and its use in India has also been implemented in a scientific manner," he said.The BJP's response came after Kejriwal alleged that the Centre was continuing with the E20 policy despite public concerns and claimed the government was pushing ethanol-blended fuel under external pressure.
Kanchan Yadav is a writer at The Times of India, where she covers business, politics, international affairs and social issues. Her reporting also focuses on policy, governance and economic developments, with a close lens on how decisions in corridors of power affect everyday lives and community well-being.

items.title: Six killed in Sri Lanka as heavy rain triggers landslides, floods
items.summary: The adverse weather has affected five districts, with incessant downpours triggering landslides, flooding and strong winds, disrupting normal life and forcing nearly 1,900 people into relief centres
items.body_text:
At least six persons were killed and three others injured as heavy rain, landslides and flash floods battered parts of Sri Lanka over the past two days, officials said on Tuesday (August 4, 2026).
The adverse weather has affected five districts, with incessant downpours triggering landslides, flooding and strong winds, disrupting normal life and forcing nearly 1,900 people into relief centres.
Police said three women, aged 83, 58 and 47, and a 22-year-old man were killed when a mound of earth collapsed onto a house in the Polpitiya-Morahenagama area.
In a separate incident, a 53-year-old man died after falling into the Mahaweli River while crossing a bridge on the Watawala-Gnanandagama road.
Police also said a 67-year-old man was killed after a mound of earth collapsed onto a roadside shop in Solangkanda Janaudana village in Nawalapitiya.
A 45-year-old man was reported missing after being swept away by flash floodwaters in the Ambagamuwa area of Ginigathena, police said.
The central district of Nuwara Eliya recorded around 100 mm of rainfall, while authorities warned fishermen against venturing into the sea because of rough weather and strong winds.
Schools across the Central Province remained closed on Tuesday (August 4, 2026) as a precaution.
On Monday (August 3, 2026), authorities issued evacuation warnings for residents living along the Mahaweli and Kelani river basins due to the risk of flash floods. Most major reservoirs in the country had reached spill levels, officials said.
The latest spell of extreme weather comes as Sri Lanka continues to recover from the devastation caused by Cyclone Ditwa in November, which killed nearly 640 people, affected around two million others and caused an estimated $4.1 billion in damage.
Published - August 04, 2026 03:04 pm IST

items.title: Why was Singapore flight turbulence severe? | Explained
items.summary: How does turbulence or changes in air on the flight path affect an aircraft? Is there evidence that turbulence is increasing because of climate change? What are airlines doing to manage in-flight turbulence? What should be the takeaway from the injuries on board the Singapore flight?
items.body_text:
The story so far: On May 20-21, a Singapore Airlines flight, SQ321, with 211 passengers and 18 crew, from London’s Heathrow Airport to Singapore encountered severe turbulence while over the Andaman Sea/Bay of Bengal near the Irrawaddy Basin, Myanmar. A passenger passed away and several others suffered injuries of varying degrees. The crew decided to divert the Boeing 777-312ER to Bangkok, Thailand. The United States National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) is to assist Singapore’s investigation — also because the aircraft is a Boeing jet.
What do we know about the incident?
Granular flight data shows the aircraft dropping rapidly before the crew began (“controlled”) descent from 37,000 feet to 31,000 feet. It also shows the aircraft had had an altitude deviation prior to this.
Air India Phuket-Delhi flight encounters turbulence; few passengers, crew sustain minor injuries
There has been much focus on ‘turbulence’. What have experts told The Hindu?
Turbulence occurs “by the relative movement of disturbed air through which an aircraft is flying”. It could be thermal or mechanical and can happen “either within or when it is clear of cloud”. Its severity depends on the “rate at which the speed or the direction of airflow/or both changes”.
According to Professor Guy Gratton, Associate Professor of Aviation and the Environment at Cranfield University, U.K., turbulence is basically what happens when there is friction between airflow or wind flowing in different directions. When it involves aviation, there are two main forms, which are Clear Air Turbulence (CAT), which happens around jet streams, and the other being inside or around cumulonimbus clouds. These clouds have very strong upwards air currents in the middle and downwards air current around the outside, he explains, which can result in quite serious turbulence. The faster an aircraft is, the more severe the response to the turbulence.
Prof. Richard Dale, Senior Lecturer in Aviation and Tourism at the University of West London, says turbulence consists of changes in the movement of air which the aircraft is moving through over a short distance. For example, there might be updrafts that are quickly followed by downdrafts, but also changes in the horizontal movement of the air. The movement of the air, to some degree, is random and unpredictable, although the location where turbulence will be encountered is more certain. These changes cause the lift produced by the aircraft wing to change for a short time, forcing the aircraft up or down, suddenly and unexpectedly. According to A.D. Ravishankar, former Director, Aviation Meteorology, India Meteorological Department, CAT is turbulence suffered by an aircraft above 18,000 feet.
Dr. Paul Williams, Professor of Atmospheric Science, University of Reading, U.K., says that turbulence fatalities on commercial flights are, fortunately, very rare. Turbulence on flights can be caused by storms, mountains, and strong air currents called jet streams. In this last case, it is called clear air turbulence, and can be difficult to avoid because it does not show up on the weather radar in the flight deck. He adds that a detailed analysis of the meteorological circumstances and the type of turbulence that affected the Singapore Airlines flight will take some time. He also says that there is strong evidence that turbulence is increasing because of climate change. “We recently discovered that severe clear air turbulence in the North Atlantic has increased by 55% since 1979. Our latest future projections indicate a doubling or trebling of severe turbulence in the jet streams in the coming decades, if the climate continues to change as we expect.”
Will passenger injuries lead to litigation?
As visuals from the Singapore incident show, there has been serious injury to some passengers. Injuries occur from passengers not wearing their seat belts resulting in them being violently thrown from their seats, the overhead bins opening causing items to fall,

न्यूज एजेंसी PTI ने सूत्रों के हवाले से बताया कि हादसे में विमान में सवार 12 लोग घायल हुए हैं। इनमें यात्री और क्रू मेंबर्स शामिल हैं। घायलों को दिल्ली एयरपोर्ट के मेडिकल सेंटर में जांच और इलाज के लिए भेजा गया है।
एअर इंडिया ने पहले बताया था कि सभी यात्री और क्रू सुरक्षित हैं। किसी के गंभीर रूप से घायल होने की खबर नहीं है। घटना की जांच की जा रही है। टर्बुलेंस के बाद फ्लाइट की तस्वीरें सामने आई हैं, जिनमें प्लेन की सीलिंग के पैनल में दरारें दिखीं।
विमान की छत में दरारें…2 तस्वीरें…
आंख-गर्दन में चोटें, घायलों की 3 तस्वीरें
टर्बुलेंस में अचानक कई फीट नीचे आ सकता है विमान
टर्बुलेंस का मतलब है हवा का बहाव अचानक बदल जाना, जिससे विमान को झटके लगने लगते हैं। इस दौरान विमान कुछ समय के लिए ऊपर-नीचे या दाएं-बाएं हिल सकता है और कभी-कभी कुछ फीट नीचे भी आ जाता है। इसी वजह से यात्रियों को लगता है कि विमान गिर रहा है। हालांकि, ज्यादातर मामलों में ऐसा नहीं होता।
टर्बुलेंस तीव्रता के लिहाज से तीन तरह के होते हैं
- हल्के टर्बुलेंस: इसमें प्लेन 1 मीटर तक ऊपर-नीचे होता है। यात्रियों को पता भी नहीं चलता।
- मध्यम टर्बुलेंस: इसमें जहाज 3-6 मीटर तक ऊपर-नीचे होते हैं। इससे ड्रिंक गिर सकता है।
- गंभीर टर्बुलेंस: इसमें जहाज 30 मीटर तक ऊपर-नीचे होते हैं। सीट बेल्ट न लगाए रहने पर पैसेंजर उछलकर गिर सकते हैं।
क्या टर्बुलेंस की वजह से प्लेन क्रैश हो सकता है?
आधुनिक तकनीक और बेहतर सुरक्षा सिस्टम की वजह से आज टर्बुलेंस से विमान हादसे की आशंका काफी कम हो गई है। हालांकि, बेहद गंभीर टर्बुलेंस या खराब मौसम में दुर्घटना का खतरा पूरी तरह खत्म नहीं होता।
हालांकि, आज के आधुनिक विमान हर तरह के टर्बुलेंस को झेलने के हिसाब से बनाए जाते हैं। पायलटों को भी ऐसी परिस्थितियों से सुरक्षित तरीके से निपटने की विशेष ट्रेनिंग दी जाती है।
दुनिया में टर्बुलेंस से जुड़े 3 बड़े विमान हादसे
- 1994 में अमेरिका की यूएस एयर फ्लाइट 1016 लैंडिंग के दौरान तूफान से पैदा हुए टर्बुलेंस की चपेट में आकर क्रैश हो गई थी। इस हादसे में 37 लोगों की मौत हुई थी।
- 1999 में अमेरिकन एयरलाइंस फ्लाइट 1420 भी खराब मौसम और टर्बुलेंस के बाद रनवे से फिसलकर क्रैश हो गई थी, जिसमें 11 लोगों की जान गई।
- 2001 में अमेरिकन एयरलाइंस फ्लाइट 587 टेकऑफ के कुछ देर बाद वेक टर्बुलेंस की वजह से क्रैश हो गई थी। इस हादसे में विमान में सवार सभी 260 लोगों की मौत हो गई थी।
--------------------------
ये खबरें भी पढ़ें…
चेन्नई में यात्री चलती फ्लाइट का इमरजेंसी गेट खोलकर कूदा: विमान रनवे से टर्मिनल की तरफ जा रहा था
चेन्नई इंटरनेशनल एयरपोर्ट पर लैंडिंग के दौरान एयर अरेबिया की चलती फ्लाइट में एक यात्री इमरजेंसी गेट खोलकर नीचे कूद गया। घटना के बाद पायलट ने तुरंत विमान को रोक दिया और एयरपोर्ट अधिकारियों को सूचना दी। पूरी खबर पढ़ें…
हैदराबाद-हुबली फ्लाइट 2 घंटे हवा में चक्कर काटती रही:खराब मौसम के चलते हिलने लगा प्लेन; पैसेंजर रोते नजर आए
हैदराबाद से हुबली जा रही Fly-91 एयरलाइन की एक फ्लाइट खराब मौसम के चलते 2 घंटे हवा में ही चक्कर काटती रही। सोशल मीडिया में वायरल VIDEO में पैसेंजर रोते हुए और हाथ जोड़कर प्रार्थना करते दिख रहे हैं। पूरी खबर पढ़ें…

items.body_text:
- Hindi News
- National
- Udhayanidhi Stalin Trisha Krishnan Remark; Tamilnadu TVK DMK | Madras HC
तमिलनाडु के नेता विपक्ष उदयनिधि स्टालिन गिरफ्तार:एक्ट्रेस तृषा पर आपत्तिजनक टिप्पणी करने का आरोप, बोले- बदले की भावना से कार्रवाई
- कॉपी लिंक
तमिलनाडु के नेता प्रतिपक्ष और डीएमके नेता उदयनिधि स्टालिन को अभिनेत्री तृषा पर आपत्तिजनक टिप्पणी के मामले में मंगलवार को गिरफ्तार कर लिया गया। पुलिस ने उनके खिलाफ 6 धाराओं में केस दर्ज किया है।
गिरफ्तारी से बचने के लिए उदयनिधि ने मद्रास हाईकोर्ट में अग्रिम जमानत की अर्जी दाखिल की थी। हालांकि, उस पर सुनवाई होने से पहले ही पुलिस ने उन्हें अरेस्ट कर लिया।
सोमवार को तंजावुर में कावेरी जल विवाद पर आयोजित रैली में उदयनिधि मुख्यमंत्री सी. जोसेफ विजय पर निशाना साध रहे थे। इसी दौरान भीड़ से "तृषा, तृषा" के नारे लगे।
आरोप है कि इस पर उन्होंने कहा, "पानी कहीं और पहुंचे या न पहुंचे, वहां जरूर पहुंचना चाहिए।" बाद में उन्होंने सफाई दी कि उनका इशारा कावेरी के पानी की ओर था।
हालांकि, विपक्षी दलों ने इस टिप्पणी को डबल मीनिंग और महिलाओं का अपमान करने वाली बताया। इसी आरोप के आधार पर उनके खिलाफ मामला दर्ज किया गया।
मामले से जुड़े अपडेट्स पढ़ने के लिए नीचे ब्लॉग से गुजर जाइए…
लाइव अपडेट्स
- कॉपी लिंक
उदयनिधि की जमानत याचिका पर जस्टिस जी.के. इलंथिरैयन की अदालत में सुनवाई हुई। इस दौरान सरकारी वकील विजय नारायण ने अदालत को बताया कि सरकार विपक्ष के नेता को रिमांड पर नहीं भेजना चाहती। उन्होंने कहा कि पूछताछ पूरी होने के बाद उन्हें मंगलवार को ही स्टेशन बेल पर रिहा कर दिया जाएगा।
- कॉपी लिंक
DMK नेता टीकेएस इलांगोवन ने कहा कि मैंने पूरी स्पीच सुनी। जैसा कहा जा रहा है, भाषण में वैसा कुछ नहीं है। उन्होंने (उदयनिधि) केवल सीएम की नाकामियां गिनाईं। किसी का अपमान नहीं किया। उन्होंने एक्ट्रेस का नाम तक नहीं लिया। केवल सरकार पर हमले किए। इस सरकार की दिक्कत यही है कि उन्हें लोगों की परवाह ही नहीं है। डीएमके को निशाना बनाने के लिए उनका (लोगों का) इस्तेमाल किया जा रहा है।
- कॉपी लिंक
मणिथानेया मक्कल काची (MMK) के अध्यक्ष और विधायक एमएच जवाहिरुल्ला ने कहा कि उदयनिधि स्टालिन की गिरफ्तारी राजनीतिक बदले के तहत की गई। तमिलनाडु सरकार उन्हें रिहा करे।
- कॉपी लिंक
उदयनिधि स्टालिन की गिरफ्तारी को लेकर डीएमके कार्यकर्ताओं ने चेन्नई की सड़कों पर प्रदर्शन किया। कई वर्कर्स को पुलिस ने हिरासत में ले लिया।
- कॉपी लिंक
उदयनिधि स्टालिन ने कहा कि मैं किसी का नाम नहीं लूंगा। मैंने कोई बुरी बात नहीं की। मैं नतीजे का सामना करने और गिरफ्तारी के तैयार हूं।
- कॉपी लिंक
एफआईआर में उदयनिधि स्टालिन पर महिला की गरिमा का अपमान करने, जानबूझकर अपमान कर शांति भंग करने, अलग-अलग समूहों के बीच वैमनस्य फैलाने, आपराधिक साजिश रचने और आपराधिक धमकी देने जैसी धाराओं में मामला दर्ज किया गया है।
इसके अलावा उनके खिलाफ तमिलनाडु महिला उत्पीड़न निषेध अधिनियम, 2002 और सूचना प्रौद्योगिकी (आईटी) अधिनियम की धारा 67 के तहत भी केस दर्ज किया गया है।
- कॉपी लिंक
मामला दर्ज होने के बाद बड़ी संख्या में पुलिसकर्मी उदयनिधि स्टालिन के चेन्नई स्थित घर पहुंचे। इस दौरान उनके समर्थक भी घर के बाहर जुट गए और पुलिस कार्रवाई का विरोध करने लगे।
कुछ देर तक मौके पर धक्का-मुक्की और नारेबाजी हुई। इसके बाद पुलिस उदयनिधि को हिरासत में लेकर अपने साथ चली गई।
- कॉपी लिंक
टीवीके विधायक रेवंत चरण ने कहा कि इससे डीएमके की राजनीतिक संस्कृति और सोच उजागर होती है। टीवीके नेता आधव अर्जुन ने उदयनिधि को ‘अश्लील निधि’ बताते हुए कहा कि उन्होंने राजनीतिक संवाद का स्तर गिराया है।
तमिलनाडु भाजपा के मुख्य प्रवक्ता नारायणन तिरुपति ने टिप्पणी को अश्लील और शर्मनाक बताते हुए उदयनिधि की गिरफ्तारी की मांग की। भाजपा नेता खुशबू सुंदर ने कहा कि उन्हें अभिनेत्री तृषा से बिना शर्त सार्वजनिक माफी मांगनी चाहिए।
- कॉपी लिंक
डीएमके सांसद टी.आर. बालू ने आरोपों को खारिज करते हुए कहा कि उदयनिधि ने किसी महिला का नाम नहीं लिया। पूरा विवाद झूठा है।
वहीं, पूर्व मंत्री टी. मनो थंगराज ने इसे राजनीतिक साजिश बताते हुए कहा कि कावेरी मुद्दे और डेल्टा क्षेत्र के किसानों की समस्याओं से ध्यान हटाने के लिए इस विवाद को हवा दी जा रही है।
- कॉपी लिंक
तृषा कृष्णन और अभिनेता सी. जोसेफ विजय ने 'घिल्ली', 'थिरुपाची', 'आथि', 'कुरुवी' और 'लियो' जैसी कई फिल्मों में साथ काम किया है। दोनों की जोड़ी तमिल सिनेमा की सबसे सफल जोड़ियों में गिनी जाती है।

- Hindi News
- National
- Arvind Kejriwal E20 Fuel Protest Photos Update; AAP Vs Ethanol Petrol | PM Residence Delhi Police
केजरीवाल ने PM आवास तक मार्च निकाला, पुलिस ने रोका:फिरोजशाह रोड पर धरने पर बैठे, बोले- E20 के खिलाफ 2 लाख+ लोगों की चिट्ठियां सौंपेंगे
- कॉपी लिंक
दिल्ली के पूर्व CM और आम आदमी पार्टी (AAP) संयोजक अरविंद केजरीवाल ने मंगलवार को E20 फ्यूल के खिलाफ प्रधानमंत्री आवास तक मार्च निकला। हालांकि, दिल्ली पुलिस ने केजरीवाल, मनीष सिसोदिया, जैस्मिन शाह समेत पार्टी के अन्य नेताओं को फिरोजशाह रोड पर ही रोक दिया।
इसके बाद केजरीवाल सहित अन्य AAP नेता फिरोजशाह रोड पर ही बीच सड़क पर धरने पर बैठ गए। AAP ने करीब 100 नेताओं और कार्यकर्ताओं के साथ यह मार्च निकाला था। पार्टी का दावा है कि उसने देशभर से 2.30 लाख से ज्यादा लोगों की याचिकाएं जुटाई हैं, जिन्हें प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी को सौंपना था।
मार्च के दौरान केजरीवाल ने कहा कि E20 के खिलाफ 2 लाख से ज्यादा लोगों ने प्रधानमंत्री को चिट्ठियां लिखी हैं, जिन्हें वे खुद प्रधानमंत्री को सौंपना चाहते हैं। लेकिन हमें पुलिस ने रोक दिया। हमने सभी चिट्ठियां मोदी जी को भेज दी हैं। केजरीवाल ने बताया कि उन्होंने प्रधानमंत्री को मैसेज भेजा है। उन्होंने कहा- हमें उम्मीद है कि पीएम हमसे मिलेंगे।
केजरीवाल के पीएम आवास मार्च से जुड़े अपडेट्स के लिए नीचे लाइव ब्लॉग से गुजर जाइए…
अपडेट्स
- कॉपी लिंक
- कॉपी लिंक
E20 के विरोध में धरने के दौरान अरविंद केजरीवाल ने आरोप लगाया कि ट्रम्प के दबाव में मोदी सरकार अमेरिका से एथनॉल खरीद रही है। अमेरिका दुनिया में सबसे ज्यादा एथनॉल बनाता है और उसने भारत पर इसे खरीदने का दबाव बनाया।
केजरीवाल ने कहा- अमेरिका का कचरा खरीदकर हमारी 30 लाख गाड़ियों पर थोपा जा रहा है। इसे रोकने के लिए हमें NEET आंदोलन से भी बड़ा आंदोलन करना होगा। उन्होंने लोगों से इस अभियान में शामिल होने की अपील करते हुए कहा कि E20 नीति के खिलाफ उनकी लड़ाई जारी रहेगी।
- कॉपी लिंक
दिल्ली AAP अध्यक्ष सौरभ भारद्वाज ने कहा- हम 2 लाख से ज्यादा लोगों की याचिकाएं लेकर आए हैं। हमें आगे जाने दिया जाना चाहिए। अगर कोई दिक्कत है तो प्रधानमंत्री कार्यालय (PMO) का कोई अधिकारी यहां आकर ज्ञापन ले ले और इस मुद्दे पर चर्चा के लिए तैयार हो जाए।
सौरभ भारद्वाज ने भारी पुलिस बल की तैनाती पर भी सवाल उठाया। उन्होंने कहा- इतनी बड़ी संख्या में पुलिस, RAF, लाठियां और ढाल देखकर हैरानी हो रही है। हम सिर्फ लोगों की चिट्ठियां प्रधानमंत्री तक पहुंचाने आए हैं।
- कॉपी लिंक
- कॉपी लिंक
केजरीवाल ने बताया कि उन्होंने पिछले महीने प्रधानमंत्री को लेटर लिखा था। जिसमें E20 पेट्रोल से जुड़ी चिंताओं पर चर्चा के लिए समय मांगा था।
केजरीवाल का दावा है कि उन्हें इस चिट्ठी का कोई जवाब नहीं मिला। इसलिए अब वे खुद पीएम आवास जाकर जनता की साइन की हुई याचिकाएं सौंपेंगे।
आम आदमी पार्टी संयोजन ने यह मांग भी रखी है कि पेट्रोल पंपों पर शुद्ध पेट्रोल और E20 दोनों के ऑप्शन मिलने चाहिए। E20 पेट्रोल की कीमतों में कटौती की जाए।
- कॉपी लिंक
दिल्ली बीजेपी अध्यक्ष हर्ष मल्होत्रा ने केजरीवाल के मार्च के ऐलान पर निशाना साधा। उन्होंने कहा कि यह कांग्रेस और केजरीवाल के बीच देश का नंबर 1 अराजकतावादी बनने की होड़ का हिस्सा है।
मल्होत्रा ने आरोप लगाया कि जब से कांग्रेस ने पीएम आवास पर प्रदर्शन किया है, केजरीवाल खुद को पीछे महसूस कर रहे हैं। बिना परमिशन धरना-प्रदर्शन करना और फिर विक्टिम कार्ड खेलना केजरीवाल की पुरानी राजनीतिक शैली है।
उन्होंने दावा किया कि जब पुलिस उन्हें बिना अनुमति के पीएम आवास में घुसने से रोकेगी, तो केजरीवाल फिर से यही कहेंगे कि सरकार ने उनसे बात करने से इनकार कर दिया।

items.title: Release Udhayanidhi Stalin today after questioning, Madras High Court tells cops
items.summary: Release Udhayanidhi Stalin today after questioning Madras High Court tells cops
items.body_text:
Release Udhayanidhi Stalin today after questioning, Madras High Court tells cops
During the hearing, Tamil Nadu Advocate General Vijay Narayan informed the Madras High Court that Thanjavur Police had arrested Udhayanidhi and taken him to Thanjavur. However, he clarified that the police did not intend to seek his judicial remand and only wanted to question him before releasing him on station bail.
The Madras High Court on Tuesday directed Tamil Nadu Police to release Assembly Leader of Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin on station bail the same day, hours after he was arrested in connection with a controversial remark that many have interpreted as referring to actor Trisha.
The court order came moments after he was arrested over a controversial remark made during a speech in which he was targeting Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay over the Cauvery water dispute.
The remark has been widely read as a sexual innuendo and as a reference to actor Trisha and her friendship with Vijay. It has also drawn condemnation from political parties across Tamil Nadu.
A complaint was lodged at Thanjavur East Police Station by S Bairavi, TVK's Central District Women's Wing Organiser for Thanjavur. The complaint alleged that when the crowd chanted "Trisha, Trisha" during the Leader of the Opposition's speech on the Cauvery issue on August 3, he responded with an obscene double-meaning remark.
The complainant accused Udhayanidhi and DMK IT wing office-bearers of intentionally degrading women, causing mental agony to the actor and women in general, and deliberately circulating a 2:39-minute video of the incident on the social media platform X to trigger public unrest.
An anticipatory bail petition was filed immediately after police arrived at Udhayanidhi's Neelankarai residence.
During the hearing, Tamil Nadu Advocate General Vijay Narayan informed the Madras High Court that Thanjavur Police had arrested Udhayanidhi and taken him to Thanjavur. However, he clarified that the police did not intend to seek his judicial remand and only wanted to question him before releasing him on station bail.
"The police do not intend to remand him to judicial custody but only to question Udhayanidhi," the state told the court.
Earlier in the day, Stalin's arrest triggered protests by DMK workers across Tamil Nadu, with cadres staging flash strikes and road-roko demonstrations condemning the police action. DMK president MK Stalin chaired a meeting at the party headquarters to decide the next course of action ahead of the Assembly session, which is set to begin on August 5.
He was booked under various sections of law, including provisions related to the use of obscene words, insulting the modesty of a woman, promoting enmity, provocation with intent to cause a riot and criminal intimidation.
Speaking to reporters before being escorted away, Udhayanidhi said, "court will decide." He also said, "Did I mention anyone's name except the CM's? (at the protest held in Thanjavur) Then why do you think this is happening? Let the court decide."
Meanwhile, TVK stepped up its protest over Udhayanidhi's alleged remark by filing complaints with the local police and the National Commission for Women on Tuesday.
At the same time, TVK national spokesperson Pazha Selvakumar submitted a formal complaint to the NCW in New Delhi, urging the Commission to issue a notice seeking an explanation and to demand an unconditional public apology from Udhayanidhi.

items.title: Air India Phuket-Delhi flight hit by severe turbulence, 12 passengers injured
items.summary: Air India PhuketDelhi flight hit by severe turbulence passengers injured
items.body_text:
Air India Phuket-Delhi flight hit by severe turbulence, 12 passengers injured
In a statement, Air India said all the passengers and crew disembarked flight AI2379 after it landed in the national capital, adding that the injured persons were taken to a medical facility at the airport for treatment.
An Air India flight operating from Phuket to Delhi encountered severe turbulence on Monday, briefly losing altitude and leaving at least 12 passengers with minor injuries. According to multiple reports, the aircraft dropped about 300 feet during the turbulence.
Data available on flight-tracking website Flightradar24 showed that flight AI2379, operated by an Airbus A320, briefly lost altitude shortly before landing in Delhi.
In a statement, Air India said all the passengers and crew disembarked the aircraft after it landed, adding that the injured persons were taken to a medical facility at the airport for treatment.
"The safety and well-being of our passengers and crew remain Air India's highest priority. We are providing all necessary support to those affected and are cooperating fully with the relevant authorities as part of the investigation," an Air India spokesperson said.
Footage from inside the aircraft has gone viral on social media, showing cracks in the cabin ceiling allegedly caused by the impact of the turbulence.
Speaking to news agency ANI, a passenger on board the flight claimed the aircraft experienced a sudden jolt about an hour and a half into the journey while most passengers were asleep.
According to the passenger, the aircraft abruptly dropped and swayed violently for nearly two to three minutes, leaving several people injured.
He claimed that a majority of those on board were affected, and said legal action would be pursued against Air India over the incident.
Tuesday's incident comes more than a year after a Delhi-Srinagar IndiGo flight was caught in severe hailstorm-induced turbulence while approaching the J&K capital city, damaging the aircraft's nose cone during its landing attempt.
Videos recorded inside the cabin during the ordeal had gone viral, showing hailstones pounding the aircraft as it shook violently, with frightened passengers screaming and praying amid the intense turbulence.

items.summary: How PKs Bankipur win hands him frontrow seat to take on Bihar CM

How PK's Bankipur win hands him front-row seat to take on Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary
Jan Suraaj's Prashant Kishor, who led a fierce campaign against Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary, is set to enter the Assembly after his historic win in Bankipur bypoll. With Kishor now set to become an MLA, his challenge to the chief minister will now shift from rallies and press conferences to the Assembly floor, where he can hold it to account on record.
Prashant Kishor (PK) won the Bankipur Assembly bypoll on Monday, securing the first seat for his Jan Suraaj Party in the Bihar legislature. The victory places the Jan Suraaj founder inside the House where he can now confront Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary directly. PK has been targeting Choudhary relentlessly since the latter was made the chief minister in April, and his criticism of the BJP leader has been an important poll plank of the poll-strategist-turned politician.
Kishor returned to Bihar after years as a political strategist across states to build a political alternative. In a state where many with resources choose to leave, his decision to stay, struggle, and contest has already changed how people see him — as someone willing to invest his future in Bihar. Now, his repeated targeting of Choudhary, who PK alleged has a criminal background and is incompetent to lead the state, the Bihar CM would remain in the first-time MLAs crosshairs in the Assembly.
As an MLA, Kishor is expected to carry into the Assembly the style of politics that has defined his campaign — combining fact-and-data-driven criticism of governance with scathing attacks on CM Samrat Choudhary.
While PK has consistently questioned the BJP government over jobs, migration, education and healthcare, his most sustained political offensive has been directed at Choudhary. His victory in Bankipur now gives him institutional space to pursue a campaign that, until now, has largely been fought through press conferences, padyatras and public meetings.
Unlike the Opposition's broader attacks on the BJP-led government over governance and unemployment, Kishor has centred much of his criticism on Samrat Choudhary himself. His strategy has been to repeatedly raise questions about two decades-old criminal cases and challenge the Chief Minister to publicly address them.
His attacks, however, have not been limited to the ruling BJP. Kishor has also repeatedly mocked RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav over his educational qualifications, referring to him as "9th fail", while arguing that Bihar cannot be transformed by leaders whom he portrays as lacking the qualifications and vision to govern.
Yet, it is Choudhary who has remained the principal target of his most sustained and personal political offensive.
WHY SAMRAT WILL FIND A THORN BY HIS SIDE IN THE ASSEMBLY
Prashant Kishor's entry into the Bihar Assembly is expected to reshape the nature of opposition within the House beyond the personal allegations he has already levelled.
Kishor has repeatedly flagged issues of governance, development and administrative accountability. With an official seat in the House, those criticisms can now be backed in typical PK style — with data and facts, which might force the government to respond on record.
Kishor has long raised Bihar's persistent problems of unemployment, migration, poor learning outcomes, inadequate healthcare infrastructure, and uneven infrastructure delivery. In public meetings and press interactions, he has frequently cited official statistics on migration, school dropout rates, job creation under various schemes and the condition of rural roads and power supply.
Once inside the Assembly, he is likely to deploy the same approach to pin the Samrat Choudhary administration down.

items.title: Renowned education pioneer & former West Bengal, Bihar Governor Dr D Y Patil passes away aged 90
items.summary: Renowned education pioneer, former Governor of Bihar, West Bengal and Tripura, and Padma Shri recipient Dr D Y Patil passed away on Tuesday at the age of 90 in Kolhapur following age-related illness.
items.body_text:
Image Credit: Renowned educationist, philanthropist, and former Governor of Bihar, West Bengal, and Tripura, Padma Shri Dr Dnyandeo Yashwantrao (D Y) Patil. (IANS)
Padma Shri Dr Dnyandeo Yashwantrao (D Y) Patil, a visionary who transformed Maharashtra's landscape across education, healthcare, and social development, has passed away. His demise has sent a wave of grief across the nation's academic, political, and social circles.
Through his forward-thinking leadership and philanthropic vision, Dr Patil elevated higher education, medical care, and sports infrastructure in India to unprecedented heights, building institutions that continue to shape millions of lives.
Dr D Y Patil is widely regarded as one of India's most prominent educationists. For him, education was not merely a medium to obtain degrees, but the foundation for character building and nation-building.
Historic achievement: Dr Patil holds the unique national record of establishing seven independent universities across India—a landmark milestone in Indian higher education history.
Global footprint: Through these deemed and state universities, thousands of domestic and international students gain access to modern professional courses, cutting-edge research, and academic excellence.
Alongside education, Dr Patil made massive contributions to the public health sector.
He established state-of-the-art super-specialty hospitals and medical colleges in key urban hubs including Kolhapur, Pune, and Navi Mumbai. These facilities have provided quality, affordable healthcare to millions of patients while simultaneously advancing medical education, clinical training, and scientific research.
Dr Patil's vision extended well beyond academics and medicine into sports infrastructure.
He established the world-renowned D Y Patil Stadium in Navi Mumbai, widely acknowledged as one of the most modern sports complexes in Asia. Equipped with international-grade facilities, the stadium has hosted iconic national and international sporting events, including the Indian Premier League (IPL) and FIFA tournament fixtures.
Beyond his role as an institution builder, Dr Patil served with distinction in high constitutional offices as the Governor of Bihar, Tripura, and West Bengal.
During his gubernatorial tenures, he was widely admired for upholding constitutional dignity, personal simplicity, and a deep commitment to public welfare. His vast administrative experience and compassionate social perspective set a benchmark in governance.
Academics and policy experts note that while creating an institution is challenging, sustaining it over decades with uncompromised quality, integrity, and discipline is a rare feat. Dr Patil turned this challenge into a lifelong mission, establishing a sustainable, gold-standard model for private education and healthcare in India.
Following the announcement of his passing, prominent leaders from political, social, and academic spheres expressed deep condolences. With his demise, India loses a pioneering educationist, a compassionate leader, and a dedicated public servant whose legacy will inspire generations to come.

items.title: J&K on high alert: Massive security operations underway ahead of Independence Day after twin terror attacks
items.summary: Kashmir Valley remains on high alert after twin terror attacks. Security forces intensify operations amid the Amarnath Yatra, Independence Day preparations, and efforts to track terrorists still at large.
items.body_text:
Image Credit: Zee News.
Security has been placed on high alert across the Kashmir Valley, from south Kashmir to north Kashmir, following two recent terror attacks and intelligence inputs suggesting that terrorists may attempt further strikes. Authorities have intensified security measures across the region as they work to track down the attackers, protect the ongoing Amarnath Yatra, and secure upcoming Independence Day celebrations. The heightened alert comes amid concerns that Pakistan is attempting to shift international attention away from developments in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (POK).
According to intelligence officials, Pakistan is seeking to divert global focus from Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir toward the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir. At the same time, security agencies are dealing with a three-fold challenge: apprehending the terrorists responsible for the recent attacks, safeguarding the Shri Amarnath Yatra, and ensuring robust security ahead of Independence Day.
The latest attacks have heightened concerns across the Valley. In separate incidents, a head constable of the Jammu and Kashmir Police and two non-local labourers were killed. The attacks prompted an immediate security response and led to enhanced deployment across sensitive areas.
Security forces have strengthened their presence throughout the Valley, particularly at vulnerable locations, crowded markets, transport hubs, and prominent public spaces such as Lal Chowk in Srinagar.
In Srinagar, the Jammu and Kashmir Police have established additional checkpoints and vehicle barricades at key entry and exit points. Vehicles are undergoing extensive inspections, while commuters are being subjected to identity verification checks as part of the heightened security measures.
A comprehensive three-tier security arrangement is already in place for the ongoing Shri Amarnath Yatra. The security grid extends from the Bhagwati Nagar base camp in Jammu to the twin base camps at Pahalgam and Baltal, and further up to the holy cave shrine.
- Enhanced deployment along Yatra routes
- Round-the-clock surveillance and monitoring
- Additional checkpoints at sensitive locations
- Coordination among multiple security agencies
Officials said the attacks over the past fortnight have emerged as a major concern for security agencies. The Resistance Front (TRF), which is widely assessed as a proxy of Lashkar-e-Taiba, claimed responsibility for the attacks and reportedly threatened to continue carrying out similar strikes.
Following these developments, security forces have intensified search-and-cordon operations across all districts of the Kashmir Valley to identify and neutralise those involved.
After the Anantnag attack that claimed the life of a police head constable, security agencies detained nearly 3,300 suspected overground workers (OGWs) from various parts of the Valley for questioning as part of the wider investigation.
Meanwhile, the probe into the Kulgam attack, in which two non-local labourers were killed, remains ongoing. Officials said extensive operations are underway and all available leads are being pursued to identify and apprehend those responsible.
Over the last 24 hours, security forces arrested two suspected overground workers from Pulwama and Baramulla districts. During the operations, arms, ammunition, and anti-national posters were recovered. Investigators believe the posters were intended for anti-India propaganda ahead of Independence Day celebrations.
Officials said, “Security will remain on high alert across the Union Territory until the Independence Day functions conclude. Forces continue to balance the urgent task of tracking the terrorists still at large with the simultaneous requirements of protecting the Amarnath Yatra and ensuring heightened security for the forthcoming national celebrations.”

items.body_text:
Image Credit: Leader of Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin. (IANS)
The Tamil Nadu Police on Tuesday arrested Leader of Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin immediately after a case against him was booked in connection with remarks that he had made in a political rally. The remarks, made in response to a heckler who interrupted him in a rally criticizing Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on the issue of the Cauvery water dispute, have received widespread political backlash in the state.
After the police raid on his Chennai home, Udhayanidhi has moved the Madras High Court for anticipatory bail, with the court due to hear the application in the afternoon.
#WATCH | DMK leader and LoP Udhayanidhi Stalin detained by Police from his Chennai residence, following an FIR against him over his alleged defamatory remarks against actor Trisha and CM Vijay. Slogans directed at actor Trisha were raised at his rally yesterday. pic.twitter.com/JUk7cpaTdG
— ANI (@ANI) August 4, 2026
The political row broke out when the DMK party's Udhayanidhi was addressing a public meeting on the failure of the incumbent Tamil Nadu Vetri Kazhagam (TVK) government in getting Cauvery water for delta farmers.
What happened? During the course of his speech, a heckler from the crowd screamed the name "Trisha". Pausing for a second, the DMK leader made a statement that has now become a political row involving various political parties in the state.
Condemnation: All major political parties in Tamil Nadu have condemned the statement, describing them as vulgar, derogatory, and inappropriate in the political discourse.
The ruling TVK has fired a barrage at the Leader of Opposition after the incident:
"The DMK leader is tarnishing the movement spearheaded by the great scholar Annadurai through obscene language and double-meaning speeches. This kind of statement is indicative of perversion regarding women which will not be appreciated by mothers, sisters, or parents in Tamil Nadu," said TVK leader Aadhav Arjuna on social media.
Felix Gerald, the spokesman for the TVK, went on to ask if Udhayanidhi would use such statements even in front of his own family members, while the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has called for immediate legal action:
BJP stand: The BJP spokesperson in Tamil Nadu, Narayanan Thirupathy, described the remarks as "disgusting, obscene, and shameful," and has called for the arrest of Udhayanidhi.
Demand for apology: The BJP leader Khushbu Sundar called for Udhayanidhi to give an unconditional apology to actress Trisha, while another former state BJP president, K. Annamalai, condemned the speech.

items.title: ‘Kanwariyas neither beat up police nor tore uniforms’: Meerut Police debunk viral claims spread by Leftist, Extremist handles
items.summary: Meerut Police stated that the video going viral on social media with the claim that Kanwariyas assaulted police personnel and tore their uniforms is completely false
items.body_text:
During the month of Sawan, Kanwariyas seem to bother left-wingers the most. Consequently, continuous efforts are made during this period to tarnish their image in every possible way. A recent attempt was made regarding an incident in Meerut, where a video went viral on social media, spreading rumours that Kanwariyas had assaulted police personnel. However, when the police issued an official statement on the matter, the truth turned out to be completely different.
What Was in the Video?
In the viral video on social media, a few Kanwariyas can be seen standing outside a jeep, repeatedly shouting phrases like “Pull him out, get him out!” They had surrounded the police jeep, continuously trying to drag someone out of the vehicle. Several left-leaning individuals and extremists shared this video from their social media handles to build a specific narrative.
Accusations Against Kanwariyas for Beating Police Officers
Consider the tweet by ‘Muslim Voice Cell’. Targeting the Kanwariyas, the tweet read: “Look at the state of law and order in UP. In Meerut’s Daurala, after a collision with a motorcyclist, plainclothes police officers who reached the spot were dragged out of the jeep and beaten up by Kanwariyas.”
Journalist Piyush Rai also shared the video with a similar claim, which was subsequently reposted by fact-checker Mohammed Zubair.
Sachin Gupta similarly claimed in his tweet that after a motorcyclist hit the Kanwariyas, the police arrived at the scene. However, the Kanwariyas started beating up the police officers while the motorcyclist who caused the accident fled.
Zakir Tyagi similarly spread the news, claiming that the Kanwariyas beat the police so mercilessly that the officers had to run to save their lives.
Police Statement
Meerut Police has now issued an official statement regarding this incident. They stated that the video circulating on social media with claims that Kanwariyas assaulted police officers and tore their uniforms is completely false.
According to the police, the investigation revealed that on the night of August 3, two groups of Kanwariyas came face-to-face. A person named Sonu, along with his companion Guddu, was heading to Haridwar in a vehicle when they got into a collision and a subsequent brawl with another group of Kanwariyas coming from the opposite direction.
In response, the Daurala police station team arrived at the spot and tactfully tried to intervene and stop both parties. During this process, Sonu and Guddu were seated inside the police vehicle. It was at this moment that the opposing group became aggressive and attempted to pull these two individuals out of the vehicle. A senior police officer clarified that following the incident, both parties were taken for medical examinations, and further legal action is currently underway.
Misleading Media Coverage
It is worth noting that this entire incident was misrepresented not just on social media, but in mainstream media as well. Without verifying the facts with the police first, it was initially reported that Kanwariyas had beaten up police officers. Although news outlets later updated their reports after the police issued a statement, channels like TV9 Bharatvarsh initially broadcast the news with headlines explicitly stating that “2 police personnel were beaten up.”

The arrest of DMK leader Udhayanidhi Stalin over his alleged vulgar remarks targeting actor Trisha Krishnan has once again put the Tamil Nadu minister’s political style under the spotlight. While the DMK has predictably dismissed the action as “political vendetta,” the controversy is part of a much longer pattern.
For years, Udhayanidhi Stalin has built a reputation for making inflammatory remarks, seemingly secure in the belief that outrage would only strengthen his political brand.
His latest controversy stems from a public rally in Thanjavur, where he responded to chants of actor Trisha’s name with an offensive double entendre. The remarks prompted complaints from the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), BJP leaders, and appeals to the National Commission for Women, who argued that such comments normalise the objectification of women in public life.
Yet, if there is one episode that best encapsulates Udhayanidhi Stalin’s penchant for reckless rhetoric, it is his infamous September 2023 speech calling for the “eradication” of Sanatana Dharma.

On 2 September 2023, Udhayanidhi Stalin attended the so-called “Eradicate Sanatan Conference” organised by the Tamil Nadu Progressive Writers and Artists Association in Chennai. Rather than distancing himself from the event’s provocative title, he openly endorsed it.
“The title of this conference has been excellently coined. You’ve named it ‘Eradicate Sanatan Conference’ and not ‘Oppose Sanatan Conference’,” he declared, congratulating the organisers.
He then proceeded to compare Sanatana Dharma to diseases and pests.
“Mosquitoes, dengue, flu, malaria, corona, we should not oppose these things. They have to be eradicated. The same is the case with Sanatanam.”
The analogy sparked nationwide outrage because it went far beyond criticism of religious practices or social customs. By equating Sanatana Dharma, a faith followed by hundreds of millions of Hindus, with diseases that must be eliminated, Stalin crossed into rhetoric that many viewed as openly hateful towards an entire religious tradition.
He did not stop there.
Attempting to justify his position, Udhayanidhi claimed that Sanatana Dharma represented inequality, caste discrimination, and opposition to social justice. He asserted that it was something “eternal” that could not be questioned and therefore deserved abolition rather than debate.
Following the event, he reiterated his position on social media, stating that they would continue their efforts to eliminate Sanatan.
A government minister at an anti-Hindu platform
The controversy was amplified because Udhayanidhi was not merely a party functionary but a serving minister in the Tamil Nadu government. The conference was also attended by HR&CE Minister P.K. Sekarbabu and several prominent leaders from the DMK and its ideological allies, including Dravidar Kazhagam chief K. Veeramani, VCK leader Thol. Thirumavalavan, Congress leader Peter Alphonse, CPI(M) representatives, and others.
The participation of ministers at an event explicitly advocating the “eradication” of Sanatana Dharma strengthened criticism that the DMK government was lending legitimacy to rhetoric directed against Hindu beliefs while simultaneously controlling thousands of Hindu temples through the state’s HR&CE Department.
A pattern of provocation
The Trisha controversy therefore appears less like an isolated lapse and more like another chapter in a recurring pattern.
Whether it was comparing Hinduism to dengue and malaria, celebrating an event dedicated to the “eradication” of Sanatana Dharma, or now allegedly making vulgar insinuations about a woman actor during a political rally, Udhayanidhi Stalin has repeatedly chosen provocation over restraint.

items.title: Muslim consolidation in Bankipura by-election and ideological clarity: How Muslims sacrificed RJD for Prashant Kishor to defeat BJP
items.summary: The Bankipura by-election saw Muslim voters and several other communities rally behind Prashant Kishor over the RJD, signalling a major political realignment driven by the desire to defeat the BJP.
items.body_text:
The Bankipura Assembly by-election has highlighted a clear shift in voting behaviour, with many Muslim voters choosing Jan Suraaj Party (JSP) founder Prashant Kishor over the Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD). Conversations with voters suggest that the decision was driven less by traditional political loyalties and more by the belief that Kishor was the strongest candidate to defeat the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). This thinking also found support among sections of Yadavs, upper castes, Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Kayasths.
Muslims shift from RJD to Prashant Kishor
In Sabzibagh, where Muslim voters have a strong presence, many residents said the community backed Prashant Kishor because they did not see the RJD candidate as capable of defeating the BJP. Mohammad Rizwan, a resident, said community members met at a nearby mosque and encouraged people to vote for the candidate who had the best chance of winning against the BJP. He said Kishor’s campaign created the impression that he was giving the BJP its toughest contest.
RJD’s weak campaign helped Kishor
The same mood was visible in Yaarpur and Jakkanpur, where many Yadav voters shifted towards the JSP. Mangesh Yadav said Tejashwi Yadav joined the campaign only in its final two days after returning from a foreign trip. He added that senior RJD leaders, including Sudhakar Singh, Misa Bharti, Sanjay Yadav and Manoj Jha, were largely absent, while the BJP had deployed around 40 star campaigners. According to him, many voters felt Kishor was fighting the election almost single-handedly and decided to support him.
BJP stronghold slips despite development work
The result was significant because Bankipura had remained a BJP bastion for nearly three decades. In the 2025 Assembly election, BJP national president Nitin Nabin retained the seat for a fifth consecutive term by defeating RJD’s Rekha Kumari by more than 51,000 votes. His father, Navin Kishore Prasad Sinha, had represented the constituency since 1995. In May 2026, Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary and Nitin Nabin inaugurated the ₹115-crore Mandiri Nala project, with the road named after Nabin’s father. Even so, voters rejected BJP candidate Neeraj Kumar Sinha.
Support came from different communities
Deepak Sharma, a Bhumihar from Mandiri, said Kishor appealed to voters because he focused on public issues and gave the message of voting for the future of children rather than making big promises. Brahmin voter Akhilesh Mishra said the BJP had become overconfident after winning the seat repeatedly and fielded a candidate who failed to connect with voters.
In SC-dominated areas such as Peermuhani and Daldali Road, residents said Kishor personally visited them and sought support for change. Bittu Kumar said Kishor even told people they could accept money from BJP workers if offered but should vote for the JSP.
The BJP also lost support in Kayasth-dominated localities such as Boring Canal Road, Kadamkuan, Exhibition Road, and Rajendra Nagar. One Kayasth voter, who had campaigned for the BJP, said he ultimately voted for Kishor and even asked his wife to press serial number 9 instead of the BJP’s serial number 2. Many residents also expressed anger over police action against students during the 25th July Bihar Bandh over NEET-UG irregularities.
A vote for change
Political observer Sanjay Kumar said Bankipura has never voted for a single ideology consistently and has elected candidates from the Congress, CPI, Left parties, the Janata Party, and even independents in the past. According to him, this election reflected the voters’ desire for change, with many communities putting aside old political preferences and rallying behind Prashant Kishor because they believed he was the most credible challenger to the BJP.

items.title: US Holds Off 'Biggest Strike Since WWII', Trump Calls New Iran Talks 'Last Chance'
items.summary: Trump called new US-Iran talks the "last chance" for a deal and paused a planned major strike after Gulf allies urged restraint, saying negotiations will focus on reopening the Strait of Hormuz and denuclearization.
items.body_text:
US Holds Off 'Biggest Strike Since WWII', Trump Calls New Iran Talks 'Last Chance'
Trump called new US-Iran talks the "last chance" for a deal and paused a planned major strike after Gulf allies urged restraint, saying negotiations will focus on reopening the Strait of Hormuz and denuclearization.
- World News
- 6 min read
Washington: President Donald Trump has played this hand before during the 5-month-old Iran war — but this time, he insists it’s different.
The president on Monday said that new talks between Washington and Tehran are the “last chance” for Iran to forge a deal and avoid an escalation of U.S. strikes on the country.
Trump, speaking at the Oval Office, said he expects negotiations will focus on reopening the Strait of Hormuz and create a pathway for Iran to address the United States’ concerns about its nuclear program. He told reporters they would likely learn about the status of the negotiations “today or tomorrow.”
“The first phase is the opening of the straits. The second phase will be the denuclearization," the Republican president said. “And that will take a little while.”

items.body_text:
25 US States Sue Trump Over Sweeping New Tariffs On 60 Countries, Call It Illegal Tax Hike
25 states sued the Trump administration over new 10%-12.5% tariffs on 59 countries, calling them an illegal workaround after the Supreme Court struck down prior IEEPA tariffs.
- World News
- 4 min read
Washington: Twenty-five states sued the Trump administration Monday over its latest tariffs, calling them a pretext for replacing import taxes the Supreme Court struck down in February.
The United States last month imposed double-digit tariffs on 59 countries and the European Union, charging that they had not done enough to crack down on imports produced by forced labor. The new tariffs took effect just as the clock ran out on temporary tariffs President Donald Trump had turned to after the Supreme Court defeat.
“After losing at the Supreme Court, the administration is once again trying to illegally raise taxes on families and businesses with a new round of tariffs,” said New York Attorney General Letitia James.
Joining New York in the lawsuit announced Monday are Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, Hawaii, Illinois, Kentucky, Massachusetts, Maryland, Maine, Michigan, Minnesota, Nevada, New Jersey, New Mexico, North Carolina, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, Virginia, Vermont, Washington and Wisconsin.
Advertisement
Trump, who argues that high tariffs will revive American manufacturing, last year overturned decades of U.S. policy that favored lower tariffs and ever-freer trade. Invoking the 1977 International Emergency Economic Powers Act, or IEEPA, he imposed double-digit tariffs on imports from almost every country, saying America’s longstanding trade deficit amounted to a national emergency.
But the Supreme Court ruled that IEEPA did not authorize tariffs. The decision forced the administration to send refunds to importers who’d paid the tariffs. Eager to make up the lost revenue, Trump turned to temporary 10% worldwide tariffs. But they expired at midnight July 24.
Advertisement
Now he’s tapping more durable tariffs under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, which permits the president to impose import taxes and other sanctions against countries found to engage in unfair trade practices. Trump used Section 301 to impose big tariffs on China in his first term, and they survived court challenges.
The administration invoked Section 301 to impose the forced-labor tariffs, which range from 10% to 12.5% and hit countries that provide 99% of American imports.
“The United States is using its lawful authority to obtain the elimination of unreasonable acts, policies, and practices that burden U.S. commerce,” White House spokesman Kush Desai said. “A foreign country’s failure to impose and effectively enforce a prohibition on the importation of goods produced with forced labor is unreasonable and burdens U.S. commerce, including American workers, and must be addressed. Section 301 tariffs have proven to be a legally durable tool since the President’s first term, and they remain so now.”
The states’ lawsuit follows two other lawsuits filed in the Court of International Trade in July by small businesses that also challenged the 301 tariffs.
Both of those lawsuits argue that the government didn’t adequately establish its case against each specific economy or spell how the tariffs will eliminate the specified practice they are being levied for, as required by Section 301.
Barry Appleton, a law professor and co-director of New York Law School’s Center for International Law, said the challenges stem from the fact that the 301 tariffs are the third time the administration has tried to impose similar worldwide tariffs under different statutes, and their “nearly copy-pasted” nature could pose a challenge to defend in court.
However, he said while the statutes that the administration implemented tariffs under previously were novelties and hadn’t been used before for that purpose, Section 301 has been used before.

items.title: Pakistan Blocks Al Jazeera Website, Tightens Rules for Foreign Media Amid Kashmir Unrest
items.summary: Pakistan has restricted access to Al Jazeera and other news websites after coverage of unrest and elections in Pakistan-administered Kashmir, raising concerns over press freedom. New rules for foreign journalists and cyber crackdowns highlight tightened media control.
items.body_text:
Pakistan Blocks Al Jazeera Website, Tightens Rules for Foreign Media Amid Kashmir Unrest
Pakistan has restricted access to Al Jazeera and other news websites after coverage of unrest and elections in Pakistan-administered Kashmir, raising concerns over press freedom. New rules for foreign journalists and cyber crackdowns highlight tightened media control.
- World News
- 3 min read
Pakistan has restricted access to Al Jazeera's website inside the country, along with several other news websites, after the channel's coverage of ongoing unrest and elections in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir. The move has raised fresh concerns about press freedom in the region.
What Is Happening
Users across Pakistan have reported that they cannot open Al Jazeera's website. Screenshots shared online show error messages such as "connection reset" and "network connection was lost" when people try to load the site. Along with Al Jazeera, several local and regional news websites are also said to be affected.
There has been no official statement from the Pakistani government confirming that it has blocked these websites. However, the timing has led many to link the restrictions to recent reporting on protests and a security crackdown in the region.
Why Tensions Are High
The restrictions come during a tense period in Pakistan-administered Kashmir. The region recently held elections, and voting was disrupted in several areas due to protests and road blockades.
Advertisement
Local groups say that protests and unrest in the region have caused a large number of deaths since June. A civilian rights body linked to the protests has also shared visuals that appear to show security personnel using force against unarmed people, though this has not been independently confirmed.
An international human rights organisation has asked the authorities to stop using force against protesters, restore communication services in the region, and hold anyone responsible for wrongdoing accountable.
Advertisement
Government's Response to Al Jazeera
Pakistan's Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has openly criticised Al Jazeera's reporting. In a statement posted on its official social media account, the ministry said the channel had reported only from a few selected polling stations in Muzaffarabad and used specific timings and prepared statements from certain individuals to give a one-sided picture of the election.
The ministry described this as poor-quality journalism and claimed it was an attempt by outside forces to question the fairness of the election and the choice made by voters in the region.
New Rules for Foreign Journalists
Alongside the restrictions on Al Jazeera, Pakistan's Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has also issued new guidelines for foreign media working in the country. Under these rules, international journalists and media staff will need special permission, called a No Objection Certificate (NOC), if they want to report from places other than the three major cities of Lahore, Karachi, and Islamabad.
This means that for regions like AJK, where the current unrest is taking place, foreign reporters would need to first get approval from the government before travelling there for coverage.
Reports also mention that Pakistan's cyber crime authorities have taken action against several YouTube channels, accusing them of sharing content that is critical of state institutions, adding to the wider picture of tightened media control during this period.

items.title: 'I Look At It As Comedy': Udhayanidhi Stalin Reacts After Detention Over Remarks On Actor Trisha
items.summary: 'I Look At It As Comedy': Udhayanidhi Stalin Reacts After Detention Over Remarks On Actor Trisha
items.body_text:
Udhayanidhi Stalin was detained by Tamil Nadu Police following a complaint from the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK). The complaint was lodged over his alleged derogatory remarks concerning actor Trisha.
'I Look At It As Comedy': Udhayanidhi Stalin Reacts After Detention Over Remarks On Actor Trisha
Complaints against DMK senior leader Udhyanidhi Stalin were filed by the ruling TVK at the Thanjavur East police station and by the National Commission for Women.
- DMK's Udhayanidhi Stalin detained, calls police action
- Police booked Udhayanidhi for alleged derogatory remarks, creating enmity.
- Udhayanidhi denied wrongdoing; DMK leaders defended his statements.
Senior Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) leader Udhayanidhi Stalin on Tuesday described his detention by Tamil Nadu Police as a "comedy" in his first public reaction after being taken into custody over his alleged remarks on actor Trisha.
Police detained Udhayanidhi after the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) lodged a complaint against him at the Thanjavur East police station. A separate complaint was also submitted to the National Commission for Women (NCW) in New Delhi.
He has been booked under various provisions of the Bharatiya Nyay Sanhita (BNS), the Information Technology Act and Section 4 of the Tamil Nadu Women Harassment Prevention Act over allegations of making derogatory remarks about women and creating enmity among a section of people.
ALSO READ | Udhayanidhi Stalin Detained Over 'Trisha' Chant Remark At Cauvery Protest; Vijay's TVK Calls It 'Disgusting'
'I Am Ready to Face the Consequences'
Speaking to reporters while being escorted by police amid a large crowd, Udhayanidhi dismissed the action against him.
"I look at it as a comedy," he said.
While seated inside the police vehicle, the DMK leader added, "I did not name anybody and I did not speak in bad taste. I am ready to face the consequences and I am not afraid of arrest. I don't think they have that much brains."
Udhayanidhi Denies Making Any Wrong Remarks
Reiterating his stand, Udhayanidhi maintained that he had not made any objectionable comments.
"I have not said anything wrong. I have not said anything wrong against anybody," he said.
Chennai Police Commissioner A. Amalraj also reached the spot before Udhayanidhi was taken away by the police for questioning.
DMK Defends Leader as Political Row Escalates
Senior DMK leader and party MP T.R. Baalu defended Udhayanidhi following the detention.
"He has not mentioned anyone, and no reference was made against any particular woman by the leader of the opposition. These are cooked up false stories," Baalu said.
The controversy erupted after Udhayanidhi allegedly made offensive remarks about actor Trisha, triggering criticism from the ruling TVK as well as the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Congress.

items.body_text:
