items.title: Pakistan, Iran reaffirm resolve to expand bilateral trade to $10bn
items.summary: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan and Iran on Tuesday reiterated their resolve to expand bilateral trade to $10 billion, with Commerce Minister Jam calling for transforming “historic brotherly relations” with Iran into a robust economic partnership. Since March this year, both countries have rolled out a series of measures to facilitate border trade, including easing customs procedures, formalising Taftan as a customs station, and notifying new transit routes, against the backdrop of the ongoing US-Iran confl
items.body_text:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan and Iran on Tuesday reiterated their resolve to expand bilateral trade to $10 billion, with Commerce Minister Jam calling for transforming “historic brotherly relations” with Iran into a robust economic partnership.
Since March this year, both countries have rolled out a series of measures to facilitate border trade, including easing customs procedures, formalising Taftan as a customs station, and notifying new transit routes, against the backdrop of the ongoing US-Iran conflict in the Middle East that has strained economies in the region and beyond.
Their latest engagement took place at the 10th session of the Pak–Iran Joint Trade Committee (JTC), which is being held in Islamabad from August 3-5. The meeting was co‑chaired by Iranian Industry, Mine and Trade Minister Mohammad Atabak and Pakistan’s Commerce Minister Jam Kamal Khan.
On the occasion, Khan also underscored the urgency to finalise the Pak–Iran Free Trade Agreement, a statement issued by his ministry said.
He called for the removal of barriers in border logistics and cargo movement, highlighting that joint border markets and electronic data interchange could significantly boost trade flows, it added.
According to the statement, both sides reviewed the measures already taken to enhance bilateral commerce at the meeting.
Moreover, the commerce minister said the private sector in both countries was prepared to expand trade, stressing that it was the responsibility of both governments to provide a “predictable and favourable” environment for business to them.
He expressed hope that the JTC meeting would help evolve a practical roadmap to transform trade connectivity and raise the bilateral volume to its maximum potential, the statement said.
For his part, the Iranian minister called Pakistan Iran’s “long‑term strategic trade partner”, the statement said, adding that he expressed Tehran’s desire to expand regional trade and logistics cooperation through Karachi and Gwadar ports, and the optimism that the Pak–Iran FTA would be concluded soon.
Atabak said electricity trade and regional connectivity were “new avenues of economic opportunity” for both countries, according to the statement.
It said Pakistan and Iran “reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthen cooperation in trade, investment, connectivity, and private sector partnerships”.
Tuesday’s meeting takes place around two weeks after Iranian Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni’s visit to Islamabad, where he also held a meeting with Railways Minister Hanif Abbasi. During that meeting, the two sides agreed to expand railway cooperation and strengthen cross-border connectivity.
They also discussed the revival of the Islamabad-Tehran-Istanbul (ITI) freight train service and measures to enhance regional connectivity, the statement said.
As maritime trade faces uncertainty due to the Gulf crisis, Pakistan also permitted exporters in March this year to continue shipping food and pharmaceutical products to Iran via land routes without mandatory banking instruments.
Simultaneously, Islamabad allowed rice exports to Central Asian Republics and Azerbaijan through Iran. In total, 10 food items — including rice, seafood, potatoes, meat, onions, maize, citrus fruits, bananas, tomatoes, and frozen chicken — along with two non‑food items (pharmaceuticals and tents) were cleared for land‑route exports without financial instruments.
To strengthen border management and formalise cross‑border flows, Pakistan established the same month a new customs station at Jeerak in Panjgur district, designated as the fifth crossing point for trade and transit with Iran. The facility aims to regulate passenger movement, document personal baggage, and channel informal trade into the formal economy.
This builds on earlier steps, including the opening of the Kohak Cheedgi crossing in January 2025 and the Gabd Rimdan border point in December 2024.

items.body_text:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan on Monday invited Iran’s parliament speaker and foreign minister for urgent consultations on regional developments, as Tehran described Islamabad as its primary mediator with the US.
National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq invited Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Iran’s chief negotiator with Washington and speaker of parliament. Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, meanwhile, invited his Iranian counterpart, Seyyed Abbas Araghchi. The invitations were delivered in Tehran late Monday night after Dar spoke with Araghchi.
“They exchanged views on regional and international developments, including the deteriorating situation in Occupied East Jerusalem,” the Foreign Office said in a statement.
It remained unclear when Ghalibaf and Araghchi would travel to Pakistan. A diplomatic source said both men had been asked to come as soon as possible for discussions on regional and international developments. Araghchi was in Iraq on Monday for Arbaeen, which is being observed on Tuesday.
The invitations came roughly 36 hours after US President Donald Trump announced he had canceled imminent strikes against Iran. Trump said allies had urged him to hold off because a deal appeared imminent.
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman spoke with Trump and persuaded him to call off the planned military action. Trump had also named UAE and Qatar as among the countries that had asked him to cancel the planned strikes.
Iran has been holding talks with Oman about the future of the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian authorities say they are close to an agreement but have not indicated whether the waterway would reopen or remain closed.
Pakistan has been relatively quiet on the mediation front compared with earlier efforts that produced the Islamabad MoU. It has, however, remained engaged through back channels with Iran and, together with Qatar, proposed a ceasefire plan during a nearly 13-day period of escalation.
Iran’s foreign ministry on Monday insisted that Pakistan is the main mediator with US. Spokesman Esmail Baqaei said: “The mediator in the discussions related to Iran and the US is Pakistan, and Qatar also helps in cases where necessary. To say that we have added a new mediator to the existing mediators is not, in the strict sense of the word, the case.”
Meanwhile, President Donald Trump accused Iran’s leadership of being “unbelievably duplicitous” after Tehran denied that any negotiations were underway with the US. The exchange renewed threats from Trump, who warned Iran faced “decapitation” and said he would keep up military pressure until there was a “deal, or total surrender”.
“I think we’re going to maybe get something, but I want to give them every last chance before decapitation,” Trump said, reiterating his threat to launch a major attack on Iran.
The war of words follows a familiar pattern in the five-month conflict between Washington and Tehran.
The president, who on Sunday said renewed talks would begin “tomorrow afternoon” without naming a venue or participants, added that the US Navy maintains complete control over the Strait of Hormuz.
“Nothing gets through to Iran, unless we want it to, and nothing will get through, unless a deal, or total surrender, is accomplished,” he said.
Trump had told reporters aboard Air Force One that Iran, along with Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Qatar, had asked him to hold off on what he claimed would have been “the biggest attack since World War II”.
“Would I rather make a deal? I’m not looking to kill people,” Trump said on Sunday. He described ongoing discussions as a “last chance for them to sign a good document”.
With input from Agencies
Published in Dawn, August 4th, 2026

The list published in the US Federal Register does not include Pakistan. Among South Asian c
items.body_text:
• Washington makes visa bond programme permanent; Bangladesh, Nepal among 50 countries covered, India also excluded
• Visitors from listed nations face refundable deposits of up to $20,000
WASHINGTON: Pakistan is not among the 50 countries whose citizens may now be required to deposit up to $20,000 as a financial guarantee before obtaining a US visitor visa under a new programme that took effect on Aug 1.
The list published in the US Federal Register does not include Pakistan. Among South Asian countries, Bangladesh and Nepal are covered by the programme, while India is not.
Afghanistan and Iran are not included because the United States does not maintain normal diplomatic relations with either country.
The State Department said the decision followed a review of the 2025 pilot programme, which it said significantly reduced visa overstays among travellers from participating countries and improved compliance with US immigration rules. Officials said those findings prompted Washington to make the programme permanent.
According to the department, there were 45,488 overstays from these 50 countries in 2024. In the first 10 months of the pilot, the number of overstays was fewer than 50. The visa bond requirement has also resulted in a decrease in visa issuance, as some applicants appear to self-select by not paying a bond.
Diplomatic sources also confirmed to Dawn that “Pakistan is not on the list of countries covered by the programme”.
The programme applies to applicants for B-1 business and B-2 tourist visas from countries covered by the scheme. Under the new rules, US consular officers may require selected applicants to post a refundable bond of between $10,000 and $20,000 before issuing a visa.
The regulations make permanent a visa bond pilot launched in 2025 after the US State Department concluded that it had helped reduce visa overstays.
The new rules also increase the maximum bond from $15,000 to $20,000 and eliminate the previous $5,000 minimum bond available during the pilot programme.
The 50 countries covered by the programme include 30 African nations as well as countries in Asia, the Caribbean and the Pacific.
The bond will be refunded if the visitor complies with all visa conditions and leaves the United States before the authorised period of stay expires. Applicants who overstay or otherwise violate the terms of their visas risk forfeiting the deposit.
The bond requirement does not apply automatically to all applicants from the countries covered by the programme. Instead, US consular officers will determine on a case-by-case basis whether a bond is warranted before issuing a visa.
Published in Dawn, August 4th, 2026

items.body_text:
Published August 04, 2026
The countdown is on for one last deadly game of revenge.
Disney+ has unveiled the first teaser for the second and final season of Made in Korea, confirming that Hyun Bin and Jung Woo-sung’s critically acclaimed crime thriller will return on September 09 for its six-episode farewell.
The new chapter jumps ahead nine years, with Baek Kitae (Hyun Bin) no longer hiding in the shadows.
After framing the one prosecutor he couldn't control, he's climbed to deputy director of the KCIA while quietly building a powerful cross-border drug empire.
But just when he seems untouchable, his longtime rival Jang Geonyoung (Jung Woo-sung) re-emerges with one goal: revenge.
According to Disney, both men are ready to “break every rule and cross every line to eliminate the other once and for all.”
The first season became one of Disney+'s biggest Korean hits after debuting in late 2025, earning the title of the platform's most-watched Korean original premiere of the year across Asia-Pacific.

items.title: Oil ticks up after sell-off as talks to end US-Iran war remain uncertain
items.summary: A view shows oil pump jacks outside Almetyevsk, in the Republic of Tatarstan, Russia July 14, 2025. — ReutersBrent crude up over 1% after dropping over 7%.Trump says talks with Iran underway, Tehran denies claim.Little change in shipping through Bab el-Mandeb strait: data.<p...
items.body_text:
Published August 04, 2026
- Brent crude up over 1% after dropping over 7%.
- Trump says talks with Iran underway, Tehran denies claim.
- Little change in shipping through Bab el-Mandeb strait: data.
Oil prices rebounded 1% on Tuesday from a plunge in the previous session, fuelled by concerns that Middle East supply remains at risk as a diplomatic resolution to the US-Iran war that has disrupted shipments still seems unlikely.
Front-month Brent futures rose $1.02, or 1.2%, to $84.79 a barrel by 0632 GMT after dropping 7% in the previous session to a three-week low.
US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude was up 46 cents, or 0.6%, at $80.80 a barrel after falling more than 5% in the previous session to its lowest in nearly a week.
Prices dropped after US President Donald Trump said on Sunday he was holding off on new attacks on Iran pending ongoing talks to end their war and settle claims over control of the key Strait of Hormuz.
The strategic waterway, which connects Gulf oil producers to global markets, was a channel for about a fifth of global shipments of crude oil and natural gas before the conflict.
However, on Monday, Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei rejected Trump's claim, saying no negotiations with the US were taking place and no meetings were scheduled.
"The scale of the sell-off seems fairly overdone, given that there's still considerable uncertainty. We’ve been in this situation multiple times before, only to see things unravel," ING analysts said in a note
"And with Iran denying that any talks are underway and Trump issuing warnings if no deal materialises, the backdrop clearly leaves ample room for a renewed escalation."
The Hormuz dispute is a central sticking point in talks. Washington says the memorandum of understanding agreed in June required Iran to open the waterway, while Tehran says the text explicitly preserved its authority.
Analysts at Barclays said crude oil and refined product net exports through the strait averaged 4.2 million barrels per day in the week ended July 31, versus 3.2 million the previous week.
In the Red Sea, six Saudi-flagged supertankers changed course in the Gulf of Aden recently for southern Africa, while two tankers laden with Saudi oil crossed the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, shipping data showed on Monday.
Shipping traffic at the key Gulf waterways of Bab el-Mandeb and the Strait of Hormuz held largely unchanged at the start of the week.
Hormuz remains dangerous for vessels. On Tuesday, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency flagged an incident 20 nautical miles (37 km) northeast of Oman's Al Khasab, after a cargo vessel broadcast over VHF channel 16 that it had been hit by an unknown projectile.
"While the fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis has not completely halted energy flows, it has forced longer voyage times, higher insurance costs and occasional diversions," said Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade.
"With the Strait of Hormuz, it keeps a dual-chokepoint risk in the market that prevents oil from fully unwinding its geopolitical premium."

Gul Plaza fire: IO seeks more time for completion of probe
- By Farooq Sami -
- Aug 04, 2026
The investigation into the Gul Plaza fire case could not be completed due to a lack of cooperation from the Sindh Building Control Authority (SBCA) and the Water Corporation, with the investigating officer seeking additional time from the court.
The devastating fire that broke out and engulfed Gul Plaza on the night of January 17, claimed dozens of lives, and continued for more than 32 hours before it was brought under control.
The Karachi court has granted Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) Amir Warak an extension until August 9 to complete the investigation.
DSP Amir Warak told the court that statements from officials of two departments had not yet been recorded and requested more time. Sources said officials of both departments are expected to record their statements after Chehlum.
According to sources, the investigating officer has recorded statements from officials of six government departments, including Traffic Police, Fire Brigade, Civil Defence, Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC), Deputy Commissioner South’s office, and Rescue 1122.
Sources said the investigation has placed greater responsibility on Tanveer Pasta, with investigators alleging that he failed to fulfill his responsibilities after the fire broke out.
Investigators claimed that Tanveer Pasta did not inform the Fire Brigade and instead contacted K-Electric after the incident.
The investigating officer has already recorded statements from Tanveer Pasta, Ammar Ismail, Amin, Ramzan, Nematullah, and Hudaifa.
The previous investigating officer had nominated six people, including Gul Plaza Union President Tanveer Pasta, as accused in the case. Tanveer Pasta and other suspects are currently on interim bail.

items.summary: Long-haul travelers have long complained about jet lag’s grogginess and irritability. items.body_text:
Long-haul travelers have long complained about jet lag’s grogginess and irritability. But researchers say the condition goes far deeper than fatigue, disrupting cell repair, altering liver and kidney function, and, in cases of chronic exposure, potentially raising the risk of cancer.
A Disrupted Internal Clock
The root cause of jet lag is not simply lost sleep, scientists say, but disruption to the body’s internal clock, which runs on a roughly 24-hour cycle governing when people eat, sleep and stay active.
Under normal conditions, light-sensitive cells in the eye detect darkness and trigger the release of melatonin, the hormone that induces sleep. That process is coordinated by a region of the brain known as the suprachiasmatic nucleus, or SCN.
Russell Foster, a professor of circadian neuroscience at the University of Oxford and author of the book “Life Time,” compared the SCN to an orchestra conductor that keeps the body in sync with cycles of night and day. Long-haul flights, he said, throw that system into disarray.
Symptoms tend to worsen with the number of time zones crossed, according to researchers, and are typically more severe on eastbound flights and during shorter winter days.
Airline Crews Face Chronic Exposure
While most travelers experience jet lag only occasionally, airline crews face it as a routine part of their jobs. Research has found that flight attendants working demanding schedules with little rest between flights had higher levels of the stress hormone cortisol than colleagues with lighter workloads.
Elevated cortisol helps the body manage short-term stress, but sustained exposure has been linked to a weakened immune system and increased cardiovascular risk, researchers say.
Brain scans of the flight attendants with heavier schedules also showed smaller right temporal lobes on average, and that group scored lower on memory tests, according to the research.
A separate study at the University of California, Berkeley, simulated jet lag in hamsters over four weeks, mimicking a schedule of transatlantic flights twice weekly. The animals struggled with tasks they normally handled easily, and researchers found they had stopped producing new brain cells in the hippocampus, the region tied to memory. The effects still had not reversed a month later.
Possible Links to Cancer
Laboratory studies have also raised concerns about tumor growth. Mice with induced jet lag showed faster tumor growth, while restoring a normal circadian rhythm slowed tumor development, according to the research. Separate mouse studies found chronic jet lag triggered a progression of liver disease, from fatty liver disease to hepatitis, scarring and eventually liver cancer.
Human data, while observational, points in a similar direction. A study from the 1990s found Canadian pilots had higher-than-average rates of prostate cancer. A more recent meta-analysis found female flight attendants had elevated rates of breast cancer and melanoma, and one survey found flight attendants overall reported higher cancer rates than the general population among women, though not among men.
Researchers caution that the studies are observational and cannot establish that jet lag alone drives the increased risk, since exposure to cosmic radiation during flight and other factors may also play a role.
Steps Travelers Can Take
Health experts recommend several strategies to ease jet lag’s effects:
- Adjust before departure. Travelers heading east should go to bed one to two hours earlier than usual for several days before the flight; those heading west should do the opposite.
- Consider melatonin cautiously. A 2002 Cochrane Review found melatonin can help combat jet lag, though it called for more research into its safety. The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention includes melatonin guidance in its travel recommendations, while Britain’s National Health Service does not endorse its use, citing insufficient evidence. items.summary: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan and Iran agreed Tuesday to expedite negotiations on a long-awaited free trade agreement, with officials from both countries stressing the need to conclude the pact quickly to boost bilateral trade, according to reports. Officials Reaffirm $10 Billion Trade Target The 10th Pakistan-Iran Joint Trade Committee meeting was held in Islamabad under the joint ... Read more The post Pakistan, Iran agree to fast-track $10 billion free trade agreement talks appeared first on BOL News.
items.body_text:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan and Iran agreed Tuesday to expedite negotiations on a long-awaited free trade agreement, with officials from both countries stressing the need to conclude the pact quickly to boost bilateral trade, according to reports.
Officials Reaffirm $10 Billion Trade Target
The 10th Pakistan-Iran Joint Trade Committee meeting was held in Islamabad under the joint chairmanship of Commerce Minister Jam Kamal Khan and Iran’s Minister of Industry, Mine and Trade, Mohammad Atabak, according to an official statement issued Tuesday.
The two countries reaffirmed their commitment to raising bilateral trade volume to $10 billion.
Speaking at the meeting, Jam Kamal said the time had come to transform the historic relationship between Pakistan and Iran into a strong economic partnership, and he emphasized the need to finalize the free trade agreement as soon as possible.
He said removing barriers to border logistics, customs and cargo movement was imperative, adding that establishing joint border markets and electronic data interchange systems would significantly increase bilateral trade. He said the private sectors of both countries were ready for trade and that it was the responsibility of the two governments to provide a conducive and reliable business environment.
Jam Kamal said the 10th committee meeting would chart a practical roadmap and elevate economic cooperation between the two countries.
Atabak, for his part, described Pakistan as Iran’s long-term strategic trade partner and expressed a desire to enhance regional trade and logistics cooperation through the ports of Karachi and Gwadar. He also expressed hope that the free trade agreement would be finalized soon and pointed to electricity trade and regional connectivity as new economic opportunities for both countries.
The two sides reaffirmed their commitment to further promoting cooperation in trade, investment, connectivity and the private sector. Officials said the meeting reflected the shared commitment of both countries to deepen their economic partnership, enhance regional connectivity and create new opportunities for trade and investment.
Tuesday’s meeting was the 10th session of the Joint Trade Committee since the body was established. The ninth meeting was held in Tehran from Nov. 6-7, 2021.
Pakistan and Iran have maintained a bilateral preferential trade agreement since Sept. 1, 2006. Under that agreement, Pakistan has granted tariff concessions to Iran on 338 tariff lines, while Iran has extended concessions on 309 tariff lines, with average tariff concessions of around 18%. However, due to Iran’s more restrictive tariff regime, duties applied on Pakistani exports remain significantly higher than those imposed on Iranian exports to Pakistan.

items.title: Trump criticizes Exxon, Chevron over profits; Demands lower prices at the pump
items.summary: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump on Monday criticized ExxonMobil and Chevron for posting large profits as fuel prices remain elevated, calling on the companies to pass some of those gains back to consumers in an unusual public break from an industry he has otherwise championed. Speaking to reporters, Trump said he was displeased with the scale ... Read more The post Trump criticizes Exxon, Chevron over profits; Demands lower prices at the pump appeared first on BOL News.
items.body_text:
WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump on Monday criticized ExxonMobil and Chevron for posting large profits as fuel prices remain elevated, calling on the companies to pass some of those gains back to consumers in an unusual public break from an industry he has otherwise championed.
Speaking to reporters, Trump said he was displeased with the scale of the companies’ earnings, singling out both firms by name and suggesting they were charging too much amid the current price environment. The remarks came just days after Exxon and Chevron posted strong second-quarter results, with the companies attributing part of the gains to elevated crude prices tied to the ongoing conflict involving Iran.
Neither company immediately responded to requests for comment.
A Pattern of Public Pressure
The comments fit a broader pattern for Trump, who has often used his public platform to pressure businesses rather than pursue formal regulatory action. During his first term, he leaned on automakers to keep manufacturing jobs in the United States, challenged defense contractors over contract costs, and urged pharmaceutical companies to reduce drug prices. Since returning to the White House, he has continued relying on public statements and social media posts to try to shape corporate behavior.
Earlier in the day, Trump had also criticized Chevron Chief Executive Mike Wirth over a weekend television appearance, arguing that Wirth failed to credit the administration for supporting the oil industry. In a social media post, Trump pointed to Chevron’s return to operations in Venezuela as evidence of his administration’s influence.
Chevron has maintained a presence in Venezuela for more than 100 years, continuing operations there even after the government nationalized oil projects in 2007, a period when Exxon and ConocoPhillips chose to withdraw from the country.
The American Petroleum Institute, an industry trade group, said current fuel prices reflect broader market forces rather than the actions of any single company, pointing to global supply and demand pressures along with uncertainty surrounding key shipping routes.
Political Stakes Rise With Gas Prices
Trump has made increasing domestic energy production a priority of his administration and has generally been supportive of oil and gas expansion. At the same time, he has repeatedly urged producers to keep consumer prices down, a tension that has grown more visible as fuel costs have climbed.
Trump told reporters Monday that he expects prices to fall sharply once tensions with Iran ease, and said he wants companies to lower what drivers pay at the pump.
The issue carries political weight for Trump and congressional Republicans heading into the November midterm elections, as rising gas prices, driven in part by the conflict with Iran and broader affordability concerns, have become a point of public frustration. National average gasoline prices have risen more than 30% since the U.S. and Israel struck Iran earlier this year, hovering around $4.10 a gallon.
Global crude prices fell after Trump called off a planned large-scale strike on Iran over the weekend, though retail gas prices typically take longer to reflect such shifts.
Recent earnings reports from Exxon, Chevron, Valero Energy and Marathon Petroleum showed the extent to which higher crude prices and refining margins have boosted the industry’s profits since the conflict escalated earlier this year. Valero reported its best quarterly profit since the 2022 energy crisis triggered by Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, while Chevron posted its strongest quarterly earnings in at least six years.

items.body_text:
Millions of Shia Muslims gather in Iraq’s Karbala to mark Arbaeen
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Millions of Shia Muslim pilgrims are gathering in the Iraqi holy city of Karbala to mark Arbaeen under tight security measures.
The tremendous procession follows the yearly 40-day mourning period for Imam Hussein, the Prophet Muhammad’s grandson.
Iraqi officials anticipate that up to 22 million pilgrims will visit the city. More than 4.5 million foreign travelers from 172 different countries have entered Iraq, including a significant number of Iranian pilgrims.
Thousands of security personnel have been deployed to protect the surrounding area and routes leading to the Imam Hussein Shrine.
Millions of pilgrims dressed in black walk the ancient 76-kilometer (47-mile) journey from Najaf to Karbala.
Arbaeen, one of the world’s greatest religious gatherings, has increased in popularity in the past few years.
It occurs 40 days after Ashura, the martyrdom anniversary of the Prophet Mohammad’s grandson Imam Hussein.
The event marks the end of a 40-day mourning period for the killing of Imam Hussein, the grandson of the Prophet Mohammed, by the forces of the caliph Yazid in 680 AD.
The holy city of Karbala in central Iraq represents the heart of Shiite Islam. It is where Imam Hussein and his brother Abbas are buried in two massive shrines that face one another.
Pilgrims openly demonstrate their sadness by weeping and crying in memory of Imam Hussein.

items.body_text:
Iraq tightens security to prevent cross-border attacks amid regional tensions
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi authorities have begun implementing tighter security measures to prevent rockets or drones from being launched from Iraqi territory toward neighboring countries, according to a report published Tuesday by Baghdad-based newspaper Al-Mada, citing security and political sources.
The report said security forces are increasing surveillance in Basra, the deserts of Najaf, Samawa, and Anbar, particularly in areas bordering Saudi Arabia and Jordan.
According to the sources, Iraqi authorities also plan to impose “strict penalties” on any security official found to have allowed attacks to originate from areas under their responsibility.
The reported measures follow an emergency security meeting chaired by Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, during which the government announced the formation of a joint security committee tasked with preventing further cross-border attacks.
In a statement issued after the meeting, al-Zaidi instructed security agencies to enforce the law, strengthen stability, and ensure Iraqi territory is not used as a launchpad for attacks against neighboring countries.
Government spokesman Haider al-Aboudi also said in a televised interview that the prime minister’s firm position had helped avert what he described as a potential military strike against Iraq.
Despite the new measures, Al-Mada’s sources questioned whether Baghdad would be able to completely prevent future drone launches or avoid possible retaliatory action by neighboring states.
The report said U.S. officials believe some Iran-supplied ballistic missiles remain hidden inside Iraq. However, a senior figure from a major Shiite political party, speaking anonymously, told the newspaper that armed factions have temporarily stepped back from using such missiles following U.S. President Donald Trump’s decision to halt what he described as a planned strike against Iran.
According to the report, Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) also ordered the evacuation of facilities in Nineveh as a precaution against potential future U.S. airstrikes.
Al-Mada reported that most members of the ruling Coordination Framework support the government’s official approach to responding to the regional crisis through diplomatic and, if necessary, military channels.
However, the newspaper said one influential Shiite leader continues to oppose the government’s position.
According to the report, armed factions have given the government until Friday to respond to Saudi Arabia following recent military developments, while some groups reportedly oppose Baghdad’s efforts to bring weapons under exclusive state control.
The newspaper also cited political analysts who argued that Iraq remains caught between broader regional tensions involving the United States, Iran, and Gulf countries, increasing the risk of further military escalation.
The claims published by Al-Mada are based on unnamed security and political sources and have not been independently confirmed by Iraqi authorities.

Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly reaffirmed that securing Egypt’s energy needs remains a top government priority as part of efforts to ensure the sustainable supply of petroleum products and natural gas to all sectors.
During a meeting in New Alamein City with Minister of Petroleum and Mineral Resources Karim Badawi, Madbouly stressed the importance of continued coordination among relevant authorities and the implementation of plans to increase domestic production and accelerate the development of new discoveries to strengthen energy security, maximize the use of Egypt’s natural resources and reinforce the country’s position as a regional energy trading hub.
Badawi reviewed the ministry’s plan to secure domestic energy supplies throughout August, outlining measures taken to guarantee fuel availability, operational alternatives and the implementation of various contingency scenarios.
The minister said the ministry continues to closely monitor the energy supply system, maintain a high state of preparedness and respond swiftly to any developments to ensure uninterrupted supplies to all sectors.
He added that the ministry’s emergency plans, preemptive scenarios and operational alternatives have proven effective in addressing changing conditions, helping secure natural gas and fuel supplies while maintaining stable electricity generation and supporting other vital sectors.
Badawi also said shipments of liquefied natural gas (LNG) and petroleum fuels are arriving on schedule to ensure the continuous operation of power generation facilities during the peak summer demand period, maintaining stable electricity supplies nationwide through ongoing coordination with the Central Bank of Egypt, the Finance Ministry, the Electricity and Renewable Energy Ministry and other relevant authorities.
The minister further reviewed the outcome of his recent meetings with Egypt’s regional and international partners, noting progress in implementing gas field development projects in cooperation with major international energy companies and connecting them to Egypt’s infrastructure.
He said these projects will maximize the use of Egypt’s advanced gas infrastructure, strengthen its role as a regional energy trading hub, generate added economic value for participating countries, support regional energy security and provide additional gas supplies to European markets.

items.body_text:
Clashes in Ethiopia along borders with Sudan, Eritrea stoke worry of larger regional war          
        After four years of a contentious peace between the Ethiopian federal government and the Tigray People’s Liberation Front, fighting broke out between the two sides on Saturday.
The clashes spanned from the Humera border town with Sudan in the north to Shererina in the south and began around midnight, persisting through the afternoon of the next day, three residents in the area told Mada Masr.
The residents said they could hear the sound of mortar shelling and machine gun fire throughout the day, primarily around Shererina.
The clashes began when a force of Tigrayian fighters, who have been stationed in Sudan, crossed into Ethiopia near the village of Legudi outside Humera, according to an Ethiopian military source.
Residents of the border area told Mada Masr that the force, known as “Army 70,” displaced farmers and looted properties belonging to eight agricultural investors, forcing them to flee to urban centers.
The Tigrayan force was quickly engaged by the Ethiopian federal military and pushed back, according to the Ethiopian military source.
Shortly afterward, federal forces launched attacks on TPLF positions in Shererina using heavy artillery and drones, according to the group’s leadership, which described the assault as a direct violation of the Pretoria ceasefire agreement, the 2022 peace deal that ended the two-year civil war in Tigray.
The Ethiopian military has established new checkpoints at main access gates to Humera city, imposing strict security controls and movement restrictions, the Ethiopian military source said. All vehicular and pedestrian movement outside city limits has been prohibited, effectively barring farmers from accessing surrounding agricultural fields.
In southern Tigray, tensions also flared, as eyewitnesses told Mada Masr that a military build-up was visible.
Fearing a broader conflict, hundreds of civilians from surrounding areas fled on foot toward Raya Kobo, quickly overwhelming local hosting capacities and driving further displacement south toward Woldiya and Dessie, Gobeze Aragaw, a resident of Kobo, told Mada Masr.
The clashes are an ominous sign of escalation for a region that has been on the brink of war for months.
While tensions have been steadily escalating between Tigray and the federal government for at least a year following the collapse of the Tigray Interim Administration established under the 2022 agreement, the fighting has a wider resonance.
Ethiopia’s decision to allow the Rapid Support Forces to use its territory as a staging ground for fighting in Sudan’s Blue Nile coupled with its demands for Red Sea access via Eritrea, which has subsequently thrown its weight behind the TPLF, has internationalized the stakes of the Tigray tension. Egypt, adamant in denying Ethiopia Red Sea access, has grown closer to Eritrea, while the United Arab Emirates, a close backer of the RSF and the Ethiopian government, looms in the background.
For now, however, the conflict has largely remained localized.
The TPLF said on Saturday that its forces were acting “in defense of the region” after what it described as government attempts to impose new military realities on the ground. It accused Addis Ababa of failing to implement key provisions of the agreement, including the withdrawal of non-federal forces from Western Tigray and the restoration of civilian administration in the territory.
A former Ethiopian government official who served at the country’s embassy in Khartoum said the federal government holds the TPLF leadership entirely responsible for the collapse of the security arrangements, arguing that the group has spent recent months rebuilding its military structures outside the framework established by the Pretoria agreement.
The Ethiopian military operations are intended to “protect the constitutional order” and prevent the peace deal from collapsing, the former official said. The gove

Bakeries voice concerns that new direct debit system could disrupt subsidized bread production          
        A new direct debit system launched by the government at the start of August restructures its financial relationship with mills and bakeries — the supply chain that makes subsidized bread for around 64 million people.
The new system marks the first practical step toward overhauling the workings of Egypt’s largest subsidy program, sources in bakeries across the country told Mada Masr.
The government has said it plans to phase out in-kind bread subsidies, making bread just another option in a range of goods that subsidy program beneficiaries will be entitled to purchase through a monthly cash support program.
The transition has sparked concerns that some of Egypt’s most vulnerable will be left without government-guaranteed access to bread, leaving them exposed to high inflation.
Wheat and flour have always been supplied to mills and bakeries on consignment, with financial accounts settled later.
Under that system, bakeries received payments from the Supply Ministry to cover other production costs such as energy and labor through periodic settlements, without having to purchase flour themselves or provide cash to finance production.
Now, every stage of the bread-making process is set to operate on cash transactions instead. Mills must pay the General Authority for Supply Commodities for wheat up front before receiving it, and bakeries must, likewise, purchase flour from the mills.
The government will then reimburse bakeries only for the amount of bread distributed to subsidy beneficiaries, verifying how much bread they have supplied to consumers through their ration card point-of-sale machines.
Two sources in the General Bakeries Division of the Federation of Egyptian Chambers of Commerce told Mada Masr the shift to direct debit cannot be separated from the government’s broader plans to overhaul the subsidy system. The move to a financial cycle based entirely on digital payments and bank settlements will allow the state to monitor money and goods moving through the system more closely, they said — one of the key technical requirements for the planned transition to cash support.
The new step begins to shift government support away from the movement of wheat and flour themselves and toward the flow of money instead.
In doing so, it transfers part of the burden of financing daily operations from the state to bakeries, which must now ensure they have enough cash liquidity to pay for flour before recovering their dues from the government.
Supply Minister Sherif Farouk said in a TV interview on Wednesday that the changes will have no impact on citizens. He affirmed that subsidized bread will continue to be priced at 20 piasters per loaf, with each loaf weighing 90 grams, and each beneficiary will continue to be entitled to receive five loaves per day.
He said the new system is intended to strengthen oversight on the movement of wheat and flour, reduce waste and improve the efficiency of subsidy management without affecting beneficiaries’ entitlements.
But many people working in the subsidized bakeries sector said that the new system would turn their operations upside down, adding to already high costs that threaten the viability of their operations.
New cashflow requirements add to existing financial burden on bakeries
The new financial burden posed by the need for extra liquidity is added to rising costs that have already strained bakeries in recent months, bakery owners said to Mada Masr.
Days before the new system took effect, the General Bakeries Division called for their production subsidy to be raised by around 40 percent, arguing that current rates no longer reflect accumulated increases in labor costs, energy prices, operating expenses and administrative fees.

items.body_text:
Egyptian Drug Authority studies new flexible pricing system as pharmaceutical companies push for increases          
        A new formula that would allow more frequent medicine price fluctuations is under review by the Egyptian Drug Authority (EDA), according to four informed sources who spoke to Mada Masr.
An EDA official and the head of a pharmaceutical company who spoke to Mada Masr on condition of anonymity said the EDA, which is responsible for setting prices nationwide, is looking into the system against the backdrop of repeated disputes with pharmaceutical companies requesting price increases.
Drug prices have spiraled in recent years as the pound has weakened against the dollar and raw materials costs have increased accordingly.
Yassin Ragai, the assistant to the EDA’s head, told Mada Masr that the drug authority held meetings this month with various stakeholders in the pharmaceutical industry to discuss the new mechanism in light of various pressures on the drug market in recent years.
Ragai said the meetings came amid a desire to encourage further investments in the pharmaceutical sector “through a clear and transparent formula and a publicly announced, up-to-date mechanism.”
The last amendment to the pricing system took place in 2012, said Ragai. That mechanism, established by Health Ministerial Decree 499/2012, mandated that drug price reviews should take place based on fluctuations of 15 percent or more in the exchange rate. Companies were to be allowed to submit price increase changes when that threshold was met.
Prices on Egypt’s markets are now subject to much more frequent fluctuation than they were in 2012, however. The government has intervened since then to devalue the pound by 15 percent or more on several occasions and, in 2024, introduced a more flexible exchange rate, meaning the pound now fluctuates daily against the dollar, leaving Egyptians more exposed to inflation.
As a result, some medication prices have jumped by as much as 20-30 percent in recent years.
The head of the Pharmacists Syndicate’s pharmaceutical manufacturing committee, Mahfouz Ramzy, said to Mada Masr that the EDA is now studying ways to make drug pricing more flexible.
The new mechanism under review would tie prices to the pound’s exchange rate, as well as to inflation and interest rates, he said. This means prices would move more flexibly in line with these variables to reduce the back-and-forth between the drug authority and pharmaceutical companies.
The new mechanism would determine the share of the dollar-denominated component in each product, serving as a basis for price adjustment, according to Ramzy.
Price increases would therefore be proportional to fluctuations in the dollar exchange rate and to changing interest rates, as well as to any change in the price of raw materials.
The step would protect companies’ profit margins, allowing them to continue production, said Ramzy.
Ragai explained that the goal of the new mechanism is to ensure that pricing is fair and, at the same time, affordable for manufacturers.
He said the authority is still in dialogue with all stakeholders in the pharmaceutical industry — from manufacturers to pharmacists and distributors — to listen to their proposals before issuing a final decision in August. Ragai stressed that the mechanism will not affect any of the medications currently available on the market.
Ramzy confirmed that discussions are ongoing with the aim of landing upon the best formula, given that the decision will affect the entire drug market. He added that the proposal leans toward allowing prices to be adjusted but not by the same scale as the sharp increases seen in recent years.

items.body_text:
Egyptian Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly said on Monday that Chinese investments in Egypt exceeded $10bn, highlighting growing confidence among Chinese businesses in Egypt’s investment climate as the government reviewed new opportunities to deepen economic cooperation with Beijing.
Madbouly made the remarks while chairing the third meeting of the Ministerial Committee for the China Unit, attended by several ministers and senior government officials, to follow up on the implementation of the Egypt-China comprehensive strategic partnership and explore new areas of cooperation across key economic sectors.
The prime minister said the strategic relationship between Cairo and Beijing continues to deepen under the guidance of the leadership of both countries, building on the progress achieved in recent years to support Egypt’s development agenda and advance shared interests.
He reviewed the latest developments in bilateral cooperation and the progress of several joint projects, stressing the importance of continued coordination among government entities to ensure the effective implementation of the strategic partnership.
Madbouly said Chinese investments in Egypt have now surpassed $10bn, with a large number of Chinese companies operating across a broad range of sectors.
“The figure reflects the growing confidence of the Chinese business community in Egypt’s investment environment and the promising opportunities the country offers to investors,” he said.
According to Cabinet spokesperson Mohamed El-Homsany, the meeting reviewed a pipeline of joint projects and investment opportunities with Chinese partners across several priority sectors, underscoring the breadth of the economic partnership between the two countries.
The discussions covered cooperation in industrial development, seawater desalination, localisation of advanced technologies, telecommunications, transport, mining, clean energy, specialised chemical industries, engineering industries, agriculture, and expanding exports of Egyptian agricultural products.
The proposed projects are expected to support Egypt’s sustainable development agenda by facilitating technology transfer, attracting additional Chinese investment, boosting local manufacturing, and further expanding economic cooperation between the two countries.
Participating ministers also reviewed progress on ongoing Egypt-China projects and discussed additional opportunities to strengthen collaboration across a wide range of strategic sectors, reaffirming both countries’ commitment to deepening their long-standing economic partnership.

items.body_text:
Egypt’s banking sector recorded a sharp increase in net foreign assets (NFA) in June 2026, with the balance rising to $27.965bn, equivalent to EGP 1.378trn, up from $22.9bn, or EGP 1.198trn, in May, according to data released by the Central Bank of Egypt (CBE).
The increase came as the Egyptian pound strengthened against the US dollar, with the exchange rate improving from EGP 52.3297 per dollar in May to EGP 49.2763 in June.
According to the CBE, the banking sector’s total foreign assets—including those of the Central Bank and commercial banks—stood at the equivalent of EGP 4.939trn in June, compared with EGP 4.989trn in May.
Meanwhile, total foreign liabilities fell to the equivalent of EGP 3.591trn, down from EGP 3.790trn a month earlier, contributing to the improvement in the sector’s net foreign asset position.
Net foreign assets are widely regarded as one of the key indicators of the strength and resilience of the banking sector. They represent the difference between the banking system’s total foreign assets and foreign currency liabilities, providing an indication of its capacity to meet external obligations and support stability in the foreign exchange market.
Foreign assets held by the banking sector include foreign currency deposits and savings, gold holdings, foreign securities, and Special Drawing Rights (SDRs), while foreign liabilities comprise repayable external debt, deposits belonging to foreign entities, and import-related obligations.

items.title: Syria Interior Ministry Moves to Release Ain Mneen Detainees Amid Protests, Shop Closures and Municipal Resignations
items.summary: Syrian authorities said Sunday that legal procedures are underway to release individuals detained during recent unrest in the town of Ain Mneen, as residents staged peaceful demonstrations, shuttered shops and local officials resigned in protest over the arrests. The post Syria Interior Ministry Moves to Release Ain Mneen Detainees Amid Protests, Shop Closures and Municipal Resignations first appeared on The Syrian Observer.
items.body_text:
Syrian authorities said Sunday that legal procedures are underway to release individuals detained during recent unrest in the town of Ain Mneen, as residents staged peaceful demonstrations, shuttered shops and local officials resigned in protest over the arrests.
Protests, Detentions and a Full Municipal Resignation
Tensions rose sharply in Ain Mneen on Sunday as residents held a peaceful sit-in and observed a broad commercial closure. According to local sources and reporting by Enab Baladi, demonstrators demanded the release of all detainees arrested during Friday’s confrontation — including university students, elderly residents, shop owners and local workers — and called for accountability for security personnel accused of assaulting civilians.
In a video circulated online, the town’s mayor announced his resignation, along with the entire municipal council, before a reconciliation committee.
“Residents stand with the state, not against it; they are simply demanding their rights,” he said, adding that municipal leaders would refuse any negotiations until all detainees are freed and those responsible for the assaults are held accountable.
By Sunday afternoon, calm had reportedly returned to Ain Mneen, with discussions underway over possible negotiated solutions.
Interior Ministry Addresses the Arrests
The Rural Damascus Internal Security Command said in a statement carried by state media that the Ministry of Interior recognises the constitutional right to peaceful assembly. Officials said the initial gathering in Ain Mneen two days earlier lacked legal authorization and involved physical attacks on security personnel.
Authorities stressed that arrests were limited to individuals accused of rioting and disturbing public order, and insisted that peaceful demonstrators were not targeted. They added that legal procedures are being finalised to release the detainees once standard undertakings are completed.
Water Dispute Sparked the Confrontation
The unrest began Friday, July 31, when heavy machinery belonging to the regional water authority arrived in the Ba’arjal area near Ain Mneen. Residents attempted to block the equipment, fearing that new drilling operations would drain the local groundwater basin. The confrontation escalated quickly, resulting in injuries and multiple arrests.
The Rural Damascus Media Directorate rejected claims that a new well was being drilled, saying the machinery was deployed solely to conduct maintenance on an existing well to improve drinking-water access. Officials added that community representatives had been briefed on the project beforehand.
Officials Reject Reports of Damascus Market Strike
Separately, Syrian officials denied widespread social-media reports claiming that major commercial markets in central Damascus — including Al-Hamidiyah, Al-Hariqa and Midhat Pasha — had launched a solidarity strike with Ain Mneen.
The head of the Al-Hamidiyah Commercial Market Committee told Syria TV that no general strike had taken place. He said a small number of shop owners briefly closed their stores to attend a solidarity gathering, while images circulating online of shuttered storefronts were taken early in the morning before businesses opened, creating a misleading impression of widespread closures.

items.title: As Bank Financing Knocks on Syria’s Door, Who Guarantees the Funds—and Who Ultimately Pays the Debt?
items.summary: World Bank documentation on Syria’s electricity sector stresses that investment sustainability depends on revenue protection and full cost recovery. The post As Bank Financing Knocks on Syria’s Door, Who Guarantees the Funds—and Who Ultimately Pays the Debt? first appeared on The Syrian Observer.
items.body_text:
Syria’s reconstruction file is entering a markedly more serious financial phase. J.P. Morgan has joined Qatar National Bank (QNB) and Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank to arrange a loan approaching $7 billion for projects undertaken by Qatar’s Power International Holding in the energy and airport sectors. It is one of the largest foreign financing commitments linked to Syria since the fall of Bashar al-Assad’s regime.
The participation of a major American institution such as J.P. Morgan carries significance that goes well beyond the loan’s headline value. Operating within a compliance environment acutely sensitive to sanctions, transfer risks and counterparty exposure, the bank’s involvement suggests that the deal’s structure has reached a level that can be scrutinized, syndicated and marketed within the international loan market—even if final execution still depends on closing terms and settlement procedures.
The transaction consists of a five-year debt facility arranged for the Qatari conglomerate, whose construction arm, UCC Holding, has secured extensive contracts across Syria. According to published details, the loan proceeds are allocated to power-sector infrastructure and the redevelopment of a major airport.
Reconstruction in Syria: Between Production and Guarantees
Economist Mahmoud Arbash, who specializes in infrastructure and development, told Syria TV that the economic impact of this financing will depend heavily on whether the projects succeed in creating a domestic productive network—local suppliers, engineering services, logistics chains and vocational training. If spending remains concentrated in foreign contractors and imported materials, he said, the broader economic spillover will be limited and fall short of the loan’s nominal value.
Arbash emphasized that sectoral prioritization will determine the long-term developmental value of these initiatives. Manufacturing, agriculture and services all require a reliable power grid and efficient logistical connections to reduce production costs. Executing mega-projects without coordination across sectors risks producing high-cost assets that operate below their economic potential.
He also noted that the Syrian government must carefully assess indirect liabilities arising from power-purchase agreements, off-take guarantees and delay-compensation clauses. These contractual obligations could evolve into fiscal burdens on public finances if not managed prudently.
Ultimately, Arbash argued, the success of the financing package will be measured by its ability to raise overall economic productivity and expand the tax base over the lifespan of the assets. Only then can maintenance and upgrades be funded through domestic revenues rather than leaving new infrastructure permanently dependent on external capital.
Meanwhile, the financial structure rests on a guarantee provided by Qatar National Bank—a central credit-enhancement mechanism that strengthens the deal’s bankability. By shifting primary credit risk to a solvent international institution, the structure shields lenders from direct exposure to Syrian project risks.
This approach aligns with standard project-finance principles that link bankability to the strength of guarantees, predictable cash flows and enforceable contractual rights. As a result, the creditworthiness of major Syrian infrastructure ventures remains tied to the sponsor’s balance sheet, the guarantor’s standing and the clarity of expected revenue streams.
Execution Will Set the Terms for Future Financing
World Bank documentation on Syria’s electricity sector stresses that investment sustainability depends on revenue protection and full cost recovery. Lenders will scrutinize power-purchase contracts, tariff structures, settlement currencies and collection mechanisms as part of their cash-flow analysis.
These parameters are especially critical for the power sector, which requires stable, long-term cash flows to cover operations, maintenance and debt service. In May

Syrian President Ahmad al-Sharaa held a phone call Saturday with Saudi Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman, reaffirming Syria’s support for the Kingdom’s security amid heightened regional tensions.
Syria Condemns Attempted Attack on Saudi Oil Facilities
According to a statement issued by the Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs, al-Sharaa began the call by renewing Syria’s condemnation of an attempted strike on Saudi oil facilities attributed to Iranian-backed militias operating in Iraq.
The ministry said al-Sharaa underscored Damascus’s “firm position” in supporting the Kingdom’s security, stability and national sovereignty.
Talks Focus on Cooperation and Regional Stability
The two leaders reviewed bilateral relations and discussed expanding cooperation across multiple sectors, according to official readouts. They also exchanged views on regional and international developments, highlighting ongoing diplomatic efforts aimed at reducing tensions and reinforcing stability across the Middle East.
Saturday’s call followed a series of high-level contacts by al-Sharaa earlier in the week. On Thursday, he held coordinated outreach with both UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman to address emerging regional security concerns.

The Syzran oil refinery in Russia's Samara Oblast is on fire following a drone attack on 4 August, according to Russian and Ukrainian monitoring channels.

Astra later analysed the available images and confirmed that the burning facility was the Syzran oil refinery. It said the fire had broken out as a result of a drone strike.
Background:
- On the night of 3-4 August, drone attacks also sparked fires at warehouse facilities belonging to Russian online retailer Wildberries in Russia's Leningrad and Moscow oblasts.

- The refinery was also targeted by drones on 18 April and 21 May.
- The Syzran refinery produces approximately 800,000 tonnes of petrol and 1.5 million tonnes of diesel fuel annually.

items.title: 25-year-old Ukrainian paramedic Eva Reuter killed in Russian double-tap strike on Kyiv
items.summary: Eva "Planochka" Reuter, a 25-year-old artist and paramedic, has been killed in Kyiv in a Russian double-tap strike on the night of 31 July-1 August. She was helping those injured during the attack.
items.body_text:
25-year-old Ukrainian paramedic Eva Reuter killed in Russian double-tap strike on Kyiv
Eva "Planochka" Reuter, a 25-year-old artist and paramedic, has been killed in Kyiv in a Russian double-tap strike on the night of 31 July-1 August. She was helping those injured during the attack.
Source: Yana Zinkevych, founder and head of the Hospitallers medical battalion
Details: Zinkevych said that Eva Reuter was an artist and art historian who worked in the games industry (game development and production). She held a bachelor's degree from the National Academy of Fine Arts and Architecture.
"She joined us in November 2022. Having every right to remain in the rear, she chose to save the lives of others. Eva was tireless: she evacuated the wounded, took care of Medical Forces supplies and took part in the 'Veterans are different. Victory is one' campaign, reminding people of respect and equality.
Eva was an extraordinarily driven, decisive and courageous young woman. Recently she had been on duty with rescue workers in Kyiv, ran towards fire to help others, and met her death as a hero," Zinkevych wrote.
Social media user Oksana Hel described the young woman as "one who always put others first".
"There are acts for which no words are sufficient. There are people who become a light in the darkest of times. And there is a choice – conscious, terrifying, yet great: to give one's own life so that someone else may have a chance. She made exactly that choice," the woman wrote.
A 20-year-old volunteer Vitalina Yarovenko was in the vehicle with Eva. She was also killed.
"Two stories that should have continued – but didn't get the chance…. They say heroes are those who do not think of themselves in a moment of danger. That is true. But they are also those with a great heart every single day, not just in their final moment…," Hel wrote.
She added that the paramedic had a great love of animals. "She had eleven cats at home – rescued, kept warm, welcomed into her small universe of care. She knew how to protect life. Even the smallest," the woman wrote.
Background: The strike on Kyiv on the night of 31 July-1 August claimed the lives of nine people. Among them was 22-year-old patrol officer Yehor Terekhiv, who was helping civilians at the scene of the attack.

items.title: Ukraine probes sabotage and safety breach in Khmelnytskyi ammunition depot explosions, body parts found
items.summary: The State Bureau of Investigation is examining two possible causes of the ammunition explosions at a military training ground in Khmelnytskyi: violations of ammunition handling procedures and sabotage. Human body parts have been discovered during the search operations.
items.body_text:
Ukraine probes sabotage and safety breach in Khmelnytskyi ammunition depot explosions, body parts found
The State Bureau of Investigation is examining two possible causes of the ammunition explosions at a military training ground in Khmelnytskyi: violations of ammunition handling procedures and sabotage. Human body parts have been discovered during the search operations.
Source: State Bureau of Investigation
Details: The State Bureau of Investigation said the uncontrolled detonation of ammunition began at around 11:55 on 31 July at a military facility on the outskirts of Khmelnytskyi and continued almost until the end of the day.
Quote: "The lives of Ukrainian service members are of the utmost value. The State Bureau of Investigation will establish all the circumstances of this tragedy and provide a legal assessment of the actions of everyone whose decisions, actions, or inaction may have led to these grave consequences."
Details: As of 3 August, five service members remain missing. Early reports indicate that they were unloading ammunition at a military warehouse when the initial explosion occurred.
During search operations, investigators recovered human remains. These have been sent for forensic pathology examination and DNA analysis to identify the victims.
The State Bureau of Investigation also reported that eight service members were injured in the explosions.
One line of inquiry is that breaches of regulations during the transport or unloading of ammunition may have triggered the initial blast, which subsequently caused the chain of detonations. Investigators are also examining the possibility of sabotage aimed at destroying military equipment and ammunition.
Background:
- On 31 July, an emergency occurred at the training ground of a military unit in Khmelnytskyi Oblast, where an explosion followed by a series of ammunition detonations took place, according to Ukraine's Special Operations Forces.
- Local authorities said the blasts damaged a number of residential buildings and municipal facilities.
- The State Bureau of Investigation launched a criminal investigation into the incident, while the Office of the Prosecutor General confirmed that four service members had initially been reported injured.
- The Special Operations Forces later announced that the ammunition detonations at the training ground had ceased, but five Special Operations Forces service members remained unaccounted for.

items.title: Russians seek to capture Lyman as springboard for offensive on Sloviansk and Kramatorsk — Trehubov
items.summary: Russian forces are attempting to seize control of Lyman in order to use the city as a base for a further offensive toward the Sloviansk–Kramatorsk urban area.
items.body_text:
Russians seek to capture Lyman as springboard for offensive on Sloviansk and Kramatorsk — Trehubov
This was stated on television by Viktor Trehubov, spokesperson for the Joint Forces Task Force, according to Ukrinform.
"The Russians want to enter Lyman and establish a foothold there. Their goal is to take direct control of the town itself, not just the surrounding area, and use it as a base for further offensive operations southward toward the Sloviansk–Kramatorsk agglomeration. Even a look at the map makes it clear that this is a necessity for them," Trehubov said.
He noted that in recent months Russian forces have been looking for alternative routes that would bypass the need to control Lyman, for example by advancing through Rai-Oleksandrivka. However, he emphasized that without control of Lyman, any attempt to enter Sloviansk would be highly risky and logistically difficult, which is why Russian forces are determined to capture the city.
At the same time, Trehubov stressed that despite these efforts, Russian troops have so far been unable to establish themselves inside the town, although they have reportedly reached its eastern outskirts.
Regarding the situation in Kupiansk, Trehubov said conditions remain difficult. Russian forces are attempting to advance on the city from the north through the village of Holubivka. Ukrainian troops are conducting operations to push Russian forces out of the city's northern outskirts.
He also added that east of the Oskil River, Russian troops continue to apply pressure along the entire line of the Ukrainian bridgehead. The most active attempts to break through are occurring in the central sector, advancing from Pishchane toward Kucherivka and other eastern settlements. The ultimate objective of these attacks is to reach Kupiansk-Vuzlovyi from the east.
Trehubov also highlighted developments in drone warfare. According to him, over the past year Ukrainian drone units have significantly expanded their capabilities, gradually shifting the balance of power in Ukraine's favor.
"The Russians still retain certain advantages, but there are also areas where they face serious problems, which they themselves acknowledge, for example, with heavy multicopter drones, which they have failed to deploy effectively. Overall, the situation is becoming more favorable for Ukraine thanks to the quantitative and qualitative growth of Ukrainian drones and drone operators. There are more of them, they are being used more effectively, and the organization of their coordination has become much better than that of the Russians," the spokesperson said.
According to Ukrinform, 226 combat engagements between Ukraine's Defense Forces and Russian invading forces were recorded along the front line over the past 24 hours.
Photo: AFU General Staff

items.title: Russia May Target Water Supply This Winter, Kyiv Warns
items.summary: Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal said Russia’s next winter campaign may focus on Ukraine’s water infrastructure after devastating attacks on the power grid. He said Kyiv is strengthening critical infrastructure while seeking additional Patriot missiles and financial support from allies.
items.body_text:
Russia could shift its winter campaign from attacking Ukraine’s power grid to targeting water infrastructure, Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal warned, saying civilians would struggle to survive prolonged disruptions to water and sewage services.
Speaking to Politico in an interview published on Tuesday, Shmyhal said Moscow’s strategy is aimed at breaking Ukraine’s resilience by crippling critical infrastructure.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
“Russia’s goal now is to destroy our water supplies,” Shmyhal said. “Last winter they targeted electricity and heating, but you could still survive if you had gas and water during electricity shutdowns.”
“It is difficult to survive for more than three days without water and sewage,” he added.
Ukraine preparing for another winter campaign
Shmyhal said Ukraine hopes its long-range strikes against Russian oil refineries and tougher Western sanctions will pressure Moscow into ending the war this autumn. However, he warned Kyiv is preparing for another winter of large-scale attacks on critical infrastructure if the fighting continues.
According to the minister, Ukraine is constructing protective shelters for electricity, water, and gas facilities while expanding the use of modular boilers and power generators that are harder for Russia to destroy than large centralized plants.
“Ukraine has acquired the ability to adapt very quickly to crises, to challenges,” Shmyhal said.
More Patriot missiles needed
The minister also stressed that Ukraine urgently needs additional PAC-3 interceptor missiles for Patriot air defense systems to defend against Russian ballistic missile attacks.
Kyiv Under Air Raid Alert as Russian Drones Threaten Capital, Regions
President Volodymyr Zelensky has previously said Ukraine aims to secure around 300 Patriot interceptors, while Kyiv and its allies continue urging countries including Spain and Greece to provide additional missiles.
Shmyhal also called for more international financial support, saying Ukraine needs another €500 million ($575 million) before winter to strengthen energy resilience and €400 million ($460 million) to help state energy company Naftogaz recover from Russian strikes.
Energy system remains under pressure
According to Shmyhal, Russia has damaged or destroyed more than 80% of Ukraine’s electricity generation capacity since launching its full-scale invasion.
Ukraine generated 54.5 gigawatts of electricity before 2014, but available capacity has fallen sharply following the occupation of Crimea, the seizure of the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant, and repeated Russian missile and drone attacks on energy infrastructure.
Despite the damage, Shmyhal expressed confidence Ukraine would withstand another winter if additional military and financial assistance arrives in time.
“He will bleed, but he will drag us into the winter,” Shmyhal said, referring to Russian President Vladimir Putin. “This is a pessimistic scenario, but my optimism is that we will survive this winter; we are ready for it.”

items.title: Ceuta Between a Migration Crisis and a Hybrid Attack: Giorgia Meloni’s Policy and Europe’s Security
items.summary: The European Democrats’ attack on Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni is politically dishonest and shows that part of Europe’s center still does not understand the world in which it lives.
items.body_text:
As the dead were being counted in Ceuta, as police and troops struggled to regain control of the city, and as residents watched tens of thousands of people cross the European Union’s border within hours, the European Democrats chose to discuss Giorgia Meloni’s clothes. On their social media account, they posted an image of the Italian Prime Minister wearing an EU scarf in 2023 and a red Donald Trump cap in 2026, accusing her of having once demanded European solidarity and now choosing propaganda instead. The party, which belongs to the centrist Renew Europe family, concluded that Meloni stages strength while governing by opinion polls.
It is difficult to imagine a more superficial response to what happened.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
Between 50,000 and 60,000 people attempted to enter Ceuta from Morocco by land and sea. In less than two days, a mass of people large enough to fill a medium-sized city crossed the border. At least 72 people lost their lives, more than a thousand required medical treatment, and the Spanish authorities had to deploy additional police and military forces. More than 48,000 people were returned only after the border had collapsed. Spain then installed a 500-meter floating barrier along part of the maritime frontier.
To describe this as an ordinary migration crisis is to refuse to confront the scale of the event. Europe faced a sudden breach of its external border by tens of thousands of people, deaths, mass panic, the temporary loss of territorial control and the mobilization of security forces on an emergency footing. In the consequences it produced, the event in Ceuta was comparable to a major terrorist attack.
The War Is Coming Home to Russians
Among those involved in the mass crossing were people who were desperate, deceived, exploited and placed in mortal danger. The circumstances of those people belong to one question; the nature of the operation to another. A person can be a victim of smugglers, disinformation or political manipulation while being used as part of an attack against another state.
A border is where a state distinguishes a genuine claim to asylum from the abuse of asylum, legal entry from smuggling, and a person in need of protection from someone who presents a security risk. When tens of thousands breach a border at once, that capacity disappears. Everyone becomes part of the same mass, without identity, screening or established intent. Giorgia Meloni’s policy restores the state’s ability to draw those distinctions. It protects both the citizens of Italy and those who are genuinely entitled to protection.
A formal designation of terrorism requires evidence of intent and of an organizer. No such evidence has yet been made public. A security assessment, however, cannot wait for years while every investigation runs its course. European law treats as terrorist acts conduct intended to seriously intimidate a population, compel a government to act or refrain from acting, or gravely destabilize political, economic or social structures. In its effect, Ceuta generated precisely that kind of pressure.
Migration as weapon
Hybrid attack is the more precise term. The European Union has warned for years that migration can be weaponized. The European External Action Service explicitly includes the instrumentalization of migration among hybrid threats. In 2021, the European Commission described the state-directed movement of migrants towards a border as a particularly cruel form of hybrid threat, intended to destabilize the Union, create a prolonged crisis and test its resolve. NATO likewise lists the instrumentalization of irregular migration among the tools of hybrid action.
The decisive questions in Ceuta are: Who enabled tens of thousands of people to gather in almost the same place at almost the same moment? Who spread claims that the crossing would be easy? Who organized the movement? Why were Moroccan forces passive in the opening phase?
