items.title: Wrongfully imprisoned Jens Ihle and Anneli Auer seek millions in compensation
items.summary: Jens Ihle's claim is believed to be the largest ever filed in Finland for wrongful imprisonment, exceeding even the compensation sought by his ex-partner, Anneli Auer.
items.body_text:
Jens Ihle (formerly Jens Kukka) is seeking more than two million euros in compensation from the state treasury after spending years in prison for crimes he did not commit.
If granted, the claim would amount to the largest compensation ever awarded in Finland for wrongful imprisonment.
Ihle is seeking just over two million euros in damages for emotional suffering, along with roughly 26,000 euros to cover other costs.
Jens Ihle and his former partner, Anneli Auer, spent years in prison before the charges against them were dismissed by a court in April.
The pair were long suspected of serious crimes, sparking a series of high-profile investigations, trials, and appeals that began about two decades ago.
Ihle was held in custody from September 2011 until April 2016. He then spent about four months in supervised probationary release before being granted parole.
Southwest Finland District Court acquitted Auer and Ihle of all the sexual offence charges. The prosecutor general did not appeal the acquittals, making the ruling final.
Auer is also seeking compensation. She is claiming a total of 1.3 million euros for the nearly four years she was deprived of her liberty.
Long-running cases
Anneli Auer first came to the attention of the Finnish public when she was named as a suspect in the murder of her husband, psychologist Jukka S. Lahti, who died in December 2006 at the family home in Ulvila, a small village on the outskirts of the city of Pori.
She was twice convicted, and then acquitted, of killing her husband in a case that became known as the Ulvila homicide.
Auer was twice convicted by a district court of her husband's murder, but both verdicts were overturned on appeal. The killer was never found.
While Auer was in custody, her children were placed with a foster family, where they began making allegations of sexual abuse. That set off another legal process, in which Auer and her former partner were handed lengthy prison sentences.

items.title: Military restricts air and maritime traffic in Gulf of Finland
items.summary: The Finnish Defence Forces says the restrictions were put in place as a precaution to protect civilians in the event of a drone interception.
items.body_text:
The Finnish Defence Forces (FDF) said early on Tuesday that they had temporarily restricted air and maritime traffic in the eastern Gulf of Finland. The restrictions were lifted at 7.13am.
According to the FDF, the measures were precautionary, intended to safeguard civilians if drones needed to be intercepted. No drones ultimately entered Finnish airspace or territory.
The airspace restrictions came into force at 5.26am, followed by restrictions on maritime traffic at 5.40am.
Air and maritime traffic has been restricted several times in recent weeks in the eastern Gulf of Finland. The measures have been linked to Ukrainian drone attacks targeting Russia.
Among other outlets, the Kyiv Independent reported that Ukrainian drones had struck targets in the St Petersburg region.
Yle News' All Points North podcast has explored drone threats over Finland and the country's civil preparedness.

items.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Tuesday
items.summary: Swedish migration minister blames Spain's migration policies for Ceuta crisis, Foxtrot leader sentenced to prison in Iraq, and other news from Sweden on Tuesday.
items.body_text:
Sweden blames Spain's lax migration policies for Ceuta crisis
Swedish Migration Minister Johan Forssell has called on Spain's government to "take back control" and learn from Sweden, after over 60,000 migrants passed over the border to its North African enclave of Ceuta last week.
"We warned of the risks of that. When you have large amnesties for people who have no right of asylum, that creates incentives for people who have no right of asylum to come to Europe," he said.
He compared the situation to that which Sweden faced in 2014 and 2015 when around 244,000 people applied for asylum in Sweden.
"Sweden had similar policies previously, ten years ago when 250,000 people came in two years. We have learned the lessons from that. That's why we've remade our policies. But Spain has gone in the other direction, and yes, many of us warned that this could have consequences – which it has as well."
Swedish vocabulary: att varna – to warn
Ultraswimmer swims from Kåseberga in Skåne to Poland
The Polish ultraswimmer Bartlomiej Kubkowski arrived in the Polish town of Dziwnów on Sunday after swimming a gruelling 160km stretch of the Baltic from Kåseberga in Skåne.
The swimmer was affected by hallucinations along the route, high waves, cold and wind. While he had support boats which provided him with drinks and food, he was not permitted to hold on to it or even touch the support boat.
Swedish vocabulary: att röra – to touch
Foxtrot leader sentenced to prison in Iraq
One of the leaders of the Foxtrot gang, who is suspected of ordering a shooting in Gävle, has been sentenced to life imprisonment in Iraq, where he has been held awaiting trial since December for drug trafficking.
Swedish police have submitted an extradition request for the man, who is described as an ally of Foxtrot leader Rawa Majid.
Six people, all young and some under 18 years old, were shot when a 13-year-old boy opened fire at Södra Kungsgatan in Gävle on the night of October 4th last year.
Swedish vocabulary: narkotikahandel – drug trafficking
Swedish PM and opposition leader launch tours as election campaign kicks off
Sweden's prime minister and opposition leader both launched bus tours on Monday, as the campaign for the election on September 13th kicked off after the summer holiday.
"Now we are going into the second half," said Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson, who leads the Moderate Party, as he got on the party's bus outside its Stockholm headquarters, expressing confidence that his party and its allies can erase the lead the opposition has enjoyed since the 2022 election.
When voters understand that the left-wing bloc would return Sweden to an old politics of higher taxes, outdated security policy and softer policies on crime and immigration, he argued, their lead would evaporate.
Social Democrat leader Magdalena Andersson said that voters did not seem too impressed by the new coalition on the right, which would bring the far-right Sweden Democrats into government.
Kristersson presented the drastic reduction on fatal shootings in Sweden as one of his government's key successes, pointing out in Eskilstuna that there had been 23 shootings in 2022 and only two so far in 2026.
Andersson, who launched a new slogan, Det är dags att ta Sverige på allvar, "It's time to take Sweden seriously", said she would focus on three main principles, making Sweden safer, richer and more cohesive.
Swedish vocabulary: andra halflek – the second half game

items.title: Swedish word of the day: paxa
items.summary: Here's a word you may not learn in Swedish class but which may come in useful whether you're spending time with children or searching for a spot to have fika.
items.body_text:
Paxa means "to reserve", but only in certain contexts.
If you're talking about reserving a hotel room, a table at a restaurant, or a seat on a train, you'd use the verb reservera – simple enough to remember, since it's close to the English. You can think of these as "formal" reservations: you'll often get a written confirmation. Another alternative is boka (to book), as in kan jag boka ett bord? (Can I book a table?).
By contrast, paxa is used to describe "informal" reservations.
If for example, you put your coat or bag down on a seat while you queue for food, to save yourself that spot, you've paxat that seat. Whether or not this is bad etiquette is a bit of a contentious question, but you should definitely avoid it in popular eateries, where you'll sometimes see signs warning paxa ej platser (no saving seats!).
English equivalents, depending on which national and regional dialect you speak, could be "to call shotgun" (although this is very specific, referring to sitting in the front passenger seat of a car), "to call dibs" or "to bagsy". Swedish uses paxa to cover most of the same contexts.
So, how do you paxa?
Simply shout pax för X and all decent people will understand that the spot is yours. You've paxat it. Note that this is an informal, colloquial term, so you wouldn't want to walk into a work meeting and shout pax för stolen vid fönstret (I call dibs on the chair by the window). But if your office has a relaxed working culture, you may well hear phrases such as jag har paxat hans kontor (I've called dibs on his office).
- Don’t miss any of our Swedish words and expressions of the day by downloading The Local's app (available on Apple and Android) and then selecting the Swedish Word of the Day in your Notification options via the User button
Children often use it while playing: pax för cykeln! (I call dibs on the bike!), pax för framsätet! (I call shotgun!). In other games, they'll also use it to choose which character they will play: pax för att vara Pippi (dibs on being Pippi). You can use pax with the verbs få or ha, but can also use the verb paxa on its own, for example jag fick pax på cykeln or jag har paxat cykeln (I called dibs on the bike).
It's not entirely clear where this word comes from (if you have a theory, please let us know!), but in Swedish pax and pass are both used to describe a "safe" space in children's games, where a player can't be caught. The English equivalent might be "den", "base", or "dell", but it varies a lot depending on the region. In Swedish you could say detta området är pass/pax (this area is safe). This probably comes from the Latin word pax meaning "peace", and it's likely that the phrase pax för in the sense of "dibs" and the verb paxa come from the meaning of "safe space".
Example sentences:
Men jag hade ju paxat!
But I called dibs!
Den platsen är paxad.
This seat is saved.

items.title: Why do Swedes use week numbers instead of dates?
items.summary: Having to regularly check which date is meant when a Swede gives you a week number can be frustrating, but there’s a method in this numerical merry-go-round.
items.body_text:
“We are closed because the team is on annual leave in week 23.”
“We’ve scheduled the meeting for week 42 as the project should be near completion by then.”
“We should be able to begin construction in week 23.”
If you’ve ever read (or heard) a sentence like any of the above in Sweden and found yourself cursing in frustration and clutching your phone while you google “what date is week 23?”, you are not alone.
The use of week numbers to refer to points in time – either in the past or future, but usually within the current year or beginning of the next one – is common in some European countries, and Sweden has embraced it since it was introduced in the 1970s.
Sweden isn’t alone in this practice and its Scandinavian neighbours Denmark and Norway also use numbered weeks to refer to dates.
In Anglophone countries, including the United Kingdom and United States, the convention is not used, and weeks are more likely to be referred to loosely as the “second week in July”. If a specific week needs to be given, it might be written down as a range of dates or something like “the week commencing Monday, July 20th”.
As such, the use of week numbers can be very jarring to people not used to them because they are difficult to connect to an actual date and therefore don’t seem to give any kind of useful reference point. They require the extra step of referring to a calendar to look up a date which could have just been given in the first place.
At the same time, Swedes often seem to instinctively be aware of the week number they’re currently in, the exact date of an earlier week number, and how far into the future a given week number might be.
Below, we look at why week numbers are commonly used in Sweden and where the tradition comes from.
How does it work?
Sweden's calendar system designates “week 1” as the first week of the year, which includes four or more days of the new year (in other words, four January days with no more than three still in December).
Another way of putting this is: the first week in which Thursday is in January is week 1.
This means that the number of weeks in a year can vary, because 52 multiplied by 7 is 364. As such, week 53 sometimes makes an appearance at the tail end of the Swedish calendar.
It follows that week 1 can start in the old year and week 53 can include days in January. It’s probably a good thing that most people are still on their Christmas holidays at this time of the year.
Why does Sweden use this system?
Sweden introduced the numbering system for weeks on January 1st, 1973 (a Monday), in accordance with an international standard, ISO 2811 (which was in 1999 replaced by ISO 8601). The country began considering Monday, rather than Sunday, as the first day of the week at this point.
This was also, incidentally, when Sweden started structuring dates with year, followed by month, followed by day number: 2026-08-03, becoming one of the few counties to adopt the new international standard.
Numbered weeks were used in Sweden before this. Then, however, weeks would begin on Sunday, and the last day of the week would be Saturday.
Some countries – like the United States – still designate Sunday as the first day of the week in calendars.
With workplaces using them, the people working there need to keep track of them, and this means they’re more likely to be able to recall which week number they’re in than someone from a country where these are not used.
The result of more than 50 years of thinking about dates in this way? It’s easier to answer quickly when the receptionist at your GP asks if you can come for your next follow-up check in “week 43”.
How can I stop being frustrated by it?
I don’t have all the answers to this, but one way of making it easier to look up week numbers is to change the settings on your phone calendar to display them.

items.title: Where extreme weather is expected in Germany this week
items.summary: Large parts of Germany were still in the grips of a heatwave on Tuesday, with high temperatures of up to 38C as well as severe storms scattered in the northeast and later in the southwest.
items.body_text:
Germany was facing another extremely hot day on Tuesday, with temperatures between 30 and 38C in most parts of the country.
At the same time, scattered thunderstorms were expected, bringing heavy rain, hail and gale force winds in places.
It's a good day to close all the windows, and shutters and curtains, early on and do what you can to keep the heat out as temperatures rise throughout the day. In places where the weather is fair enough, you may also consider a trip to the local pool or lake for the afternoon to early evening hours.
Here's where the hottest temperatures are expected.
Heat & extreme weather warnings in place
The German Weather Service (DWD) had heat warnings in place over almost all of Germany on Tuesday.
You can see the DWD's heat warning map, updated as of about 10 am, below.
In central and southern parts of the country, an 'extreme' heat warning (shown in dark purple) was in effect on Tuesday. Affected cities include Frankfurt, Stuttgart, Erfurt and Nuremberg, where temperatures look set to get close to 38C by early evening.
Most of the rest of Germany, including the southern region around Munich as well as a large part of the north, even extending as far as Bremen, Hamburg and Schwerin, had a standard heat warning in place.
Heat warnings are issued when heat stress is expected among local populations. The DWD tends to issue heat warnings when daily temperatures will exceed 32C, and extreme heat warnings from 38C.
In addition to heat warnings, level two severe weather warnings were also in place in parts of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and in Brandenburg (just south of Potsdam), Saxony-Anhalt (south of Magdeburg) and Saxony (just north of Dresden).
Starting in these areas, the DWD expects thunderstorms with heavy rain, strong winds and hail. In the afternoon, thunderstorm activity will temporarily subside, with mostly sunny skies or scattered cumulus clouds.
Later, toward Tuesday evening, the storm regions will shift, and storms will then be more prevalent in the western half of the country, especially around the Black Forest.
The only parts of the country where no type of extreme weather was expected on Tuesday were some places the Baltic coast, such as around Kiel or Rügen. Here temperatures will range from 25 to 30C.
Wednesday, Thursday and Friday
Overnight into Wednesday, more showers and thunderstorms can be expected. In the second half of the night, showers and thunderstorms will gradually subside as the system moves off toward the northeast. Night-time low temperatures are expected to range between 16 and 22C across the country.
Wednesday's forecast looks similar, if a bit milder overall. The DWD expects partly cloudy skies, with heavy showers and thunderstorms in places, especially in the southeast and east.
High temperatures up to 35C will cover most of the southeast and eastern regions, whereas highs will top out around 25C near the North Sea.
Overnight into Thursday, skies will remain partly cloudy, with isolated showers and thunderstorms still possible.
On Thursday, it will be cloudy in the southeast with showers or heavy thunderstorms. Elsewhere, it will be partly cloudy with extended sunny periods and mostly dry.
Thursday is expected to bring the end of heat warnings, with highs between 26 and 32C, and up to around 24C in the northwest.
From Friday and through the weekend, the heat is expected to subside somewhat. High temperatures up to 29C can be expected in central and southern regions on Friday, and up to around 30C on Saturday.

items.title: Today in Germany: A roundup of the latest news on Tuesday
items.summary: Germany braces for more heat and thunderstorms, legal professionals renew calls for AfD ban proceedings, hedgehog mistaken for burglar triggers supermarket alarm and more news on Tuesday, August 4th.
items.body_text:
Tuesday's top story: Germany braces for more heat and thunderstorms
A brief reprieve from hot weather over the weekend has come to an end, as most of Germany was set for extreme temperatures -- and thunderstorms in places -- again on Tuesday.
The German Weather Service (DWD) expected showers and thunderstorms locally, along with high temperatures of up to 38C in central and southern parts of the country.
In Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, Brandenburg and Berlin, heavy rain, squalls and hail are also possible. Showers and strong to severe thunderstorms were also expected to move in from the southwest.
READ ALSO: MAP - How to get the latest wildfire information and alerts in Germany
Conditions are expected to remain hot on Wednesday, again with scattered thunderstorms in some places.
The worst of the heat and the severe weather is expected to have subsided by Thursday, with highs predicted to be close to 30C, and 28C by Friday -- but don't expect the summer weather to cool down much further than that over the weekend.
As is usually the case, the coolest place in Germany during the next few days will be along the northern coast. Seaside towns along the beaches on the North or Baltic Seas will see daily high temperatures in the low- to mid 20s through most of the week.
Legal professionals renew calls for AfD ban proceedings
More than 1,000 legal professionals in Germany have signed an open letter urging the federal government and Bundestag to initiate proceedings to ban the Alternative for Germany (AfD) before the Federal Constitutional Court.
According to the Republican Lawyers’ Association (RAV), 1,051 signatories include lawyers, judges, prosecutors, public and private sector legal experts, and trainee lawyers.
The appeal builds on a legal opinion by the Society for Civil Liberties (GFF), which concluded that key AfD positions contravene the constitutional principles of human dignity and democracy. The signatories argue that the federal government and parliament should act immediately to seek a ruling declaring the party unconstitutional.
READ ALSO: 'It's about our friends and neighbours' - Left Party MP calls on Germany to ban the AfD
RAV chair Angela Furmaniak said the Basic Law provides a mechanism to address such risks and urged politicians to make use of it without delay.
The proposal has drawn criticism from BSW founder Sahra Wagenknecht, who described the debate over a ban as damaging and evidence of a growing authoritarian tendency. Under Germany’s Basic Law, only the federal government, Bundestag or Bundesrat can initiate nationwide party ban proceedings.
Deutsche Bahn's best 'super saver' prices almost never available, says consumer advocates
Deutsche Bahn (DB) passengers have little chance of getting a ticket at a 'super saver price' (Super sparpreis) for daytime trips, according to a study by the Federation of German Consumer Organisations.
The best price offer, which the railway advertises on its website, was not available for second-class journeys between 7 am and 7 pm on around three-quarters of the days examined. Instead, super saver prices on most days were between 15 and 157 percent above the advertised price.
The consumer advocacy group had tracked DB ticket prices for 23 months until the end of April.
Association head Ramona Pop told the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung that Deutsche Bahn should make its pricing system simpler and more transparent: "Anyone who advertises particularly low prices should ensure that they are available more often at normal travel times."
For its part, DB suggested that the association's survey was flawed. A DB spokesperson pointed out that the time window crucially left out trips between 6 and 7 am, which are an important commuter hour, as well as direct connections outside of major cities.

items.title: German word of the day: Schlappen
items.summary: More than 100 pairs of slippers have mysteriously vanished from a public swimming pool in Hesse. Thanks to this strange case, a handy German word is suddenly making headlines.
items.body_text:
A baffling series of thefts has hit the Freibad in Fürth im Odenwald, Hesse, where more than 100 pairs of pool shoes have reportedly disappeared since the start of the swimming season.
The culprit remains unknown, leaving locals wondering whether the losses are the work of pranksters, a collector or something else…
What does Schlappen mean?
Schlappen is a common German noun for backless slip-on footwear. In the singular it is der Schlappen (the slip-on), while the plural is die Schlappen (the slip-ons).
It’s an informal umbrella term covering a wide range of footwear, from flip-flops and slides to slippers or pool shoes.
The word is related to the adjective schlapp (limp, floppy or slack), which you might also hear in the context of ill-health. When Germans feel very weak or drained, they will often say Ich bin schlapp (I'm exhausted) or Ich fühle mich schlapp (I feel drained).
But what makes Schlappen easy to remember in the context of footwear is its similarity to the distinctive schlap-schlap sound that flip-flops make as you walk.
READ ALSO: German word of the day - Schlau
While all backless shoes can be described as Schlappen in German, the language also has a number of more specialised terms.
For example, Badelatschen is the most common word to describe waterproof footwear for swimming pools, beaches and communal showers, whereas Hausschuhe (literally ‘house shoes’) is the term used for slippers worn at home.
Why do I need to know Schlappen?
The old stereotype of Germans wearing socks with sandals never quite disappeared and is even enjoying a comeback moment in the form of sports socks matched with Adiletten (Adidas branded slides).
In addition, many Germans routinely remove their street shoes indoors. This means you may well be offered a pair of Schlappen if you visit a German home.
Finally, you may want to voice your own theory about why so many Schlappen have gone missing from the Freibad in Fürth im Odenwald.
Is it some kind of prank or mysterious TikTok challenge? Is a shoe fetishist at work? Or could animals be behind the crime?
It wouldn't be the first time the latter has happened, by the way. Foxes in particular have a history of making off with footwear in Germany, such as in Berlin-Zehlendorf in 2020 when a resident spotted a fox walking through the neighbourhood with a pair of blue flip-flops in its mouth.
Following the animal into nearby bushes, he uncovered a stash of more than 100 stolen shoes. The collection ranged from running shoes to sandals but apparently showed a marked preference for Crocs.
READ ALSO: Sommerlochtiere - Germany's wildest summer 'silly season' stories
Use it like this:
Jemand hat meine Schlappen geklaut! Jetzt muss ich barfuß nach Hause laufen.
Someone stole my pool shoes! Now I have to walk home barefoot.
Zieh dir bitte deine Schlappen an. Der Boden ist kalt.
Please put your slippers on. The floor is cold.
Er ist den ganzen Tag nur in T-Shirt und Schlappen herumgelaufen.
He spent the whole day walking around in just a T-shirt and slip-ons.
In vielen deutschen Wohnungen stehen Schlappen für Gäste bereit.
In many German homes, slippers are kept ready for guests.

items.title: Indonesia again repatriates human trafficking victims from Libya
items.summary: The Jakarta Metropolitan Police has confirmed the repatriation of three Indonesian victims of human trafficking from ...
items.body_text:
"We confirmed the repatriation of three Indonesian victims of human trafficking from Libya, they are NAR, SS, and NKR," Jakarta police's public information unit chief, Adjunct Senior Commissioner Onkoseno Sukahar, referring to the victims with their initials, stated here on Tuesday.
Sukahar said the three victims returned to Indonesia via Soekarno-Hatta International Airport following cross-country and institutional coordination.
After their return, the three victims will undergo recovery phases and receive protection and assistance to help them return to normal life, he noted.
The Jakarta Metropolitan Police, through its General Crimes Directorate and Women and Children Protection Directorate, will work with other institutions, especially the Migrant Workers Protection Ministry, to ensure the victims receive adequate assistance and continue the criminal investigation.
Related news: Indonesia calls for victim-centered approach to combat trafficking
Sukahar also reminded residents to be more careful while seeking jobs abroad and "select only migrant agents recognized by prevailing laws."
Earlier, the General Crimes Directorate at the Jakarta Metropolitan Police unraveled a suspected human trafficking syndicate targeting Indonesian migrant workers who they sent illegally to Libya.
Senior Commissioner Iman Imanuddin, during a press conference on July 24, stated that two individuals, known with initials R and DY, have been named suspects in the case.
"Their syndicate was suspected to have sent at least 105 Indonesian migrant workers overseas in the 2023-2026 period," Imanuddin said.
The police investigation found that the suspects told the victim that they will work as a domestic worker in Turkey with Rp7 million salary (around US$388). To lure more victims, they also provided an additional allowance up to Rp3 million (around US$166).
However, the victims were not flown to Turkey. They were instead flown to work in Libya.
"While in Libya, the victims were subjected to exploitation, including the withholding of their wages and passports, inadequate food, restrictions on their freedom of movement, and physical and psychological abuse," Imanuddin added.
Related news: Indonesia strengthens villages against human trafficking

items.title: Ministry releases 90 free digital textbooks for Islamic schools
items.summary: Indonesia's Ministry of Religious Affairs has prepared 90 digital textbooks on Islamic religious education and ...
items.body_text:
“All textbooks can be downloaded for free through the ministry’s website,” Director General of Islamic Religious Education Amien Suyitno said in Jakarta on Tuesday.
He noted that the collection comprises 58 core textbooks on Islamic and Arabic subjects for elementary, junior high, and senior high schools, as well as 32 titles dedicated to senior high school pupils enrolled in religious studies programs.
Suyitno underlined the initiative as part of the government’s efforts to expand access to learning materials for students and teachers while contributing to literacy enhancement.
He added that the open access to the textbooks aligns with Law No. 3 of 2017 on the book system, noting the ministry’s responsibility to provide quality teaching materials for religious educational institutions.
The official further highlighted that the textbooks “were written in stages in an organized manner” by authors selected through a rigorous screening process.
He emphasized that the publications had undergone reviews, evaluations, and quality assurance by the ministry’s Center for Religious Book Assessment, Lectures, and Religious Literacy.
Nyayu Khodijah, director of curriculum, facilities, institutions, and student affairs for madrasas, noted that the publication follows the issuance of a decree by the religious affairs minister last year.
She elaborated that the textbooks cover a wide range of subjects, including Qur’an and Hadith Studies, Islamic Creed and Ethics, Islamic Jurisprudence, History of Islamic Civilization, Arabic Language, Qur’anic Exegesis, Principles of Islamic Jurisprudence, Islamic Theology, and Sufism.
“The teaching materials enshrined in the textbooks are presented in an easy-to-understand approach to help foster strong character and morals,” Khodijah said.
She added that the elementary and junior high school textbooks adopt “an interactive approach” to promote a moderate understanding of Islam through the daily application of “tolerant and inclusive Islamic values.”

items.title: Prinsa Mandagie Pastikan Tetap Bernyanyi usai Menikah, Bersyukur Dapat Dukungan Pasangan
items.summary: Prinsa Mandagie memastikan tetap berkarier di dunia musik setelah menikah. Ia mengaku mendapat dukungan penuh dari pasangannya.
items.body_text:
Kabar Artis
Prinsa Mandagie Pastikan Tetap Bernyanyi usai Menikah, Bersyukur Dapat Dukungan Pasangan
Prinsa Mandagie memastikan tetap berkarier di dunia musik setelah menikah. Ia mengaku mendapat dukungan penuh dari pasangannya.
Ringkasan Berita:
- Prinsa Mandagie menegaskan tetap ingin berkarier di industri musik meski telah menikah.
- Ia bersyukur karena sang pasangan mendukung pekerjaannya selama membuatnya bahagia.
- Menurut Prinsa, hubungan yang sehat tetap memberi ruang bagi masing-masing untuk menjalani passion dan me time.
TRIBUNNEWS.COM - Penyanyi Prinsa Mandagie memastikan bahwa pernikahan bukan menjadi alasan untuk menghentikan langkahnya di dunia musik.
Lulusan ajang pencarian bakat Indonesian Idol itu mengaku tetap ingin berkarya dan menerima pekerjaan di industri hiburan meski suatu hari nanti telah resmi berumah tangga.
Bagi Prinsa, membangun rumah tangga dan menjalani karier bukanlah dua hal yang harus dipertentangkan.
Selama ada komunikasi dan dukungan dari pasangan, ia meyakini keduanya dapat berjalan beriringan. Hal itu pula yang menjadi prinsipnya dalam mempersiapkan kehidupan setelah menikah.
Cerita tersebut disampaikan Prinsa saat berkunjung ke kantor Tribun Network di kawasan Palmerah, Jakarta Pusat, pada 14 Mei 2026.
Dalam kesempatan itu, pemilik nama lengkap Prinsa Shafira Mandagie ini berbagi pandangan mengenai karier, hubungan asmara, hingga rencana kehidupannya di masa depan.
Prinsa menegaskan bahwa dirinya tetap ingin berkarier di industri musik meski telah menikah nanti.
"Masih (berkarir di musik)," ujar Prinsa, dikutip Selasa (4/8/2026).
Pelantun lagu Sahabat Dulu ini bersyukur karena pasangan yang dimilikinya saat ini memberikan dukungan penuh terhadap pekerjaannya sebagai penyanyi.
Menurut Prinsa, selama dirinya merasa bahagia menjalani profesi tersebut, sang pasangan tidak pernah melarang.
"Jadi alhamdulillah aku punya pasangan yang enggak ngelarang ini. Itu sih, as long ngelihat aku happy dia akan support sih," lanjutnya.
Baca juga: Prinsa Mandagie Kenang Audisi Indonesian Idol, Sempat Minder Lihat Ziva Magnolya-Novia Bachmid
Prinsa mengungkapkan bahwa sejak awal hubungan, ia sudah menyampaikan keinginannya untuk tetap berada di dunia musik.
Meski demikian, ia menyadari bahwa setelah menikah nanti akan ada tanggung jawab baru yang harus menjadi prioritas.
"Jadi selama ini aku udah bilang kalau aku masih pengin di musik, ya. Nanti misalkan aku sudah menikah, tapi aku akan tahu priority tentunya, gitu. Cuma aku masih pengin ada di sini," jelasnya.
Menurut Prinsa, dunia musik merupakan ruang bagi dirinya untuk berkembang sekaligus menjadi waktu yang ia gunakan untuk menikmati aktivitas yang disukai.

items.title: Purbaya Siapkan Stimulus Baru Kendaraan Listrik, Kuota Motor EV Jadi 500.000 Unit
items.summary: Purbaya menyebut belum ada rencana pemberian insentif bagi kendaraan hybrid, PHEV, maupun REEV.
items.body_text:
GIIAS 2026
Purbaya Siapkan Stimulus Baru Kendaraan Listrik, Kuota Motor EV Jadi 500.000 Unit
Purbaya menyebut belum ada rencana pemberian insentif bagi kendaraan hybrid, PHEV, maupun REEV.
Ringkasan Berita:
- Menkeu Purbaya mengungkapkan pemerintah akan meluncurkan stimulus baru kendaraan listrik dalam 2-3 pekan.
- Kuota insentif sepeda motor listrik akan ditingkatkan menjadi 500.000 unit, disertai insentif mobil listrik tertentu.
- Purbaya menyebut belum ada rencana pemberian insentif bagi kendaraan hybrid, PHEV, maupun REEV.
TRIBUNNEWS.COM, TANGERANG - Pemerintah kembali menegaskan komitmennya mendorong penggunaan kendaraan listrik (Electric Vehicle/EV) di tengah pasar otomotif nasional yang masih dalam tahap pemulihan setelah mencapai puncak penjualan pada 2022.
Menteri Keuangan Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa mengatakan, perkembangan industri otomotif nasional kini mulai bergeser dari kendaraan konvensional menuju kendaraan berteknologi bersih dengan emisi rendah.
Selain itu, pangsa pasar kendaraan listrik telah meningkat signifikan dalam beberapa tahun terakhir. Pemerintah tidak hanya mengejar peningkatan adopsi EV, tetapi juga ingin memastikan perkembangan industri tersebut.
Baca juga: Insentif EV Mundur Lagi, Gaikindo Minta Konsumen Tak Tunda Pembelian: Produsen Sudah Banyak Diskon
"Pangsa pasar kendaraan listrik telah meningkat hampir 18 kali lipat dalam 4 tahun terakhir. Tantangan ke depan bukan lagi hanya mendorong adopsi kendaraan listrik tetapi juga memastikan nilai tambah domestik, investasi, lapangan kerja, dan daya saing industri nasional," ungkap Purbaya dalam acara Gaikindo International Automotive Conference (GIAC) 2026, ICE BSD, Tangerang, Banten, Selasa (4/8/2026).
Pemerintah disebut masih serius mengembangkan ekosistem kendaraan listrik meski sebelumnya muncul kekhawatiran mengenai keberlanjutan subsidi atau insentif EV pada tahun ini.
Perubahan kondisi geopolitik global dan tingginya harga minyak menjadi alasan pemerintah perlu mempercepat pengurangan ketergantungan terhadap bahan bakar minyak impor.
Purbaya memastikan pemerintah akan melanjutkan kebijakan untuk mendorong penggunaan kendaraan listrik. Kebijakan tersebut dinilai sejalan dengan upaya pemerintah mengurangi ketergantungan Indonesia terhadap impor minyak.
"Pemerintah ingin mengurangi ketergantungan kita pada impor minyak secara signifikan. Itulah sebabnya kami mempromosikan EV. Kami akan terus melakukan itu," ujarnya.
Insentif Segera Diumumkan
Purbaya bahkan mengungkapkan pemerintah tengah menyiapkan stimulus tambahan untuk kendaraan listrik. Kebijakan tersebut disebut akan diluncurkan Presiden Prabowo Subianto dalam waktu sekitar dua hingga tiga pekan mendatang.
Stimulus baru tersebut antara lain mencakup dukungan untuk 500.000 unit sepeda motor listrik, serta insentif untuk mobil listrik.
"Saya rasa dua minggu atau tiga minggu dari sekarang Presiden akan meluncurkan stimulus lain untuk EV termasuk untuk 500.000 sepeda motor dan untuk mobil EV juga. PPN ditanggung pemerintah turun menjadi 1 persen untuk mobil listrik tertentu," jelas Purbaya.
Sebelumnya, insentif EV akan diberikan kepada sepeda motor dan mobil listrik dengan kuota masing-masing 200.000, yang totalnya mencapai 400.000 unit.
Diperluas ke Hybrid?

items.title: MK Minta Anggaran MBG Dipisah dari Dana Pendidikan, Akankah Berlaku Mulai 2027? Ini Sikap Gerindra
items.summary: Putusan MK ubah skema anggaran MBG. Gerindra buka suara soal kemungkinan pemisahan dari anggaran pendidikan mulai APBN 2027.
items.body_text:
Program Makan Bergizi Gratis
MK Minta Anggaran MBG Dipisah dari Dana Pendidikan, Akankah Berlaku Mulai 2027? Ini Sikap Gerindra
Putusan MK ubah skema anggaran MBG. Gerindra buka suara soal kemungkinan pemisahan dari anggaran pendidikan mulai APBN 2027.
Ringkasan Berita:
TRIBUNNEWS.COM, JAKARTA - Partai Gerindra menyatakan pemerintah masih mengkaji tindak lanjut putusan Mahkamah Konstitusi (MK) yang meminta anggaran Program Makan Bergizi Gratis (MBG) dipisahkan dari dana pendidikan.
Pernyataan tersebut disampaikan Juru Bicara Partai Gerindra, Bahtra Banong, setelah MK memutus uji materi terkait penggunaan anggaran pendidikan untuk membiayai program MBG.
Gerindra, sebagai partai politik pengusung Presiden Prabowo Subianto, menyebut penyesuaian anggaran perlu dikaji agar penyusunan Anggaran Pendapatan dan Belanja Negara (APBN) tetap sesuai dengan putusan MK.
"Ya tentu kita nanti akan melakukan kajian-kajian terkait dengan putusan MK itu. Mungkin kita akan mengkaji lebih dalam lagi karena ini berkaitan dengan APBN kita," kata Bahtra di Kompleks Parlemen, Senayan, Jakarta, Selasa (4/8/2026).
Menurut Bahtra, pelaksanaan anggaran MBG pada 2026 tidak menjadi persoalan karena MK tidak mempersoalkan skema pembiayaan yang berjalan pada tahun tersebut.
Karena itu, pembahasan akan diarahkan pada penyusunan anggaran tahun berikutnya, termasuk kemungkinan penerapan pemisahan anggaran MBG dalam APBN 2027.
Bahtra belum memastikan apakah pemerintah akan langsung memisahkan anggaran MBG dari dana pendidikan saat penyampaian Nota Keuangan dan Rancangan APBN (RAPBN) 2027.
"Saya belum dapat kesimpulannya ya, tetapi yang pasti nanti mungkin di Nota Keuangan pemerintah akan menyampaikan RAPBN kita. Semua anggaran nanti sudah ada sesuai dengan mandatory-nya masing-masing," ujar Bahtra.
Dengan demikian, Gerindra belum menyatakan bahwa pemisahan anggaran MBG pasti dilakukan mulai 2027. Pemerintah masih memiliki ruang penyesuaian sesuai batas waktu yang ditetapkan MK.
Baca juga: Politisi PDIP Minta Anggaran MBG Dipisah dari Dana Pendidikan Mulai 2027
MK Minta Anggaran MBG Dipisah
MK dalam putusan yang dibacakan Kamis (30/7/2026) mengabulkan sebagian uji materi Undang-Undang Nomor 17 Tahun 2025 tentang APBN Tahun Anggaran 2026 terkait masuknya anggaran MBG dalam komponen dana pendidikan 20 persen dari APBN.
MK memutuskan anggaran MBG tidak boleh menjadi bagian dari anggaran operasional pendidikan. Pemisahan tersebut wajib dilakukan paling lambat dalam APBN 2028.
Hakim Konstitusi Guntur Hamzah menegaskan dana pendidikan harus diprioritaskan untuk kebutuhan utama pendidikan yang berkaitan langsung dengan penyelenggaraan pendidikan.
Perkara tersebut diajukan oleh guru honorer, pelajar, mahasiswa, dan yayasan pendidikan. Para pemohon tidak menolak program MBG, tetapi meminta pembiayaannya tidak menggunakan pos anggaran pendidikan.

items.body_text:
PSEi slips on Mideast woes, inflation jitters
MANILA, Philippines – Local stocks fell on Tuesday as investors stayed on the sidelines amid renewed geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and caution ahead of the release of the Philippines’ July inflation data.
The benchmark Philippine Stock Exchange Index (PSEi) fell 0.60 percent, or 38.08 points, to close at 6,296.64.
READ: Trump says Iran facing ‘last chance before decapitation’
Philstocks Financial Inc. said market sentiment weakened after Iran denied reports that negotiations with the US for a possible deal were underway.
The development pushed global oil prices higher and weighed on the peso, prompting investors to trim risk exposure.
Market participants also adopted a wait-and-see stance before the release of July inflation figures, further dampening trading activity.
Luis Limlingan, head of sales at Regina Capital Development Corp., said the local bourse ended lower as investors locked in profits following the previous session’s gains.
“As a result, the PSEi consolidated around the 6,300 level amid continued profit-taking and subdued buying interest,” Limlingan said.
Despite the decline, foreign investors remained buyers, posting net inflows of P249.91 million.
However, overall participation stayed muted, with net value turnover reaching only P4.29 billion.
READ: Poll: Q2 PH growth likely slowed to 2.7%
Mining stocks bucked the broader market weakness, emerging as the day’s best-performing sector after gaining 0.55 percent.
Property counters suffered the steepest losses, falling 1.05 percent.
Advancers were also scarce, with only six PSEi constituent stocks ending in positive territory.
Among individual issues, Century Pacific Food Inc. led the benchmark gainers after climbing 3.86 percent to P32.25.
Meanwhile, Ayala Land Inc. was the session’s biggest drag, declining 3.75 percent to P15.40.
Ron Acoba, chief investment strategist at Trading Edge, said ALI’s stocks fell on concerns that it could be removed from the MSCI Philippines Index, with the latest index review and constituent changes set to be announced on August 12. /pai INQ

Sun Life Philippines fulfills its promise to clients with over PHP 5 billion in claims paid in 2025
Keeping true to its commitment to being the Filipinos’ Partner for Life, Sun Life, the No. 1 life insurance company in the Philippines in terms of total premium income, paid more than PHP 5.25 billion claims in 2025, providing financial support to Clients when they needed it most.
The total amount covers claims paid across Sun Life’s individual and group insurance businesses, as well as its bancassurance operations through Sun Life Grepa Financial Inc., throughout 2025. In addition to this, Sun Life also paid ₱3.17 billion in policy maturities in the past year.
“Every claim we pay represents a promise fulfilled to a Client or family who counted on us during an important moment in their lives,” said JJ Moreno, Country Head and CEO of Sun Life Philippines. “It reflects our commitment to providing financial support when it matters most.”
Sun Life continued to deliver on this promise in 2026, paying more than ₱2 billion in claims as well as releasing ₱1.4 billion in policy maturities from January – May of 2026.
For generations, Sun Life has helped people secure their future and live healthier lives. Claims and maturity payments reflect the company’s enduring role in providing financial support and peace of mind through life’s important moments.
To learn more about Sun Life’s products and services, visit www.sunlife.com.ph. Stay updated by following @sunlifeph on Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok.

items.body_text:
Richard Gutierrez joins Barbie Imperial in outreach activity at her former school
Richard Gutierrez joined girlfriend Barbie Imperial in giving back to the actress’ former school in Albay, Bicol, as she marked her 28th birthday.
Imperial shared an Instagram Reel showing highlights from their rainy-day visit, where they distributed school supplies, meals, and other necessities to students. The couple wore matching khaki jackets.
Aside from Gutierrez. Imperial’s best friend, actress Alexa Miro also joined the outreach activity. The trio spent time with the children and teachers during the event.
READ: Richard Gutierrez admits ‘Blood vs Duty’ used AI amid backlash
        View this post on Instagram            
Explaining why she chose to celebrate her birthday in her hometown, Imperial said returning to Bicol always brings her peace and comfort.
“This year, I chose to celebrate my birthday at home. I always find myself going back to where I came from. Iba talaga ‘yung feeling dito sa Bicol. Mayon has a way of making me feel so calm. Every time I come home, ang saya-saya ng puso ko,” she wrote in the caption of her post.
The actress also expressed gratitude to her grade school teachers, whom she described as her “second parents,” for helping shape the person she is today.
Imperial said giving back to her school had long been one of her goals. “I’ve always wanted to do this, to give back to my school and the teachers who helped raise me. And finally, I was able to make it happen with the help of the people I love,” she expressed.
        View this post on Instagram            
Gutierrez, meanwhile, also greeted Imperial on Instagram by posting intimate photos of the two of them with the caption, “HBD BB,” followed by a heart emoji.

items.title: Your next cafe crawl: Ube-st drinks in Makati
items.summary: From dessert lattes to boozy cocktails, we explore Makati’s ube-st drinks
items.body_text:
AT A GLANCE
“It’s not ube, it’s oob.” The fact that content creator dom.skii’s video correcting the rest of the world’s pronunciation of ube went viral says it all: ube has truly gone global. What was once a humble rice substitute for the indigenous people, or a must-purchase pasalubong from Baguio, is now a flavor trend that the world seemingly can’t get enough of.
While foodies across the globe are just catching up on how amazing ube is, local cafes have had it on their menu way before it was a trend.
We mapped out an ube crawl through the busy streets of Makati and did the groundwork so you can go straight to the best spots!
Sulok Coffee’s Balarin
For those who haven’t tasted Ube as a latte and only grew up eating ube halaya as a snack, Sulok Coffee’s Iced Ube Latte or Balarin (P205) is a great introduction to how the flavor fares in a drink.
Head barista Paul Sillar shared that they use a homemade, locally sourced ube powder. They whisk its nutty, vanilla notes directly with espresso. The result? A subtle, earthy sweetness that complements the strength of coffee. The espresso still dominates the drink, while the sweetness of ube lingers as an aftertaste.
For Sillar, the Iced Ube Latte is best paired with their best-selling desserts like tiramisu and creme brulee cake.
📍3/F, Salcedo One Center, 170 Salcedo, Makati City, Metro Manila
Oolah’s Ube Coconut Cloud
Just a seven-minute stroll from Sulok Coffee is Oolah, a small spot that is always packed with customers. Beyond their signature banana pudding dessert, the shop serves a vibrant menu of creative concoctions containing either matcha, hojicha, and of course, ube.
Oolah’s Head Barista Rence Banaag served their latest creation, the Ube Coconut Cloud, a refreshing twist on ube.
The drink has multiple layers. It begins with ube halaya as its base, followed by fresh coconut water, then blanketed by their velvety in-house ube cream. For added texture, toasted coconut crisps were sprinkled on top.
With the global ube hype, Banaag shared, more customers have been seeking their ube beverages. But they didn’t stop with what their menu offered. “We really decided on trying to offer more creative drinks on ube. So, we have Ube Halaya Matcha, Double Ube Matcha, [and] Ube Cheese Macapuno [as well].”
Banaag also served Oolah’s Ube Cheese Macapuno Pudding, a purple take on their famous banana pudding.
📍LGF, Cityland III, 417 V.A. Rufino St, corner Ormaza, Legazpi Village, Makati City
Annex House’s Iced Ube Latte
This cup of ube and coffee goodness from a cafe that moonlights as a bar in Poblacion also offers a layered experience: ube flavor mixed with espresso and coconut milk, then finished with a crunch of rice crispies or pinipig, and the richness of coconut curds or latik.
Annex House serves it with either dairy or oat milk. The oat milk variant not only caters to lactose-intolerant drinkers but also enhances the smoky depth of the latik. Annex House barista Ange Delos Reyes adds that oat milk brings out more of the natural sweetness of the ube and coconut milk.
According to Angeline, their ube latte has been a menu mainstay since the branch opened. It has also become one of the social bar’s top drinks since the trend, joining crowd favorites like their Leche Flan Latte and Biko Latte.
📍5638 Don Pedro, Makati City
Instagram | Facebook | https://annex-house.com/
OTO’s Cool Summer
To get a taste of ube mixed with booze, we visited one of Poblacion’s well-known and long-standing bars in the area: OTO.
OTO is a Japanese-themed listening room that doubles as a coffee shop by day and a cocktail bar by night. OTO puts a spin on classic cocktails through their ‘Everything is a Remix’ menu–with Cool Summer as a concoction inspired by the show Miami Vice.
Alex Javier, OTO’s bar manager, explained that while the original Miami Vice is a mix of Strawberry Daiquiri and Piña Colada, Cool Summer has Ube Amaro, Luisita Blanco rum, and a local rum in the purple blend, while the yellow blend has swee

items.title: FACT CHECK: Alex Eala quote card linking green outfit to VP Sara is fake
items.summary: No news reports or credible sources confirm the alleged statement by the Filipino tennis star, in which she supposedly denied that she wore a green outfit in support of Vice President Sara Duterte
items.body_text:
AT A GLANCE
Claim: A quote card shows Filipina tennis sensation Alex Eala denying that she wore a green outfit during the World Tennis Association (WTA) 500 Mudabala DC Open to show support for Vice President Sara Duterte.
Rating: FALSE
Why we fact-checked this: As of writing, the Facebook post has 923 reactions, 133 comments, and 81 shares.
The quote card, which appears similar to those released by GMA News, shows Eala supposedly saying, “I never wore a green outfit to support VP Sara; that’s a big no for me.”
Rappler found several social media posts bearing the same claim.
The quote card circulated amid speculation among some social media users that Eala’s green outfit was a show of support for Duterte, who is currently facing an impeachment trial.
The facts: The quote card is fake. There are no news reports or video recordings from legitimate and credible sources reporting the supposed statement by Eala.
On August 3, GMA News debunked the quote card and warned the public, saying, “May kumakalat na fake post na may logo at template na kahawig ng GMA News.”
“Hindi totoo ang quote ni Alex Eala na nakalagay sa post,” the post added.
(There is a fake post circulating online with a logo and template resembling GMA News. The quote by Alex Eala that was included in the post is not true.)
Eala also told journalist Dyan Castillejo that she chose the green outfit herself, but she did not mention any political meaning to it, as reported by PressOne.PH.
Alex Eala at WTA 500 Mubadala DC Open: The false posts circulated amid the Filipino tennis star’s historic Washington Open campaign, which saw her march to the Mubadala finals after defeating the four-time grand champion Naomi Osaka of Japan in semis, straight sets, 6-4, 6-2. (READ: Alex Eala on the cusp of Washington Open title after Naomi Osaka sweep)
In the finals, Eala faced world No. 3 Jessica Pegula and dominated the resumption of the finals game after it was halted by a lengthy rain delay and rescheduled. On Monday, August 3 (Tuesday, August 4, Manila time), the Filipina secured her first-ever WTA crown after a 4-6, 6-4, 6-0 win.
Her maiden WTA Tour crown has propelled Eala to the world top 20 for the first time in her career, climbing to No. 20 in the updated WTA rankings released on August 4.
Fact-check: With her ongoing successes in her tennis career, Eala has been a favorite target of disinformation. Rappler has debunked several false claims about her:
- FACT CHECK: Photo of Alex Eala statue in QC is AI-generated
- FACT CHECK: Hontiveros did not seek Alex Eala endorsement for LGBT advocacy
- FACT CHECK: Marcos did not give tennis star Alex Eala $100,000 bonus
– Owenh Toledo/Rappler.com
Owenh Toledo is a graduate of Rappler’s fact-checking mentorship program. This fact check was reviewed by a member of Rappler’s research team and a senior editor. Learn more about Rappler’s fact-checking mentorship program here.
Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

items.body_text:
AT A GLANCE
(The following is a press release from the F. Sionil Jose Young Writers Awards.)
The F. Sionil Jose Young Writers Award was established by the children of F. Sionil Jose and Teresita Jovellanos Jose to honor his legacy to the young and beginning writers of the Philippines.
It seeks to advance excellence, integrity, social justice, and the expression of love of country in literature.
It is also to honor the memory of his wife, Teresita Jovellanos Jose, who was his pillar of support and inspiration.
Requirements
1. Writers should be 30 years old or younger.
2. They should be Filipino citizens residing in the Philippines.
3. The awards will be for the best short stories in English and Filipino.
Submission guidelines
1. Submit one short story written in English or Filipino.
2. The story may be unpublished or published.
3. Published stories must have been published in January 2026 or later.
4. The stories must cover a maximum of 20 pages, in double-spaced, 12-point typeface. The pages must be numbered.
5. Submissions must include a cover page, which will include the complete name of the writer, their date of birth, address, email address, phone number, and the title and the language of the short story.
6. The cover page must also include a brief biography (200 words maximum) about the author. If the short story has been published, the publication source and date should be indicated.
Submission date
Entries must be received by 11:59 pm (Manila time) on August 15, 2026.
Submissions must be sent in the form of a separate cover page and the short story, both in PDF form to fsjawards2026@gmail.com.
Prizes for each category
First prize – P25,000
Second prize – P15,000
Third prize – P10,000
The awards ceremony will be held on October 10, 2026 at the PEN Philippines Congress to be held at De La Salle University.
The F. Sionil Jose Young Writers Award is funded by the children of F. Sionil Jose and Teresita Jovellanos Jose.
The awards are managed and facilitated by PEN Philippines and hosted by the Bienvenido N. Santos Creative Writing Center, De La Salle University.
To protect the integrity of the competition, the organizers reserve the right to request drafts, revision histories, research notes, or other evidence of authorship. items.title: Sara Duterte trial recap, Aug. 4: Safehouses, signatures, censored S word
items.summary: It was a remark so harsh that it was swiftly struck from the record: the prosecution calling the Office of the Vice President's use and liquidation of confidential funds nothing short of a “scam.”
items.body_text:
Sara Duterte trial recap, Aug. 4: Safehouses, signatures, censored S word
MANILA, Philippines — It was a remark so harsh that it was swiftly struck from the record: the prosecution calling the Office of the Vice President's use and liquidation of confidential funds nothing short of a “scam.”
That cutting remark by prosecution counsel Lorna Kapunan came at the end of her direct examination of former state auditor Roderick Wamil on Tuesday, August 4, and drew an immediately granted motion to strike from defense counsel Michael Poa.
The twelfth day of the trial saw both the prosecution and the defense use their full time on direct, cross, redirect and recross.
The former state auditor testified that the OVP and the Department of Education (DepEd) reported tens of millions of pesos in confidential fund spending without attaching enough supporting documents to justify the expenses, and that Vice President Sara Duterte's signature can be found as having approved or certified nearly all documents.
Poa, who served as DepEd undersecretary, chief of staff and spokesperson under Duterte, sought to draw from Wamil that the COA has not concluded actual misuse of the secret funds.
1. Speed of spending becomes a non-issue?
Nothing in the rules barred the Office of the Vice President from spending a quarter's worth of confidential funds in 11 days, Wamil testified during Poa's cross-examination.
This concession goes to the finding that first put Duterte's confidential funds under scrutiny in 2024: COA's finding that the OVP spent its P125-million allotment for 2022 between December 21 and 31 of that year.
Poa asked Wamil whether any provision of the joint circular prohibits using a quarterly cash advance within 60 days.
"Wala po (None)," Wamil answered. Asked about 11 days, he replied, "Wala din po (Also none)."
The state auditor, however, clarified that this was precisely why the 11-day expenditure of Duterte's office does not appear in his findings and was mentioned only as a fact in the audit observation memorandum.
Poa also drew out from Wamil that COA took months to act after the OVP submitted its liquidation of its confidential funds.
Wamil confirmed Duterte's office filed its liquidation report in January 2023 and that COA issued its first audit observation memorandum on the OVP on Sept. 14, 2023, about eight months later.
Prior to this, the prosecution also pursued a line of questioning on the alleged irregularity of how the OVP blew through its secret funds in 2022.
During the direct for Wamil, Kapunan established that the OVP's submissions showed P16 million spent renting safe houses over those 11 days, or P2 million a day by her computation.
The prosecution's larger point, drawn from Wamil's testimony across two days, is that whatever the pace, the spending was irregular, as the OVP charged non-confidential expenses — like medical, food and travel assistance — against the secret funds.
"We did not say, ever, that the confidential funds cannot be spent in 11 days," House prosecution spokesperson Benjamin Tolosa said at a press conference in the afternoon. "Ang tanong is: Na-justify ba ng bise presidente paano nila naubos itong P125 million in just 11 days?"
Tolosa said the question is whether the defense was able to show its speedy expenditure complied with the circular.
2. What the OVP and DepEd plans and reports did not say
Neither the OVP nor DepEd showed COA what their confidential funds were specifically for beyond broad categories, Wamil testified.
The joint circular requires a physical and financial plan, naming the confidential activities that spending will be based on.
The OVP's plan did not include this, Wamil testified.
It listed a "good government program" with an expected outcome of "safe implementation of OVP initiatives and confidence building."
DepEd's plans, meanwhile, listed four programs each quarter: counter-insurgency, abuse prevention in schools, anti-illegal activities and anti-extremism. The four totaled exac

items.title: 'Scam ito': Kapunan says on alleged OVP fund misuse at impeachment trial
items.summary: Prosecution counsel Lorna Kapunan characterized the alleged mishandling of public funds as an outright scam before the impeachment court trying Vice President Sara Duterte.
items.body_text:
'Scam ito': Kapunan says on alleged OVP fund misuse at impeachment trial
MANILA, Philippines — Prosecution counsel Lorna Kapunan characterized the alleged mishandling of public funds as an outright scam before the impeachment court trying Vice President Sara Duterte.
In her cross-examination of state auditor Roderick Wamil on Tuesday, August 4, Kapunan asked the witness whether the presumption of personal benefit applied to the unliquidated disbursements of the Office of the Vice President.
Wamil affirmed, citing a Commission on Audit circular stating that an "accountable officer's" failure to liquidate funds upon demand is prima facie evidence of misuse, and confirmed that Duterte qualifies as an accountable officer.
He said that, as head of the agency, the vice president — who served as education secretary — qualifies as an accountable officer responsible for overseeing confidential funds and ensuring full compliance.
"Ang ibig sabihin po ng prima facie evidence under 8.3 ay nagkaroon po ng presumption na ginamit 'yung funds for the personal use and benefit of the accountable officers," Wamil said.
(What prima facie evidence under 8.3 means is that there is a presumption that the funds were used for the personal use and benefit of the accountable officers.)
In response, the defense, through Michael Poa, repeatedly raised objections, arguing that the line of questioning called for a legal conclusion on matters still pending before the court.
When the court sustained the objection, Kapunan said: “Hindi prima facie evidence kung akong tatanungin. Scam ito!"
(If I were asked, this is not prima facie evidence. This is a scam!)
Poa immediately countered by moving to strike the comment, calling it "out of order."
The court granted the motion to strike Kapunan's remark from the official trial record before adjourning for the lunch break.
Wamil is the third witness under Article II of the Articles of Impeachment, which tackles the confidential funds of the Department of Education and the Office of the Vice President.
Wamil is expected to return on August 5 for the interpellation of the senator-judges.

items.body_text:
Taguig infra probe opened a 'cauldron of worms' — Lacson
MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Panfilo Lacson signaled no retreat in his ongoing investigation into alleged infrastructure anomalies in Taguig City, warning that corrupt officials will soon be “drowned in the truth” as new findings expose a wider web of unlawful activities.
In a social media post on Tuesday, August 4, Lacson said his case study on Taguig had expanded into a "cauldron of worms" following a crucial meeting with Philippine Reclamation Authority (PRA) officials.
According to Lacson, the meeting uncovered fraudulent schemes ranging from non-existent "ghost" slope protection projects to unauthorized land reclamation spanning parts of Laguna Lake.
“Aside from the PRA and the Ombudsman, we will closely coordinate with the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) central office, Laguna Lake Development Authority (LLDA) and other concerned agencies not only to jail the crooks behind these grossly anomalous and patently illegal activities but also forfeit the already reclaimed Lakeshore areas in favor of the national government,” Lacson said.
“There is no turning back!” he added.
On July 28, Lacson said he submitted the documentary and testimonial evidence from his investigation into alleged anomalies in Taguig infrastructure projects to the Office of the Ombudsman.
According to Lacson, his office estimated that Taguig accumulated around P14.4 billion worth of infrastructure projects from 2020 to 2025.
The probe into infrastructure projects in Taguig, the political stronghold of Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano, was launched after Cayetano questioned Lacson's integrity.

items.title: India fires 11 officials over multiple failures on 19 of its newest highways
items.summary: India's road transport ministry has dismissed 11 officials and taken disciplinary action against another 11 after 19 national highway projects suffered collapses, cave-ins and structural failures over the past two years.
items.body_text:
Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari disclosed the action in a reply to the Rajya Sabha, the upper house of India's parliament, on July 29.
The failures struck newly built bridges, flyovers and road surfaces during 2025 and 2026, The Tribune reported. They included damage on the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway, the roughly 1,400-km corridor Gadkari has championed as a transformative infrastructure project.
Seven of the 19 affected projects are in Kerala.
On the Delhi-Dehradun Expressway, two large potholes opened near Shamli in Uttar Pradesh on July 1. Prime Minister Narendra Modi had inaugurated the INR120 billion (US$1.26 billion) route less than three months earlier, on April 14, The Federal reported.
Motorists filmed the damaged stretch and posted the footage online. Several vehicles were reported to have suffered bent alloy wheels.
The National Highways Authority of India blamed water pooling after the season's first monsoon rain, in a statement quoted by ThePrint. Delays in commissioning a permanent cross-drainage system compounded the problem, the authority said.
A balancing culvert designed to carry rainwater across the carriageway could not be brought into service because local residents objected, having used the culvert opening as a vehicle crossing. Slope protection and chute drain work remained unfinished because of a land dispute.
The opposition Congress party alleged misappropriation of funds.
NHAI issued show-cause notices to the project director, the authority engineer and the construction contractor, and suspended several senior officials on the project, Garhwal Post reported.
The damaged section was repaired and reopened within days. A temporary drain was built while permanent drainage work continues.
In Kerala, a 250-meter section of elevated corridor on National Highway 66 collapsed at Kooriyad in Malappuram on May 19, 2025. Foundation soil proved unable to carry the load of the embankment above it.
NHAI terminated its site engineer and suspended the project director, Onmanorama reported. The authority ordered concessionaire KNR Constructions to clear the debris and rebuild the structure as a viaduct at its own expense, estimated at INR800 million ($8.4 million).
The company was barred from bidding for up to a year and faced a proposed penalty of INR118 million ($1.24 million). Kerala Kaumudi reported that show-cause notices also went to design consultants Strata Geosystem and HBS Infra Engineers and to safety consultant Sri Infotech.
The rebuilt stretch was finished and set to reopen in May 2026.
On the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway, an 8-foot-wide hole opened in a bridge deck near Ankleshwar in Gujarat, according to The Tribune. Surface collapses had been reported earlier at Dausa and Sawai Madhopur in Rajasthan.
Rain exposed ruts, cracks and surface deformation on the Sanchore-Santalpur highway in Gujarat. The contractor drew a INR28 million ($294,000) penalty and a recommendation that it be barred from bidding for a year or until the defects are rectified, whichever comes later.
Gadkari said contractors and concessionaires faced the measures set out in their contract and concession agreements, including termination, penalties, liquidated damages, debarment, blacklisting and formal designation as non-performers.
The 11 dismissed officials were removed on the basis of performance assessment. The others faced action for negligence and dereliction of duty.

items.title: Australian engineer wins $28,000 as firing over 17-minute Singapore Airlines flight delay ruled unfair
items.summary: An Australian aircraft maintenance engineer has been awarded more than A$40,000 (US$28,000) in compensation after being dismissed over a decision that delayed a Singapore Airlines flight by 17 minutes, though he will not be reinstated.
items.body_text:
The case centered on a maintenance procedure that delayed the aircraft's departure from Singapore Changi Airport.
The Brisbane-based engineer, who worked for aircraft maintenance firm Heston MRO between May 2023 and December 2025, shut down and restarted a Singapore Airlines aircraft prior to departure after multiple fault messages flashed in the cockpit, as reported by Aviation A2Z.
The pilots agreed to the reboot, which cleared the cockpit warnings but delayed the flight by 17 minutes.
Singapore Airlines subsequently revoked the engineer's maintenance authorization, arguing that the system restart was unnecessary for the reported fault and that he had relied on personal judgment rather than established protocols, causing delays and customer complaints.
The engineer, who brings more than 25 years of industry experience, maintained that restarting the aircraft was standard practice, comparing it to rebooting a smartphone to resolve minor software glitches. He stated that the action enhanced overall safety, reduced the pilots' workload, and prevented further operational disruptions.
An initial internal investigation, endorsed by several senior Heston MRO executives, including the chief executive, concluded that the engineer had followed standard practice and committed no procedural breaches.
However, Singapore Airlines disputed those findings, claiming the initial report lacked objectivity. Heston MRO then commissioned a second review led by its newly appointed head of quality and safety, who deemed the engineer's actions a "reckless violation," according to the International Business Times.
The engineer was subsequently dismissed based on the revised findings without being shown the new report or given an opportunity to respond.
He challenged his termination before Australia's Fair Work Commission (FWC). The tribunal ruled that while reinstatement was inappropriate due to an irretrievable breakdown in the employment relationship, the termination itself was procedurally unfair.
The tribunal found that Heston MRO failed to accord the worker natural justice before terminating his contract and awarded him A$40,000 for financial losses resulting from the unfair dismissal.
During FWC proceedings, Heston MRO also cited the engineer's unauthorized secondary work for Virgin Australia, claiming it violated internal guidelines regarding employee fatigue management.
The engineer countered that his extra shifts never conflicted with his primary duties at Heston MRO and consistently complied with all mandatory rest period regulations.
Fair Work Commissioner Chris Simpson ruled there was no evidence that the engineer acted recklessly or maliciously, nor that flight safety had been compromised at any point. The commissioner found no proof that the second job impaired his performance or caused workplace fatigue, according to The Sydney Morning Herald.
Simpson determined that Heston MRO breached basic disciplinary fairness by terminating the engineer without properly detailing the allegations or allowing him a right of reply. However, Simpson declined to order reinstatement, noting that the engineer's failure to formally disclose his work with Virgin Australia had damaged the mutual trust required for continued employment.
Heston MRO has indicated it plans to appeal the decision, maintaining that strict compliance with safety procedures remains paramount in the aviation industry.

items.title: Vietnam records a cancer death every five minutes, with most cases found too late
items.summary: Vietnam recorded 111,015 cancer deaths a year, an average of one roughly every five minutes, according to global estimates published in July by the International Agency for Research on Cancer.
items.body_text:
The agency's GLOBOCAN 2024 dataset, which covers 34 cancer types across 186 countries and territories, puts Vietnam's annual new cases at 177,404. It counts 404,153 people living with a diagnosis made within the previous five years.
Against roughly 100,000 new cases 16 years ago, incidence has risen 59% and deaths about 35%.
Deaths equal 63% of new diagnoses. That runs far above the 35-40% typical of the U.S., U.K. and Japan, where cancers are caught earlier, said Do Anh Tu, deputy director of K Hospital and chief of office of the Vietnam Cancer Society, at a July 31 conference on cancer prevention in Ho Chi Minh City. Many patients are diagnosed only after tumors have spread, he added.
Men accounted for 85,748 of the new cases but 63,167 of the deaths, a mortality-to-incidence ratio of 74%. Among women the figure was 52%.
Vietnamese men are diagnosed most often with lung, colorectal and liver cancer, while breast and thyroid cancer lead among women.
Breast cancer is now the most commonly diagnosed cancer in Vietnam overall, at 25,711 cases, ahead of lung cancer at 23,085. Lung cancer remains the leading killer, causing 21,340 deaths.
Vietnam has no complete national cancer registry, with data collected at a handful of large centers. The International Agency for Research on Cancer derives the country's mortality estimate by applying modeled ratios to its incidence figures rather than counting deaths directly.
Tu has called for a linked nationwide system, arguing that policy cannot be aimed accurately without one. Developed countries maintain full registries that let them detect shifts in the disease quickly.
For every 1,000 new cancer patients Vietnam has roughly 4.6 medical oncologists and 1.3 radiation oncologists, Tu said, with pathologists in shortest supply of all.
A lung cancer patient may spend close to VND170 million (US$6,500) on a year of treatment, and newer drugs are either absent from the insurance list or only partly reimbursed.
Some listed drugs are covered at only 50%, leaving patients to find VND30-60 million ($1,140-2,280) a month themselves, Nguyen Thi Thu Hang, deputy director of Ho Chi Minh City Social Insurance, told the conference. The city's insurance fund paid about VND4.86 trillion ($185 million) for cancer care across 1.19 million treatment visits last year.
Deputy Health Minister Nguyen Tri Thuc said cancer control has to run as a continuous chain from public communication and prevention through screening, treatment, nutrition and palliative care. Vietnam must stop waiting for patients to arrive at hospital already ill, he said.
"When on average a Vietnamese person dies of cancer roughly every five minutes, prevention and early detection are no longer a matter for the health sector alone," he said.
Politburo Resolution 72, issued in September 2025, commits the state to providing every citizen a free health check or screening at least once a year from 2026.
Thuc said Vietnam's specialized cancer treatment now approaches international standards but access remains uneven across regions.
About 40% of cancers are preventable through control of known risk factors, Tu said, citing tobacco, alcohol, obesity, physical inactivity and infection with HPV and the hepatitis B and C viruses.
He proposed building out screening in stages, beginning with cervical and breast cancer, where the evidence is strongest, then extending to colorectal and lung cancer.
Doctors say some cancers, including thyroid, breast, prostate and colon, carry five-year survival rates above 90% when caught early and treated promptly. Patients have remained stable for 10, 20 and 30 years after treatment.

items.title: Fake Thai ID card racket busted in Tak
items.summary: TAK - Police have arrested four Thais and seven Myanmar nationals in a crackdown on fraudulent Thai ID card issuance in this border province.
items.body_text:
TAK - Police have arrested four Thais and seven Myanmar nationals in a crackdown on fraudulent Thai ID card issuance in this border province.
A former assistant registrar for Mae Sot district is also being sought after it was found that as many as 700 people had obtained ID cards, reportedly paying between 40,000 and 100,000 baht each.
Seven of those arrested on Tuesday were Myanmar nationals holding illegally issued Thai ID cards.
The four Thais included two women, one of them a house owner who agreed to have her address used as the listed residence of the cardholders. An assistant registrar and a temporary employee of the Mae Sot municipal office were also held.
The arrests took place following raids on 25 locations in Mae Sot, according to deputy national police chief Pol Gen Samran Nualma.
He said the gang had illegally issued Thai ID cards beginning with “0” — the category for people who have no house registration records. Most people eligible for such cards live in border or remote areas or have been displaced.
The raids on Tuesday came a month after 11 people were arrested in a crackdown on illegal issuance of ID cards in Surat Thani province. Many of the holders were reportedly found to be from Mae Sot in Tak.
Detectives in Tak, meanwhile, are still looking for a former assistant registrar of Mae Sot municipality, identified only as Kit.
He was expelled from the civil service last year after his wife was linked to an arms-trafficking gang that supplied rocket-propelled grenades and ammunition to armed groups near the Thai-Myanmar border.
“Zero-number” ID cards are issued to non-citizens, stateless individuals or ethnic minorities legally residing in the country. Holders of have fundamental rights to education, medical treatment and employment in Thailand. After holding the cards for five years, they can travel freely in the country and apply for Thai citizenship.
Pol Gen Samran, who will take over as national police chief on Oct 1, said after the Surat Thani operation that authorities were cracking down on all forms of registration fraud.
These can include identity theft involving inactive registrants, false birth registrations, false marriages, and misuse of education entitlements, he said.
