items.title: Court acquits 'Aem Cyanide' of sixth murder charge
items.summary: The Criminal Court has acquitted convicted poisoner Sararat "Aem Cyanide" Rangsiwuthaporn of the sixth murder case brought against her.
items.body_text:
The Criminal Court has acquitted convicted poisoner Sararat "Aem Cyanide" Rangsiwuthaporn of the sixth murder case brought against her.
The court ruled on Tuesday that prosecutors had failed to prove beyond reasonable doubt that she murdered a close friend with cyanide-laced food in 2015.
It was the sixth case filed by public prosecutors from the Office of Criminal Litigation Region 6 against Sararat on charges of murder.
In this case, Sararat, 39, was charged with poisoning Monthathip "Sai" Khao-in with cyanide at the victim's luxury condominium in Bangkok's Thong Lor area on July 7, 2015.
Prosecutors alleged the motive was Sararat's desire to eliminate a debt owed to the victim. She denied the charge.
The court in its judgement said Sararat and Monthathip were close friends and moved in the same informal-loan circle, and that Sararat had borrowed money from her.
The court heard that Sararat had lost more than 30 million baht through online gambling. The victim lived in Canada and owned commercial rental properties in Sam Phran district of Nakhon Pathom. She entrusted Sararat with managing the properties.
On the day of the alleged crime Monthathip returned from Canada. Sararat and several other friends met her at Suvarnabhumi airport. The group stopped for rice porridge before going to the victim's condominium, where she later died.
The court said the autopsy report stated Monthathip died of heart failure, or possibly an underlying medical condition. The examining physician was unable to confirm that her death was the result of cyanide poisoning.
The court ruled that the prosecution's evidence contained uncertainties and there was no witness or direct evidence proving that Sararat had administered cyanide to the woman.
Under the principle that criminal convictions must be supported by evidence establishing guilt beyond reasonable doubt, the court said the benefit of doubt must be given to the defendant and dismissed the case.
Sararat was taken from the Central Women's Correctional Institution to the court to hear the judgement on Tuesday.
The court has previously delivered judgment in five other murder cases against her, imposing one death sentence and two life imprisonment sentences and acquitting her in two cases. With the latest acquittal, Sararat has now been cleared in three cases.
Prosecutors have filed a total of 15 cases against Sararat - 14 for murder and one attempted murder. Her involvement in a series of cyanide-related deaths attracted widespread public attention.
The Kanchanaburi native, dubbed "Aem Cyanide" after police found traces of cyanide in the victims' bodies, was arrested on April 25, 2023. She was pregnant when caught.
Police wrapped up their investigation into the criminal cases against her in June 2023, about the same time she miscarried during the fifth or sixth month of her pregnancy.

items.title: Why our leadership isn’t ready for AI (Part 4)
items.summary: It’s common to hear that employees are anxious about artificial intelligence. They’re worried about their roles, reluctant to use the tools. Quietly resistant, nodding through the training session, then returning to the old way of working the moment it ends.
items.body_text:
It’s common to hear that employees are anxious about artificial intelligence. They’re worried about their roles, reluctant to use the tools. Quietly resistant, nodding through the training session, then returning to the old way of working the moment it ends.
But this framing misses the point. The issue isn’t the technology. It’s what leaders have, and haven’t, said about it.
In most organisations, AI arrived without a story. No clarity on what changes, no clarity on what doesn’t, and no clarity on how success will be judged from here.
One day there was no AI tool. The next, there was a tool, a login, and a vague expectation to “start using it”, with no explanation of what that meant for people’s roles, their targets or their future.
Into that silence, people write their own story. And it’s rarely an encouraging one:
- Why would I share how I use this if it might replace me?
- If using the tool well makes me look replaceable, the safest move is to quietly under-report how much I rely on it.
- Why would I get faster if speed simply means more work for the same pay?
If efficiency gains are absorbed into a bigger workload with no corresponding recognition, why would anyone volunteer to become more efficient? What does good performance even look like now?
If the annual review still measures the old things, hours logged and tasks completed manually, while quietly expecting AI fluency, people are being judged by a standard nobody actually wrote down.
These aren’t unreasonable questions. They’re the ones leadership hasn’t answered yet.
At the same time, leaders are navigating their own uncertainty: new tools. new risks, boards asking difficult questions about return on investment, competitors making bold claims that may or may not be true.
Both groups are unsettled. Just in different ways — and mostly in silence, because admitting uncertainty out loud feels risky from either side.
Consider the difference between two organisations rolling out the same technology. In one, a leader stands in front of the team and says:
“I don’t fully know where this ends either. Here’s what I do know. Your value was never just the task. It was the judgement behind it. Here’s how we’re going to figure this out together, and here’s how I’ll support you while we do.”
The anxiety doesn’t disappear, but it becomes something people can work with.
In the other organisation, leadership says nothing meaningful. The tool arrives via a memo, and the rumour mill fills every gap.
Anxiety hardens into quiet resistance, knowledge gets hoarded, and eventually the organisation loses exactly the people it can least afford to lose.
The challenge isn’t managing AI anxiety. It’s designing a leadership narrative that is clear enough for people to bring their real questions instead of their private fears.
That means naming the difficult truths — some roles will change, some tasks will disappear — instead of pretending everything stays the same.
It also means being explicit about what remains uniquely valuable: judgement, relationships, accountability, and the things AI genuinely cannot do.
Fear rarely announces itself directly. It appears first in small, difficult-to-trace behaviours:
- a slower response when someone is asked to share a prompt library;
- a reluctance to document how work actually gets done;
- a preference for keeping knowledge in one person’s head instead of a shared system.
None of these appear on an engagement survey. All of them are among the earliest and most honest signals leadership will receive.
By the time fear shows up in an exit interview — “I didn’t feel there was a place for me here anymore” — the organisation has already lost months of quiet disengagement because nobody was looking for it. And nobody created a safe way for people to talk about it earlier.
Because the future of work won’t be defined by how advanced AI becomes. It will be defined by whether leaders were honest about what AI means for people, early enough to matter, and specific enou

items.title: Suspected heatstroke kills three lions at Japan zoo
items.summary: TOKYO, Aug 4 — Three lions from a Tokyo zoo have died from suspected heatstroke and others are under treatment, a...
items.body_text:
TOKYO, Aug 4 — Three lions from a Tokyo zoo have died from suspected heatstroke and others are under treatment, a spokeswoman said Tuesday, with the big cats struggling with high levels of humidity.
Japan sweltered through its hottest summer on record last year and parts of the country have hit 40 degrees Celsius in recent weeks, qualifying for the new designation “cruelly hot day”.
Since mid-July, 10 of the 16 lions in Tama Zoological Park have suffered symptoms such as “loss of appetite and decreased activity”, and three lionesses died, the zoo said in a statement.
One passed away on Tuesday, another died on Friday, and the third died on Sunday, it said.
“According to our veterinarian, the cause of the deaths is suspected to be heatstroke” as dehydration and multiple organ failure were observed, a spokeswoman told AFP.
“Even though lions are thought to be resistant to heat, zoo keepers have been strengthening countermeasures to cope with Japan’s summer heat in recent years. Heat here comes with high humidity; that is different from heat with dry air in Africa,” she said.
“But this summer, heat arrived suddenly after the rainy season was over” in late July, she said.
“We are strengthening measures against the heat (further), sprinkling water, improving ventilation and installing spot air conditioners,” she said.
Several lions are still being treated, she added.
Close to 18,600 people were taken to hospital for heatstroke between July 20 and 26, with 45 of them pronounced dead on arrival, according to the fire and disaster management agency.
Japan experiences about 1,300 heat-related deaths annually and is aiming to halve that number by 2030.
Scientists say human-induced climate change is increasing the frequency and intensity of extreme heat events in Japan and elsewhere.
Its highest recorded temperature was registered on August 5, 2025, at 41.8C in Isesaki, north of Tokyo.
Authorities have adjusted the timings of a string of cultural and sporting events in recent years because of the heat, including the World Cosplay Summit in Nagoya, which held its last summer edition last weekend. — AFP

items.title: Forest fire spreads in Dutch nature reserve
items.summary: THE HAGUE, Aug 4 — Firefighters are rushing to contain a forest blaze in the southeast of the Netherlands tha...
items.body_text:
THE HAGUE, Aug 4 — Firefighters are rushing to contain a forest blaze in the southeast of the Netherlands that spread overnight to engulf 100 hectares today, authorities said.
It was the latest in a string of wildfires to hit western Europe, following deadly heatwaves that have dried up riverbeds and vegetation — extreme weather events scientists have linked to human-made climate change.
The fire started around yesterday noon in a nature reserve near the village of Oostrum in the Limburg province, close to the border with Germany.
The blaze spread to 100 hectares as of early today and was still not under control, provincial authorities said on their website.
The winds kept changing direction and sped up the fire’s spread, a regional safety spokesperson told the ANP news agency.
Around 300 emergency workers took part in containing the blaze overnight, and firefighting helicopters were set to resume operations on Tuesday morning, authorities said.
A nearby campsite was evacuated, and trains passing through the area were suspended.
“Because of the drought, fire can spread quickly in nature reserves,” the provincial authorities said, without specifying the cause of the fire.
European countries are facing a major drought, marked by dried-up rivers, water restrictions and devastating forest fires, following an unprecedented heat wave in June.
Human-fuelled climate change has accelerated moisture loss from soil, lakes and rivers, heightening the risk of extreme droughts, scientists from World Weather Attribution warned last month. — AFP

items.title: Nippon Steel raises FY2026 profit forecast on strong US Steel earnings
items.body_text:
Nippon Steel raises FY2026 profit forecast on strong US Steel earnings
TOKYO, Aug 4 : Japan's top steelmaker Nippon Steel on Tuesday raised its full-year net profit forecast by 32 per cent to 290 billion yen ($1.84 billion), citing stronger earnings at U.S. Steel amid a firmer U.S. steel market.
• Nippon Steel posted a 75.30 billion yen net profit for the April-June first quarter, compared with a 195.83 billion yen net loss a year earlier, when it booked a hefty one-off loss related to the sale of its stake in the AM/NS Calvert joint venture.
• "U.S. Steel drove our group earnings," Nippon Steel Chief Financial Officer Takahiko Iwai told a news conference, adding that measures to improve quality and operational efficiencies at U.S. Steel after its acquisition also contributed to higher profits at the U.S. unit.
• Nippon Steel raised its underlying business profit forecast for U.S. Steel in the financial year to March 2027 to 180 billion yen or more, from its May prediction of 100 billion yen or more.
• It also raised its full-year assumption for the U.S. hot-rolled coil market by $100 to $1,000-$1,100 per short ton in light of the recent rise in prices.
• CFO Iwai said an expected increase in inventory valuation gains, driven by the weak yen against the U.S. dollar and rising raw material costs, also contributed to the upward revision of the profit forecast.
• Meanwhile, the Middle East conflict reduced first-quarter earnings by 25 billion yen and is expected to have a 60 billion yen negative impact for the full year, Iwai said.
• As profits from domestic operations remain stagnant, Nippon Steel aims to pass on higher raw material and fuel costs to customers going forward, Iwai said. "The Japanese government has finally imposed anti-dumping measures," he said, adding that if measures can help curb imports of cheap steel, it may become possible to see stronger domestic prices.

items.title: Hong Kong June retail sales rise 4.6%, seem support from visitors growth
items.body_text:
Hong Kong June retail sales rise 4.6%, seem support from visitors growth
HONG KONG, Aug 4 : Hong Kong's retail sales jumped 4.6 per cent in value in June from a year earlier to HK$31.5 billion ($4.02 billion), marking the 14th month of gains, government data showed on Tuesday.
• In May, retail sales jumped 7.9 per cent on the year.
• In volume terms, June retail sales increased 2.3 per cent from a year earlier, compared with a 4.8 per cent rise in May.
• The sector remained on a positive trajectory in June and growth was broad-based across many retail categories.
• For the first six months of 2026, the total retail sales value increased by 9.6 per cent from a year earlier, while retail sales volume rose 7.2 per cent.
• "Continued economic expansion, rising local incomes, and a steady increase in inbound visitors are expected to provide support to the sector," a government spokesperson said, while noting that global conditions constituted a risk for local consumption, which the government would monitor.
• Visitor arrivals in June rose 6.9 per cent year-on-year to 3.72 million, data from the Hong Kong Tourism Board showed. The number of mainland Chinese visitors surged 10.5 per cent to 2.88 million.

items.title: Japan may not have intervened in FX market on Monday despite yen's surge, BOJ data suggests
items.body_text:
Japan may not have intervened in FX market on Monday despite yen's surge, BOJ data suggests
TOKYO, Aug 4 : Japan may not have intervened in the currency market on Monday, central bank data indicated, despite a sudden surge in the yen that led traders to anticipate a third straight day of intervention.
The Bank of Japan's projection for money market conditions for Wednesday points to a shortfall of 3.38 trillion yen ($21.43 billion) versus brokerage forecasts of a shortfall of between 2.32 trillion and 2.6 trillion.
Tuesday's data did not indicate a large outflow in the central bank's current account balances. Outsized outflows are typically interpreted as correlating with the size of any intervention.
The yen suddenly leapt in the Asian morning on Monday to hit 155.20 per dollar, its strongest in about three months, as traders kept on alert for further intervention by authorities.
The yen's jump came after Japan's finance ministry confirmed it had engaged in joint yen-buying intervention with the United States on Friday.
On Monday, Bank of Japan data showed Tokyo may have spent as much as $36.58 billion to buy yen to strengthen the currency.
Friday's joint intervention followed Tokyo's solo intervention worth up to $.58.97 billion in New York markets a day earlier.
($1 = 157.8500 yen)

items.title: Climate change set to redraw Africa’s malaria map, study finds
items.summary: Malaria killed an estimated 579,000 people in Africa in 2024, about three-quarters of them children under five.
items.body_text:
Climate change set to redraw Africa’s malaria map, study finds
CAPE TOWN – Climate change is poised to expose more people to malaria in cooler parts of Africa by the end of the century, with cases potentially rising as much as 20 per cent in coastal southern Africa, according to a new study published in Nature.
By 2050, rising temperatures are projected to expand the range of malaria-carrying mosquitoes into cooler parts of southern and eastern Africa, increasing cases by about 5 per cent in the East African highlands – including parts of Kenya and Ethiopia – as well as in Angola, Zambia and eastern South Africa, the study found.
The reverse is expected in some of Africa’s hottest regions, where transmission is projected to fall by about 5 per cent in countries including Nigeria, Burkina Faso and Mali. In parts of the Sahel, conditions may become too hot for mosquitoes to survive, potentially eliminating the disease altogether.
In South Africa, far more children are at risk of contracting the disease, with three north-eastern provinces most vulnerable, said Christopher Trisos, director of the Climate Risk Lab at the University of Cape Town and a co-author of the study.
“South Africa and its global health partners need to prepare local malaria control and health systems now for this growing risk,” he said.
Malaria killed an estimated 579,000 people in Africa in 2024, about three-quarters of them children under five, according to the World Health Organization.
“Our study shows that climate change’s influence on childhood malaria risk is not uniform across Africa, underscoring the difficulty and complexity of adaptation and health planning across the continent,” said Romaric Odoulami, co-author and researcher at the African Climate and Development Initiative.
Still, the researchers said the projected increase is not inevitable.
Limiting global warming to 2 deg C would prevent about five more malaria cases per 1,000 children in southern Africa, with even greater benefits in the East African highlands, according to the study.
Efforts to cut emissions must be matched by stronger malaria surveillance and control, particularly in southern and eastern Africa, where there is less experience tackling it, the study found. Bloomberg

            MAC to train ‘united front’ awarenessFOREWARNED IS FOREARMED: As China subsidizes more and more student visits, the MAC aims to train more Taiwanese to view ‘united front’ efforts critically
  - By Huang Ching-hsuan and William Hetherington / Staff reporter, with staff writer and CNA
 The Mainland Affairs Council (MAC) yesterday said it would work with schools to reinforce awareness about China and the risks of traveling there after a government watchdog warned about increasingly one-sided cross-strait educational exchanges. According to a statement by the Control Yuan last Wednesday, China has expanded efforts to attract Taiwanese students through scientific research programs, talent competitions and other exchange activities in the past few years. The number of Taiwanese students participating in such programs far exceeds the number of Chinese students taking part in educational exchanges in Taiwan. The Chinese and Taiwanese flags are pictured in a graphic.Photo: CNA Control Yuan members Lin Wen-cheng (林文程) and Tien Chiu-chin (田秋堇) issued a report saying Beijing has long targeted young Taiwanese with its “united front” strategy, with those efforts extending from elementary-school students all the way to university students. Following the easing of COVID-19 restrictions in 2023, the number of Taiwanese students traveling to China for exchanges increased sharply, the report said. The number of university students participating in exchanges with China rose from 2,196 in 2022 to 5,745 last year. Among high-school and vocational-school students, the number increased from 676 to 1,161 over the same period. Junior-high school participation rose from 0 to 1,021 students, while elementary-school participation increased from 38 to 1,045. The number of accompanying teachers also nearly doubled, from 661 to 1,281. Soldiers practice marksmanship in an undated photograph.Photo: Taipei Times By contrast, the number of Chinese students participating in MAC-organized activities in Taiwan declined each year, dwindling from 76 in 2022 to just 16 last year. The report found that although the Ministry of Education (MOE) established an online registration platform in 2019 requiring schools to report educational exchange activities in China, underreporting remains widespread. In some cases, teachers independently recruited students for trips to China without informing the school, leading parents to mistakenly believe the activities had been officially organized by the schools, the report said. The Control Yuan’s Internal Administration and Indigenous Affairs Committee and Education and Culture Committee approved the report on July 21 and called on the MAC and the MOE to review and improve oversight of cross-strait educational exchanges. The MAC said it would continue working with the MOE to improve the exchange registration platform and strengthen related oversight mechanisms. It plans to assist schools at all levels by using social media, news conferences, student camps and other channels to educate students about the risks of traveling to China and issues that should consider when participating in cross-strait academic exchanges. In response to Beijing’s efforts to extend “united front” work to younger Taiwanese, the MAC said it is cooperating with the MOE, university general education centers and academic organizations to improve education about China and students’ understanding of the Chinese Communist Party’s “united front” activities. The council said it would investigate reports of civic organizations recruiting students to participate in activities in China. If potential legal or regulatory violations are identified, the cases would be referred to the appropriate authorities or handled through interagency coordination, it said. items.title: Bureau of Labor Funds reports healthy returns
items.body_text:
- 
            Bureau of Labor Funds reports healthy returnsSOLID GAINS: Driven by the AI craze, the funds managed by the bureau, led by the Labor Pension Fund, saw robust returns in the first six months
  - Staff writer, with CNA
 Labor funds administered by the Bureau of Labor Funds reported a return of 28.46 percent in the first half of this year, driven by a boom in the global equity market amid demand for artificial intelligence (AI) products, data released by the bureau showed yesterday. The accumulated gains in the value of assets in the funds’ portfolios and income on investment was about NT$2.2 trillion (US$67.82 billion) from January to June, after these funds posted NT$77.1 billion in gains in June, the bureau said in a statement. As of the end of June, the combined value of the funds the bureau manages — including the Labor Pension Fund, the Labor Retirement Fund, the Labor Insurance Fund and the Employment Insurance Fund — stood at NT$8.896 trillion, bureau data showed. The Bureau of Labor Funds sign is pictured at its office in Taipei in an undated photograph.Photo: Lee Chin-hui, Taipei Times The six-month gains of NT$2.2 trillion translated into a rate of return of 28.46 percent during the January-to-June period, up from 27.7 percent during the January-to-May period, the bureau said. Global equity markets posted initial losses in June amid tensions in the Middle East, which pushed up oil prices, but then geopolitics improved to smooth out market sentiment, the bureau said. Thanks to sound fundamentals, Taiwan’s market continued to receive a boost from strong AI demand, it said. In the first six months of the year, the TAIEX, the Taiwan Stock Exchange’s benchmark index, soared 59.25 percent and the MSCI World Index rose 11.25 percent, while the Bloomberg Barclays Global Aggregate Bond Index dropped 0.21 percent. The bureau said 54.37 percent of its investments were made overseas from January to June, while the remaining 45.63 percent were invested in the domestic market. The labor funds managed by the bureau are mainly aimed at aiding workers. The Labor Pension Fund collects contributions from employers and employees every month and are managed by the bureau to boost asset value to help workers save and invest for retirement. The value of assets in the Labor Pension Fund, launched in 2015, was NT$5.796 trillion as of the end of June, the highest among all labor funds, and its rate of return for the January-to-June period stood at 28.19 percent, the bureau said. The Labor Retirement Fund, which has been in place since 1984, had about NT$1.16 trillion in assets as of the end of June, with a rate of return of 40.74 percent for the six months, it added. Meanwhile, the Bureau of Public Service Pension Fund said yesterday that the Public Service Pension Fund, which the bureau manages, recorded NT$331.08 billion in gains in the first six months of this year, equal to a rate of return of 25.03 percent.

items.title: NPS to begin charging visitors to some national parks
items.body_text:
- 
            NPS to begin charging visitors to some national parks
  - By Huang Yi-ching, Wu Liang-yi and Esme Yeh / Staff reporters, with staff writer
 The National Park Service (NPS) is planning to charge visitors to many of the 100 Peaks of Taiwan as early as next year in order to fund environmental conservation and park operations. It has drafted amendments to the National Park Act (國家公園法) to establish a national park fund and charge visitors applying for an entry permit to ecologically protected areas of any of the nine national parks or the Shoushan National Nature Park (壽山國家自然公園). The draft would be sent to the Executive Yuan for review early next year, and could be implemented by the end of next year, sources said. Hikers are pictured in undated photograph.Photo: Wu Liang-yi, Taipei Times The NPS sought the regulatory change after the Control Yuan last year said the Ministry of the Interior should consider charging entry fees, collecting donations and covering facility maintenance costs, based on the “user pays” principle, they added. About 200,000 applications have been received to hike in one of the three alpine national parks — Yushan (玉山), Shei-Pa (雪霸) and Taroko (太魯閣). The draft amendments outline the legal basis and sources of revenue of the national park fund and how it would be spent. Sources of revenue would include government budgets, interest, conservation fees, operating income, fines or forfeits, donations and climate adaptation grants, according to the bill. According to the draft amendments, funds would be on environmental conservation and education, recreation services, international exchanges, volunteer incentives, and other allowances or compensation. Most areas within the three alpine national parks are ecologically protected areas that would charge visitors for entry permits under the pending regulatory change, including 76 of the 100 Peaks of Taiwan, as well as dozens of hiking trails. Entry permits to such protected areas are currently free and receive hundreds of thousands of applications every year, but there is a limit on the daily number of visitors allowed into these areas given the limited environmental carrying capacity. Kenting National Park’s (墾丁國家公園) Longkeng (龍坑) and Nanrenshan (南仁山) and the Yangmingshan National Park’s (陽明山國家公園) Lujiaokeng (鹿角坑) and Huangzuishan (磺嘴山) are ecologically protected areas with many visitors. At present, only a few facilities of national parks, such as parking lots, the Yangming Shuwu (陽明書屋) building, the Oluanpi Park (鵝鑾鼻公園) and the Guangao Lodge (觀高山屋), have fees that flow to the national treasury. Mountain cabins built down the line would also charge fees, such as the one on the Qilai (奇萊) ridgeline within the Taroko National Park, expected to enter service this year. The fees would go to the national park fund if the bill is passed, sources said, adding that the draft stiffens fines and penalties for certain crimes at national parks. For example, burning trees or vegetation would be punishable by imprisonment for up to a year, short-term detention, or a fine of up to NT$1 million. The penalty could be increased by 50 percent if the fire results in a disaster, it added. NPS Deputy Director Chang Wei-chuan (張維銓) said the service has completed the draft but has yet to officially discuss the fee amounts, how to charge them and whether the rates should vary by region. The draft bill was formulated on advice from administrative agencies, civic groups, academics and experts, he said. It would be sent to the ministry for review in October and then sent to the Executive Yuan and the Legislative Yuan for review, he added. National Pingtung University of Science and Technology forestry assistant professor Wu Hsing-ju (吳幸如) said it is not unusual for national parks to charge an entry fee, which Taiwan could have done earlier, in line with international practices. items.title: HSBC resumes buyback after big profit jump in first half of 2026
items.summary: British Banking giant HSBC said Tuesday it would buy back up to US$1 billion of shares after a big jump in profits in the first half of 2026. The jump in profits was due to “growth in banking net interest income and higher fee and other income”, HSBC said in its earnings report, adding that […]
items.body_text:
British Banking giant HSBC said Tuesday it would buy back up to US$1 billion of shares after a big jump in profits in the first half of 2026.
The jump in profits was due to “growth in banking net interest income and higher fee and other income”, HSBC said in its earnings report, adding that the profit in banking increased by US$1.4 billion.
“HSBC is becoming the stronger bank we set out to build. We are executing our strategic priorities with pace, precision and discipline,” CEO Georges Elhedery added in a statement.
Profit attributable to shareholders rose around 27 percent to US$14.6 billion in the six months to June, up from US$11.5 billion a year earlier.
Pre-tax profit increased 23 percent on-year to US$19.5 billion.
In a sign of confidence, HSBC said it would proceed with a share buy-back of up to US$1 billion, with its board having approved a second interim dividend of US$0.10 per share.
“We also intend to initiate a share buy-back of up to $1 billion, which we expect to complete by our third quarter 2026 results announcement,” it said in the filing.
The bank said it was resuming repurchases after it paused them following its move to take full ownership of Hang Seng Bank.
However, good news was partly offset by expected credit losses of US$2.4 billion — US$400 million higher than the first half of 2025.
The bank said it lost US$400 million in a fraud case involving a British financial sponsor, and US$200 million in Hong Kong’s commercial property sector.
In recent weeks, HSBC has announced a series of deals to sell off business units, as under Elhedery, the lender has been carrying out a global restructuring to focus on its core markets.
HSBC’s share price has broken through its all-time high this month, with shares in Hong Kong trading above HK$160 each.

items.title: More than 1,000 drivers apply to take written tests for new ride-hailing regulatory regime
items.summary: More than 1,000 drivers have applied to take written tests required under new regulations for providing ride-hailing services such as Uber, the Transport Department has said. The department’s announcement was made on Monday as some of the legal provisions under the new laws for regulating ride-hailing services came into effect. Under the regulatory regime, the […]
items.body_text:
More than 1,000 drivers have applied to take written tests required under new regulations for providing ride-hailing services such as Uber, the Transport Department has said.
The department’s announcement was made on Monday as some of the legal provisions under the new laws for regulating ride-hailing services came into effect.
Under the regulatory regime, the government now requires ride-hailing drivers to to hold a specific licence, for which passing the test is a pre-requisite.
The test for taxi drivers has been merged with the new test, meaning both ride-hailing and taxi drivers will sit for the same exam.
The first batch of the 45-minute written exams will be held in mid-September, the Transport Department told local media. Licences will be issued from November.
The ride-hailing services laws, passed last October, stipulate that drivers convicted of carrying passengers for hire or reward without a permit will be disqualified from driving for between 12 months and three years.
They also face a fine of up to HK$10,000 for a first offence.
Before the new laws, the offence carried a maximum penalty of HK$5,000 for a first offence and no driving disqualification.
Speaking on an RTHK programme, Roundtable lawmaker Mark Chong said that ride-hailing drivers may continue to operate, believing the risk of enforcement is low.
He suggested they pivot to working as taxi drivers before obtaining their licences later this year.
New legislation
Ride-hailing services have grown in popularity over the years amid increasing public frustration over taxi service standards.
Uber was first introduced to Hong Kong in 2014, but ride-hailing vehicles have always operated in a legal grey area with no dedicated legislation.
The city’s taxi industry has long accused ride-hailing platforms of impacting cab drivers’ livelihoods.
Besides ride-hailing drivers, ride-hailing platforms must also obtain a licence under the new rules.
From next August, when the regulatory regime comes into full force, operators of ride-hailing platforms that do not have a licence will face a maximum fine of HK$1 million and up to a year in jail.
Hong Kong has set a ride-hailing permit cap of 10,000 vehicles. After the government announced the cap, Uber said a survey of riders found many were concerned about longer wait times and increased fares.
Uber, as well as mainland Chinese ride-hailing platform Didi, have said they are preparing their licence applications.

items.title: Hikers draw scrutiny after entering Hong Kong reservoir spillway during flood discharge for photos
items.summary: Two hikers have drawn scrutiny after entering the spillway of a reservoir in Yuen Long during a flood discharge and posing for photos, prompting a government department to investigate. The Water Supplies Department (WSD) said on Tuesday it was “very concerned” about recent viral social media footage showing two hikers entering the spillway at Ho […]
items.body_text:
Two hikers have drawn scrutiny after entering the spillway of a reservoir in Yuen Long during a flood discharge and posing for photos, prompting a government department to investigate.
The Water Supplies Department (WSD) said on Tuesday it was “very concerned” about recent viral social media footage showing two hikers entering the spillway at Ho Pui Reservoir.
The video, filmed on an unknown date, shows a woman climbing down a ladder to the spillway, where another man is already standing. In the video, the woman is holding onto the ladder and extending her arm, appearing to pose for pictures as the floodwaters gushed behind her.
A woman can be heard warning the pair: “Don’t go down further, it’s very dangerous… Aren’t you afraid of the water discharge? You could be swept away to who knows where.”
In an emailed reply to HKFP, the WSD said it would investigate the incident and prosecute if there was sufficient evidence.
The WSD said that when the water level in a reservoir approaches its capacity, the overflow system will drain the excess water, causing water flow in nearby and downstream water facilities to rise sharply.
“Hikers should not enter water facilities without approval to avoid accidents,” the department said.
The WSD noted that unauthorised entry into water facilities could violate the Waterworks Ordinance, with a maximum fine of HK$50,000 and up to two years’ imprisonment upon conviction. Damaging water facilities is also an offence, with a maximum fine of HK$25,000.
The department added that it would step up patrols at reservoirs and explore expanding smart surveillance systems to improve security.
The WSD also posted a warning on social media on Tuesday, urging hikers not to trespass into water facilities.
Hong Kong has seen exceptionally rainy weather in recent weeks.
Last month was Hong Kong’s second-rainiest July on record, with 20 amber rainstorm warnings and five red rainstorm warnings issued.
The total monthly rainfall was 790.3 mm, the Hong Kong Observatory said in a Facebook post on Sunday. The figure is double the normal rainfall in July of 385.8mm.

items.body_text:
After Ref Cam lights up World Cup, what’s next for Lenovo’s AI tech in football?
Chinese multinational raised the bar for television coverage, now bosses eye bringing their expertise to the game’s mainstream
Having created one of the runaway television hits of this summer’s Fifa World Cup, Lenovo is plotting to up the AI ante for the women’s version next year in Brazil.
In addition to building digital twins for all 1,248 players to enhance semi-automated offside technology for the 2026 finals, labelled “the first AI World Cup”, and rolling out an analytical tool aimed at “democratising football”, the tech giants were responsible for Ref Cam, which made its major tournament debut in North America.
Ken Wong, executive vice-president of Lenovo, said the company was “exploring with Fifa what else we can bring” for future tournaments, as well as looking at how they can bring the technology “into the football mainstream”.
“These technologies are only available for Fifa right now, but we want to replicate them so they’re available for everyone,” added Wong, who also serves as president of Lenovo’s solutions and services group.
In the six-to-nine months before the World Cup, Lenovo was tasked with considerably reducing a 40-second wait time for broadcast-quality Ref Cam images.
“There’s a juicy story behind it,” said Wong, talking exclusively to the South China Morning Post in Atlanta.

items.body_text:
您即將進入之新聞內容 需滿18歲 方可瀏覽。
健康網》魚刺哥連2天遭同一條魚刺卡進急診 醫警：做這些事恐更糟
〔健康頻道／綜合報導〕魚刺卡喉時，有些人第一時間可能會急著吞飯、喝醋，希望把魚刺推下或軟化。基隆長庚醫院肝膽腸胃科醫師錢政弘分享，日前急診遇到1名30多歲男性，連續2天竟因吃同一條魚卡到魚刺、2度接受胃鏡取出。提醒會卡住的魚刺往往又硬又尖，繼續進食反而可能讓魚刺卡得更深。此外，單靠喝醋也無法「化骨」，若出現吞嚥疼痛或持續異物感，應停止進食並盡速就醫。
錢政弘於臉書粉專「錢政弘 胃腸肝膽科醫師」發文表示，前述這名患者日前因吃魚不慎吞下魚刺，感覺卡在胸部相當不舒服，急診照會胃腸科值班醫師，緊急以胃鏡取出卡在食道的魚刺。由於魚刺已造成食道撕裂傷，特別叮嚀患者，返家後不要吃刺激或太硬的食物，以免傷口擴大。
錢政弘說，未料隔天晚上同一時間，這名男子又到急診報到，表示自己再度因吃魚，感覺魚刺又卡住。經胃鏡檢查，果然在食道發現1根約1.5公分且相當尖銳的魚刺，最後順利取出。他指出，同一個人、同一個時間、因同一條魚卡刺，算是急診史上頭一回，也引來醫護質疑。對此，男子解釋，因為覺得前一天那條魚沒吃完很可惜，雖然已經很小心吃，沒想到仍再次中招。
魚刺卡喉6點處理原則
錢政弘提醒，遇到魚刺卡住，處置時，應注意以下6點：
●立刻停止進食：張嘴照鏡子或請旁人用手電筒照看喉嚨狀況，有些可能看得到、夾得出，若卡在喉嚨看得到，儘速找耳鼻喉科處理。
●出現深處異物感應就醫：若魚刺已吞下去，感覺胸口或喉嚨深處持續有異物感、吞嚥痛，甚至無法吃東西，代表魚刺已經到食道，需找腸胃科照胃鏡夾出。
●疼痛處不等於卡住位置：疼痛位置與實際卡住位置未必相同，就醫時，應主動說明「吃了什麼魚、什麼時候吃、痛在哪」，讓醫師檢查判斷。
●X光不一定看得到：X光檢查幾乎是看不到魚刺，偵測率僅11.24%，若症狀未緩解，仍應進一步做電腦斷層或胃鏡檢查。
●不要吞菜硬推：不要想靠吞菜、饅頭或大口白飯，試圖把魚刺推下去。通常會卡住的魚刺往往又硬又尖，此時若再吃東西，反而可能讓魚刺卡得更深。
●喝醋無法快速軟化：魚骨若要酥脆到能咬碎，需要大量的醋加上長時間小火慢煨料理。一般料理的魚刺，無法單靠幾口醋停留數秒軟化。
錢政弘提醒，當不慎吞食魚刺時，若異物鈍小、吞嚥無症狀，可先觀察；但若吞嚥疼痛或有異物感，千萬不要再進食，建議應儘快就醫。

items.body_text:
成本推升房價是假象？數據曝這縣市房價狂漲166%「遠超成本4倍」
數據顯示，營造成本確實會推升房價，但並非是所有城市房價上漲的唯一原因。（記者朱語蕎攝）
近年房價持續上漲，不少人認為主因是缺工、缺料，加上原物料價格上漲，導致營造成本節節攀升。不過，若把房價和營造成本放在相同期間比較，就會發現，成本上升並不能完全解釋各城市房價的漲幅。
好時價依據清華安富房價指數及行政院主計總處營造工程物價指數分析，在2012年8月至2026年6月，營造工程物價指數累計上漲40.50%。同一期間，六都房價以台南上漲166.83%居冠，其次為台中148.07%、高雄130.52%、桃園121.89%、新北68.99%，台北則上漲40.71%。
若直接比較房價與營造成本的差距，可以發現台北幾乎與成本同步，房價僅比營造成本多上漲0.21個百分點；但其他五都則高出28至126個百分點不等。其中，台南房價漲幅更是營造成本的4倍以上。
這代表營造成本確實會推升房價，但並不是所有城市房價上漲的唯一原因。
好時價觀察，房價與營造成本的差距在疫情期間更加明顯，在2020年1月至2023年12月，營造工程物價指數上漲22.74%；同期六都房價以台南上漲65.89%最多，台中54.49%、桃園53.38%、高雄52.92%、新北33.25%，台北則上漲22.85%。
換句話說，疫情期間台北房價幾乎與營造成本同步，但台南、台中、桃園及高雄的房價漲幅，都比成本高出30個百分點以上，其中台南更高出43個百分點。這也反映，除了成本增加之外，當時低利率、資金充沛、產業投資、重大建設以及市場對房價持續上漲的預期，也共同推升了房價。
營造成本確實是房價的重要支撐，但不是所有城市房價上漲的共同答案。未來住宅政策若能依各城市房價偏離成本的程度及市場特性，採取因地制宜的措施，才能真正回應不同地區的居住需求，也避免「成本上漲」成為房價全面上漲的唯一理由。
值得注意的是，桃園、台中、台南與高雄的房價漲幅約為營造成本的3至4倍，建議政府除了關注營造成本外，更應檢視產業投資、公共建設、土地價格及預售屋交易等因素，並透過增加可建築土地、提供社會住宅，降低市場過熱風險。

items.body_text:
史庫柏爾。（美聯社）
〔體育中心／綜合報導〕道奇日前重磅交易來老虎2屆塞揚王牌史庫柏爾（Tarik Skubal），目標直指3連霸，不過《今日美國》記者皮特（Josh Peter）卻以「為何道奇交易來史庫柏爾還不夠」為題，撰文點出衛冕軍的弱點。
皮特開門見山直言，史庫柏爾的降臨，並不能保證道奇能夠3連霸，除非他還能守右外野和游擊，還能在打擊區展現穩定破壞力。目前道奇打線存在重大問題，其中之一就是右外野手塔克（Kyle Tucker），季前簽下4年2.4億美元大約的他，本季回報給道奇的打擊三圍僅.237/.335/.368。
另一人則是游擊手貝茲（Mookie Betts），今年他曾受傷勢影響，表現持續低潮，目前打擊三圍僅.229/.286/.399，與生涯.288/.365/.509有巨大差距。皮特直言，33歲的貝茲已經難以看出昔日8屆全明星的模樣，而他的12年3.65億美元合約，還有7年要走。皮特直言，道奇最大的問題不是在錢，是在得分，強如史庫柏爾也同樣需要火力支援，但目前來看，塔克和貝茲都是道奇的負擔。
此外，雖然史庫柏爾能更強化道奇先發，但目前這套鬼神輪值裡傷兵一堆，大谷翔平自7月3日以來就沒有再登板投球，也沒人能保證葛拉斯諾（Tyler Glasnow）和史奈爾（Blake Snell）能在季後賽開始前恢復到最佳狀態；除了先發輪值，主戰捕手史密斯（Will Smith）也因傷持續缺陣，皮特諷刺，如果史庫柏爾能靠一己之力解決上述弱點，那這些當然就完全不成問題。

More than 60 North Korean defectors who lived near the country’s nuclear test site were found to have chromosomal abnormalities, though researchers have yet to confirm a direct link to nuclear testing, according to South Korea’s Ministry of Unification. 
Radiation exposure tests conducted annually between 2017 and 2025 on 214 North Korean defectors from areas near the Punggye-ri nuclear test site found that 64 people, or 29.9%, showed genetic abnormalities that could be linked to past radiation exposure, a spokesperson from Seoul’s Unification Ministry told NK News on Monday, citing data from state-funded National Radiation Emergency Medical Center.

Russian assistance does not appear to have directly strengthened North Korea’s military yet, but the rapid and expanding cooperation between the two countries could boost Pyongyang’s armed forces over the medium to long term, Japan’s Ministry of Defense (MOD) warned in its latest white paper released Tuesday.
The annual report on regional security developments and the activities of the MOD and Self-Defense Forces described North Korea’s military as posing “an even more grave and imminent threat” to Japan’s national security than ever.
The MOD identified deepening Russia-North Korea military cooperation as one of the most significant developments affecting regional security.

items.title: Pyongyang busts luxury smuggling ring selling to elite wives
items.summary: A special task force in Pyongyang has arrested the manager of a foreign currency store and a trade official accused of smuggling luxury brands such as Chanel and Rolex into the country and secretly selling them to the wives of high-ranking officials, in a case that has since widened into a bribery scandal implicating local […]
items.body_text:
A special task force in Pyongyang has arrested the manager of a foreign currency store and a trade official accused of smuggling luxury brands such as Chanel and Rolex into the country and secretly selling them to the wives of high-ranking officials, in a case that has since widened into a bribery scandal implicating local police officials.
A Daily NK source in Pyongyang said Tuesday that the Special Joint Group for Eradicating Non-Socialist Practices, a task force organized under central party instructions to monitor illicit foreign currency dealing and luxury consumption trends in the capital, raided a foreign currency store in Pyongyang’s Taesong district on July 11 after months of internal investigation, catching the manager and a trade official on the scene.
According to the source, the store manager had built out informal channels to bring in luxury goods such as Chanel and Rolex products to meet demand among Pyongyang’s elite, then sold them to the wives of high-ranking officials, pocketing substantial amounts of foreign currency in the process. A trade official who colluded with the manager reportedly used his position, which gave him authority over customs clearance procedures, to help smuggle high-end luxury items into a secret storage room inside the shop.
When the task force raided the store in mid-July, officers found bags of undeclared dollar and yuan cash bundles that hadn’t been hidden in time, along with smuggled goods that had never been entered into the store’s books, and confiscated everything on the spot. The manager and the trade official, both present at the time, were taken into custody without any chance to resist, the source said.
Bribery scandal widens to police officials
As the task force investigated the case, it uncovered a pattern of corruption among Taesong district police department officials who had been protecting the store manager in exchange for bribes, and the fallout from the case has continued to grow since, according to the source. Task force members reportedly raided the Taesong district police department itself, seizing documents and arresting officials on the spot, and word of the case has since spread across Pyongyang, unsettling the capital’s elite circles.
“After this surprise crackdown at the heart of Pyongyang, power organs are in considerable disarray as police officials who were colluding with the ringleaders keep getting hauled away one after another, an unprecedented situation,” the source said.
The source added that ordinary Pyongyang residents and lower-ranking officials who have learned of the case have also been shaken, and are watching the fallout in stunned silence as senior officials once seen as untouchable suddenly find themselves facing prosecution.
Reporting from inside North Korea
Daily NK operates networks of sources inside North Korea who document events in real-time and transmit information through secure channels. Unlike reporting based on state media, satellite imagery, or defector accounts from years past, our journalism comes directly from people currently living under the regime. We verify reports through multiple independent sources and cross-reference details before publication.
Our sources remain anonymous because contact with foreign media is treated as a capital offense in North Korea — discovery means imprisonment or execution. This network-based approach allows Daily NK to report on developments other outlets cannot access: market trends, policy implementation, public sentiment, and daily realities that never appear in official narratives.
Maintaining these secure communication channels and protecting source identities requires specialized protocols and constant vigilance. Daily NK serves as a bridge between North Koreans and the outside world, documenting what’s happening inside one of the world’s most closed societies.

items.title: North Korea apartment nearly collapses weeks after passing inspection
items.summary: North Korean authorities carried out an emergency evacuation in South Pyongan province this month after a newly built apartment building showed signs of imminent collapse, and have since detained a construction section chief blamed for pushing the project through with unsafe, rushed construction methods. A source in South Pyongan province told Daily NK on Monday […]
items.body_text:
North Korean authorities carried out an emergency evacuation in South Pyongan province this month after a newly built apartment building showed signs of imminent collapse, and have since detained a construction section chief blamed for pushing the project through with unsafe, rushed construction methods.
A source in South Pyongan province told Daily NK on Monday that serious signs of collapse risk were recently discovered in a new three-story apartment building in Pyongwon county, even though the building had formally passed its completion inspection at the end of last month. In response, county safety department officers rushed to evacuate both residents who had already moved in and people passing near the building in the predawn hours of mid-July, the source said.
According to the source, the building’s management had already issued move-in certificates, and some residents were living there when the danger emerged. As the region’s summer rainy season weakened the ground beneath the structure and cracks began spreading across its exterior walls, the county safety department immediately warned of the danger, evacuated residents and completely blocked off the surrounding road.
The scene turned chaotic in the early morning hours, the source said, as safety officers shouted for people to evacuate and residents rushed outside without time to grab their belongings. Displaced residents reportedly stood helplessly outside the cordoned-off area, unsure what to do next.
Blame falls on a rushed construction campaign
The source attributed the near-disaster to Pyongwon county’s push to complete a construction assignment handed down from the central government within a fixed deadline, using soldiers and shock brigades, mobilized labor units North Korea often deploys on tight construction and production timelines, to build the apartment through a so-called speed battle, a mobilization-style campaign that prioritizes rushing projects to completion over following proper procedure.
Construction crews reportedly skipped proper foundation compaction and concrete curing periods to keep pace with the rushed timeline, and officials overseeing the project concealed the substandard work well enough to pass a nominal completion inspection in June. But as the rainy season set in, the ground beneath the building began to subside and the exterior walls developed serious cracks, exposing defects that had been hidden during the inspection process.
The county safety department moved into emergency response mode as the risk of collapse escalated, and local officials reported the incident to the central government, which ordered a more thorough re-inspection process over the next three months, the source said.
“Central government authorities determined that responsibility for this incident lies entirely with the construction officials who led the shoddy work and failed to properly supervise it,” the source said, adding that authorities dismissed the construction section chief on the spot and ordered him detained for investigation.
Authorities transferred the detained official to the county prosecutors’ office, where investigators are scrutinizing allegations that he diverted construction materials and ignored proper technical procedures to rush the project to completion, the source said. Local observers reportedly believe he is unlikely to escape an exemplary punishment meant to serve as a warning to others.
“People who had dreamed of moving into a new apartment were devastated and furious to see it turn into a near-collapsed eyesore overnight,” the source said. “People are asking who they’re supposed to trust to live safely when a building can pass its completion inspection and still nearly collapse before anyone has even properly moved in, and residents who witnessed the predawn evacuation are now anxious that their own homes could give way at any time.”

items.title: North Korea sends 10,000 workers to China in a month
items.summary: North Korea has sharply ramped up the number of new workers it is sending to China this summer, with roughly 10,000 laborers crossing the border in a single month as ties between Pyongyang and Beijing continue to recover, according to a Daily NK source, and more than 50,000 workers are already under contract to follow […]
items.body_text:
North Korea has sharply ramped up the number of new workers it is sending to China this summer, with roughly 10,000 laborers crossing the border in a single month as ties between Pyongyang and Beijing continue to recover, according to a Daily NK source, and more than 50,000 workers are already under contract to follow them.
A Daily NK source told the outlet on Monday that around 10,000 newly dispatched workers crossed from North Korea into China in the roughly month-long period since mid-June. The workers travel by bus from Sinuiju, North Pyongan province, across the Sino-Korean Friendship Bridge into Dandong, Liaoning province, with a daily average of 500 to 600 people entering the country and as many as 10 buses, each carrying 50 passengers, crossing together in a single convoy.
“On days when North Korean workers come through, some 10 buses cross the bridge almost all at once, each one carrying 50 people,” the source said. “Hundreds of people enter in a short span of time, so the line of buses passes by in an instant.”
One change from past practice, according to the source, is that Chinese local governments are now directly involved in managing personnel and paperwork for these worker groups. In previous years, dispatch relied mainly on contracts negotiated directly between North Korean trading companies and Chinese firms, but now those companies must report worker numbers and entry plans to the relevant local government in advance and receive approval before anyone crosses.
“No matter how many people are entering, they have to file in advance with the local government and get entry approval,” the source said. “Even for a small group, it isn’t enough for a company and a North Korean trading firm to work things out between themselves. It has to go through the relevant government’s approval process.”
That shift suggests the current wave of entries is proceeding under the active management, and at least tacit approval, of Chinese local governments rather than at the sole initiative of private firms or trading companies, though Beijing’s central government does not appear to be directly involved in the day-to-day administrative process. Central authorities are likely aware of the large-scale movement of North Korean workers but appear content to leave the matter to local officials rather than intervene directly, the source said.
Most of the workers are entering China under “industrial trainee” status, a designation ostensibly meant for people learning technical skills or production processes, even though they are in practice placed directly into factory jobs. That arrangement has drawn scrutiny as a workaround for U.N. Security Council sanctions that bar the employment of new North Korean workers abroad.
The Security Council’s Resolution 2397, adopted in December 2017, required member states to repatriate North Korean nationals earning income within their jurisdiction, along with the North Korean officials overseeing them, within 24 months, meaning workers were in principle required to return home by December 2019. Repatriations effectively stalled after North Korea sealed its borders in 2020 amid the spread of COVID-19, leaving North Korean workers stationed in China, Russia and elsewhere. Earlier Security Council resolutions separately banned new employment and work-permit approvals for North Korean laborers specifically to cut off the country’s foreign currency income, which means workers entering as “industrial trainees” but ultimately placed into productive labor and earning wages remain difficult to distinguish from a straightforward sanctions violation.
China wary of attention falling on dispatches
China also appears wary of the large-scale entries becoming public knowledge. Workers cross the border almost entirely during the predawn hours, when traffic and foot traffic are lightest.

items.title: Clarkson happy with handshake to extend contract as North set to miss finals
items.summary: As speculation mounts over his future at Arden Street, North Melbourne coach Alastair Clarkson addresses his contract situation.
items.body_text:
North Melbourne coach Alastair Clarkson says he won't be pushing for a contract extension in the off-season after another frustrating year for the Kangaroos.
Clarkson has one year left on his five-year contract, and he urged the club to mimic others like Brisbane and Adelaide by "sticking to the path".
What's next?
The Kangaroos, who are 13th on the ladder, face a challenging run home starting with Western Bulldogs on Thursday night.
North Melbourne coach Alastair Clarkson is unfazed going into the final year of his contract, saying he just needs a "handshake".
As Clarkson comes towards the end of his fourth season in charge, North will spend a 10th-straight year without experiencing finals action.
Speculation has started to mount that Kangaroos hierarchy might consider letting Clarkson go at the end of his current five-year deal, signed in late 2022 in what was a massive coup for the club.
Although North have improved this year, they are yet to beat a team above them on the ladder and will fall short of a wildcard berth.
"Old school" Clarkson will not be pushing for a contract extension beyond 2027 this off-season and is happy to wait it out.
"All I require is a handshake and a wink and a nod, and that'll do me," the four-time Hawthorn premiership coach said on Tuesday.
"We'll work our way through whatever we need to do.
"I'm really here to serve the footy club … it's not just me, but those that are in leadership positions at the club have done a really good job stabilising the footy club.
"We're really keen to progress and get ourselves up the ladder, but all we do know is that that's done best when you've got stability."
Clarkson drew on examples of Brisbane Lions, Fremantle and Adelaide of clubs who were patient with their coaches and find themselves in powerful positions on the field.
"I've been in the caper for a long time, so that's a bit of water off the duck's (back)," he said of speculation about his future.
"The best examples are the reigning premiers (Brisbane) who took a while to get going and then Adelaide with 'Nicksy' (Matthew Nicks) and Fremantle with Justin Longmuir.
"The governance and administration of the club just sticking to the path and sticking to the course, and we're going to be no different."
Clarkson's record at North is 19-1-59, a far cry from his glory years with the Hawks.
The Kangaroos face a challenging run home, starting with the Western Bulldogs at Docklands on Thursday night.
They have long losing streaks against the Bulldogs, and their final two opponents, Geelong and Sydney.
Clarkson bristled when asked how important it would be to beat one of those teams to finish off this season.
"You're just searching, searching for a headline," he said.
"Teams that have been in the bottom four or five on the ladder haven't beaten the top teams very often in the last five or six years.
"That's the reason why they've been in that position on the ladder."
AAP

items.title: Clubs stand firm after AFL's controversial finals memo
items.summary: The AFL warns clubs they risk being sanctioned should they rest players in round 24, but several coaches say they will not be paying attention to the memo.
items.body_text:
Melbourne coach Steven King has doubled down on the issue of resting players, saying he will take any decision that is best for his club in the face of AFL warnings.
AFL football boss Greg Swann has written to clubs warning the league will scrutinise team selections in the lead-up to finals.
With the introduction of the wildcard round, teams seven to 10 will not have the week off between round 24 and the start of finals.
The AFL's warning to clubs about resting players before the newly introduced wildcard round has not gone down well with coaches.
Clubs have been threatened with sanctions if they decide to make mass changes for their games in round 24.
"While legitimate player management of player fatigue or injuries is permitted, the AFL will scrutinise club team selection decisions in the lead-up to AFL finals," AFL football boss Greg Swann wrote in a memo to clubs on Monday.
The AFL has had a pre-finals bye since 2016, allowing the top-eight teams a week off before the last month of the season.
But with the finals system effectively becoming a top-10 due to the wildcard weekend, not every club will be afforded that luxury should they qualify.
Loading Twitter content
Teams ranked seventh to 10th at the end of the home-and-away season will have to back up and play the following week.
The top-six will all rest before preparing for respective qualifying and elimination finals, starting on September 3.
The Western Bulldogs are almost certain to finish in the wildcard bracket, creating a dilemma for coach Luke Beveridge.
"The main consideration for the teams who might be certainties to play a wildcard game going into that round is the fact that the six teams above the seventh have all got a week off," Beveridge told Fox Footy.
"I'm sure within the ranks of the teams that are certainties, you're processing who needs a week off.
"I'd question how the AFL could question a club, because you're questioning the medical department from a club as well, if that happens."
Steven King, in his rookie season as Melbourne coach, was also left perplexed by the AFL's directive.
"I'm the coach of the Melbourne footy club," he told Fox Footy.
"I'll make any decision that's best for our football club and best for the management of our players."
Fremantle famously made 10 changes for their final home-and-away game in 2013, leading to them being thrashed by struggling St Kilda.
The following week, the Dockers pulled off a historic qualifying-final win in Geelong over the highly fancied Cats.
In 2015, North Melbourne rested nine players ahead of a finals campaign when they lost against Richmond.
The move paid off for the Kangaroos, who turned the tables on the Tigers in an elimination final and also won a semi-final in Sydney.
Former North Melbourne coach Brad Scott rested nine players in the final round of the 2015 season, while Ross Lyon made 10 changes in the final round of the 2013 season when he was in charge of Fremantle.
AAP

items.title: Aussie swimmer out of leadership group after reported drinking session

items.body_text:
Australian swimmer Isaac Cooper out of leadership group after reported Glasgow Commonwealth Games drinking session
Tue 4 Aug 2026 at 11:24am
Australian swimmer Isaac Cooper has stepped down from the Dolphins's leadership group after a drinking session at the Commonwealth Games.
Cooper was reported to be out drinking when he was expected to be supporting teammates at Glasgow's Tollcross International Swimming Centre last Wednesday night.
Cooper was also seen drinking at the Australian team hotel during that day, the report said.
"Isaac did not attend the final night of the swimming competition or final team meeting in Glasgow, which is in conflict with team expectations," a Swimming Australia statement said.
"Isaac has since voluntarily stood down from the team's athlete leadership group."
Cooper was scheduled to race the 100m backstroke final that night but withdrew from the event after qualifying eighth-fastest.
Swimmers were expected to support teammates at the Glasgow Games when not racing, while Cooper also missed the team meeting that night.
The 22-year-old won gold at the Glasgow Games as a member of the 4x100m medley team after swimming in the heats.
He also finished sixth in the 50m backstroke final, an event he won a silver medal at the 2024 world championships.
Cooper will next compete at the Pan Pacific championships in the United States starting August 12.
AAP

items.title: From deadline to details: The six things you need to know to handle the census
items.summary: Some questions have fallen away since the first census in 1911, while others have been introduced. But no matter where you are, you must fill it in – or pay a whopping fine.
items.body_text:
From deadline to details: The six things you need to know to handle the census
When is census night, how do you fill it out, and do you need to be at home?
Census night this year is August 11. But, as more than 1.2 million households have already done, you can complete your census form before that date.
If you complete your census form before August 11, you need to fill it out as if you were home on that day.
If a member of a household is away from home on the special night, you can include them as if they were home. If you are visiting someone, make sure you’re included in their household form. But make sure you’re counted only once.
For those travelling or staying at hotels, caravan parks and registered campgrounds, operators should have census forms for you to complete.
If you happen to be free camping or staying at a remote location, various visitor information centres will have census forms. If that doesn’t work, you can get a census number from the ABS so you can complete your form when you have access to the internet.
Why do we have the census?
Since the Babylonians in 3800 BC, governing bodies have sought to count the number of people under their control.
The census that features in the Gospel of Luke was conducted by authorities for taxation and administration reasons as Rome brought the province of Judea under its control.
Outside of tax, censuses have been used to plan for services such as schools and cemeteries, while in many countries they are central to the allocation of electorates in parliaments.
The first official census in this country was in 1828. It was termed a “muster” and held in NSW to help align the number of people in the colony with its food supplies. Colonial headcounts were carried out until the mid-1880s.
In 1905, the federal government passed the Census and Statistics Act. The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) was created the following year. The first national census was held on April 2, 1911.
That census counted 4.45 million people (excluding the nation’s Indigenous population).
Some of the questions used in that census have disappeared. We are no longer asked if we live in a wagon or if the family home is made from spinifex or calico.
But others have remained constant, though maybe the answers change. In 1911, 79 people said their religion was Callithumpian, while another 32 described their belief as “wowser”.
At the 2001 census, almost 70,000 people said they were Jedi.
What happens if you don’t complete the census?
Completing the census is compulsory, and has been since the first count in 1911.
If a household does not complete and submit a census form, the ABS will contact you and ask for it to be done. If a household continues to hold out, it can be served a formal direction to complete the census, which is a legal instruction.
At this point, if you continue to refuse to fill out the form, you can be prosecuted and fined up to $364 a day.
What is a census field officer, how are they chosen, and how much are they paid?
The census is one of the nation’s largest one-off job opportunities. The ABS is employing more than 16,000 field officers – the people who go around to households with forms and then pick them up – through the census period.
It’s a job that appeals to seniors or those looking for some casual work, and the pay starts around the $33-an-hour mark.
There are thousands of other positions that require more specialist skills or being in particular parts of the country, such as isolated regions.
What has changed in Australia because of the census?
One of the most important discoveries in health was uncovered by Australian statistician Oliver Lancaster.
He used the 1911, 1921 and 1933 censuses – which asked a question on deaf-mutism – to establish for the first time the link between rubella and congenital problems in unborn children.
More recently, housing experts noticed a drop in the number of home owners between the 1996 and 2001 census. This continued into the national headcount

items.title: The best public schools in HSC maths, ranked – and how one non-selective surprised everyone
items.summary: Balgowlah Boys has a stronger HSC average maths mark than most selective schools. Search the list to see your school.
items.body_text:
The best public schools in HSC maths, ranked – and how one non-selective surprised everyone
Balgowlah Boys, Fairvale High and Killarney Heights High recorded the highest average marks in advanced mathematics of any non-selective public schools in last year’s Higher School Certificate.
A Herald analysis of average marks in the subject shows the 43 students at Balgowlah Boys who enrolled in the advanced course achieved an average mark of 90.3 – stronger than all but four selective schools.
For the Mathematics Standard 2 course, fully selective school Merewether High in Newcastle had the best average marks, followed by Manly selective and then Balgowlah Boys.
Balgowlah’s head of mathematics, Chris Hickford, traces its HSC success back to year 7 and teachers’ focus on building strong algebra skills, an ability to think formulaically and interpret critical information in written questions.
“We do have, I suppose, a traditional approach to maths teaching here at the school,” he said.
A typical lesson contains teacher-led examples, student questioning, followed by a “gradual release” for the students to work independently. Or, in teacher parlance, it is an “I do, we do, you do” approach.
Many students took up mathematics because they aspired to work in a trade and could see the value of numeracy skills to real life, he said, while other students wanted to take mathematics-based university courses. Others simply enjoy the subject because they’re good at it.
“The explicit nature of the subject appeals to the boys … seeing a clear result and an answer that very rarely can be ambiguous or misinterpreted. I think that clarity of it really appeals to the boys,” Hickford said.
It is easy to slip behind during the fast-paced year 11 and 12 courses, so the teachers focus on “ensuring the students are actually doing the work” with rigorous checks.
“We find just keeping the students to account for actually getting their work done makes a huge difference,” he said.
Eddie Woo, Professor of Practice at the University of Sydney, said there was no single method to improve mathematics results but successful schools often closely analyse results data provided by the NSW Education Standards Authority.
“It gives super granular data. We can drill down to individual classes and items in an exam,” he said.
Schools could detect areas of weakness and learn from their teachers whose classes had produced excellent results in certain topics, such as discrete random variables.
Another key to success was structured mentoring and purposeful skill development for teachers, which included pairing new teachers with experienced ones so they could see how they approached teaching the mathematics course.
“Some schools do it extremely well and other schools have constraining factors, so that means it doesn’t happen as much,” Wu said.
“Just because you can do the content yourself is not the same as being able to teach it ... anyone who has taught someone how to drive can attest to this. It’s a whole different set of skills.”
Most private schools do not publish subject averages, though the high-ranking selective Sydney Grammar School reported an average of 87.7 for advanced maths. Girls school Roseville College reported a mean of 83.2.

items.title: Red flags: A tech company claims it can identify Australia’s most at-risk children
items.summary: Ruby O’Rourke says every warning sign of her own abuse as a child had been missed. She spent 12 years building software so that won’t happen to the next child.
items.body_text:
Red flags: A tech company claims it can identify Australia’s most at-risk children
An Australian company founded by a survivor of childhood abuse is bringing a machine-learning system to childcare centres to flag children who may be at risk of harm, as the sector grapples with balancing young people’s privacy against a need to keep them safe.
The warning system’s rollout in daycares across the country comes as the sector undergoes its biggest safety overhaul since the national quality framework began.
The company says its eponymously named SAFE system is already in use in more than 1000 early childhood services. Educators log everyday observations – a bruise, a missed meal, a parent affected by drugs at pick-up – and the machine-learning model turns those fragments into a live picture of which children may be most at risk. Parents are not asked to opt in; the company says consent is given when families enrol their kids to a daycare and agree to its professional systems.
Chief executive Ruby O’Rourke, a longtime children’s rights campaigner who ran for federal parliament in 2019, built the company after a childhood shaped by forced adoption, domestic violence and abuse that, she says, culminated in a family member holding her under the water at a Melbourne creek. Passersby revived her. The family member was never charged.
Her argument is that none of it was invisible. “The schools, the Brownies, the Girl Guides, all of these signals were missed,” she said. Neighbours told her years later that they had heard her scream, and done nothing.
“If I’m going to leave my life with anything,” she said, “it’s knowing the next generation has this layer of SAFE sitting under the surface” – what she calls a “flight control tower” for children at severe risk.
O’Rourke began building childcare software in the mid-2000s; the predictive layer started in 2012 with NICTA, the country’s former information and communications technology research centre that is now part of the CSIRO.
Co-founder David Salajan describes SAFE as a machine paired with human reviewers.
“It’s just an observation, no matter how big or small,” he said. The software returns a risk score and guidance on whether a concern meets the mandatory reporting threshold; every case is then reviewed by former child protection workers. A national dashboard, seen by SAFE’s team rather than the daycare centre staff, triages every case so they can see which children are at highest risk.
The pitch lands at a volatile moment for the childcare sector. Changes to national laws governing the industry took effect on February 27, making children’s safety the paramount legal consideration, creating a workers’ register and mandating carers to attend child safety training by August 27. A $226 million government package also funds a national CCTV trial.
The overhaul follows recent abuse cases such as that of Queensland worker Ashley Paul Griffith, jailed for life in 2024 over 307 offences against 73 children. In Sydney, daycare worker Hamish Alexander Edward Tait was arrested last month, facing more than 320 charges over his alleged abuse of 150 children under his care.
Those cases involved alleged abuse at childcare centres though, rather than abuse elsewhere detected by an educator. The SAFE system also raises privacy concerns: a private company holds a live, prioritised register of children it deems most at risk, plus behavioural records on about 200,000 workers in the childcare industry.
The Office of the Australian Information Commissioner would not comment on SAFE, but a spokesperson said behavioural information about a child in a care setting may count as personal – and sometimes sensitive – information under the Privacy Act, carrying obligations to collect only what is necessary, keep it secure and not reuse it. items.body_text:
Minns government will not implement recommendation of long-awaited hate speech report
Penry Buckley
The NSW government will not expand a controversial offence for inciting hatred to include religion, sexual orientation or gender identity, against the recommendation of a report which it has been sitting on for eight months.
In a statement this afternoon, the NSW attorney general, Michael Daley, said the government was today releasing the report by former supreme court justice John Sackar, firstprovided to the government in November.
In the report, Sackar has recommended that section 93ZAA of the NSW Crimes Act, an offence for inciting hatred on the grounds of race, brought in last year against the recommendation of the NSW Law Reform Commission, be “amended to included all attributes currently protected by section 93Z”.
Section 93Z, the offence for inciting violence, covers offences committed on the basis of someone’s race, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity or intersex or HIV/Aids status.
Daley said:
After careful consideration of the Sackar Review and its recommendations, the NSW Government has decided not to expand the existing criminal offence of inciting racial hatred to apply to additional protected attributes.
There is no place for hatred in NSW. Everyone deserves to feel safe, respected and free from intimidation, regardless of their background, faith, sexuality or identity.
The Government’s view is that expanding the racial hatred offence to cover other attributes raises complex questions about freedom of expression, freedom of religion, and the consistent application of the criminal law across the community.”
That’s where we’ll leave our live coverage for the day.
Before we log off, let’s recap the top headlines:
NSW police have arrested and charged two men after one of them allegedly brandished a fake replica gun, wearing a bulletproof vest with a US flag and carrying a toy police badge, at a busy Sydney entertainment precinct.
Top NSW officials urged people to avoid the emergency department except in cases of extreme health needs, warning the next three weeks will see hospitals at capacity amid a surge in winter illness.
Thomas Bradley, aQueensland supreme court judge, will be appointed Queensland’s new governor. Bradley will replace the former state chief health officer Jeannette Young, who has served in the role since 2021.
Betting giant Sportsbetsaid it has no evidence to substantiate allegations made in Monday’s hearing about the Albanese government’s gambling bill, including that gambling companies provided illegal drugs and sex workers to customers.
The new Victorian premier, Ben Carroll, has had his new cabinet sworn in today in what appears to be a major shake-up to portfolios.
Australians lodged nearly 120,000 complaints with the Australian Financial Complaints Authority in the most recent financial year, a record number that reflects the intense economic pressures being felt across the community.
The Australian Medical Association Victoria branch said doctors will engage in a stop-work action on Thursday 13 August, affecting hospitals across the Melbourne CBD and in Parkville. It’s the first time doctors have taken protected industrial action in the area in 20 years.
The chief executive of the Bureau of Meteorology has commissioned an independent review of the agency to “ensure it delivers value to Australians in a rapidly changing environment”.
